papers.title: Long-Term Exposure to Fine Particulate Matter and Kidney Function among Patients with Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.journal: Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is the fourth leading cause of end-stage kidney disease. Although the condition is primarily genetic, environmental exposures such as air pollution may influence disease progression. We investigated whether long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is associated with kidney function decline among individuals with PKD and whether this association differs by age, sex, initial kidney function, and tolvaptan use. Using the Korea National Health Information Database, we identified 18,898 adults with PKD who underwent at least two health screenings between 2016 and 2023. Annual mean PM2.5 exposure was estimated with a high-resolution (1 km2) machine learning-based model. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to assess the association between PM2.5 exposure and changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and lifestyle covariates. Each 1 µg/m3 higher lag 0-1 year PM2.5 was associated with a -0.09 mL/min/1.73 m2 change in eGFR (95% CI, -0.16 to -0.01). More evident associations were observed among younger adults (-0.26; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.09), individuals with preserved baseline kidney function (-0.14; 95% CI, -0.21 to -0.07), male (-0.10; 95% CI, -0.21 to 0), and individuals who were not prescribed tolvaptan (-0.12; 95% CI, -0.20 to -0.04). Chronic exposure to PM2.5 appears to be an environmental modifier of kidney function decline in PKD, particularly among younger individuals and those with preserved kidney function.
key_findings: Each 1 µg/m3 higher PM2.5 associated with -0.09 mL/min/1.73m2 eGFR change in 18,898 PKD adults
Stronger associations in younger adults and those with preserved kidney function
Tolvaptan users showed attenuated PM2.5-eGFR association
papers.what_happened: A Korean registry study of 18,898 adults with PKD found a modest association between chronic PM2.5 exposure and faster eGFR decline, particularly in younger individuals and those not on tolvaptan.
papers.why_it_matters: This is the first large-scale study examining air pollution as a potential environmental modifier of kidney function decline in PKD, suggesting non-genetic factors may contribute to disease progression.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective observational design with residual confounding likely; effect size is small (-0.09 mL/min/1.73m2 per µg/m3); eGFR is a surrogate endpoint; and the PKD population was identified by ICD codes without genetic confirmation, so the cohort likely includes non-ADPKD forms.

papers.title: Emodin retards renal cyst progression in ADPKD by inhibiting cell proliferation and decreasing oxidative stress
papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a common monogenic genetic disease characterized by bilateral renal cyst formation and enlargement. The purpose of this study was to explore the therapeutic effects of emodin, which is a key active constituent of traditional Chinese herbal medicine Rhubarb, on ADPKD and its underlying mechanisms. Herein, we found emodin significantly inhibited renal cyst progression in ADPKD. RNA-sequencing analysis and network pharmacological analysis indicated that emodin may exert its therapeutic effects by modulating cell proliferation and oxidative stress, in which the Wnt and Nrf2 related signaling pathways probably played important roles. These findings were subsequently verified. Emodin was shown to downregulate cell proliferation and oxidative stress levels, inhibit the proliferation-associated Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, and activate the antioxidant Nrf2/GPX4 signaling pathway. Furthermore, we found that the Wnt pathway exerted an inhibitory effect on Nrf2/GPX4 axis upstream. Through inhibition of the Wnt pathway, emodin may relieve its suppression of Nrf2/GPX4 axis, ultimately achieving dual modulation of proliferation and oxidative stress. Emodin also potentially acted as a direct binder to Wnt7a.
key_findings: Emodin inhibited cyst progression in ADPKD preclinical models via Wnt/beta-catenin and Nrf2/GPX4 pathways
Wnt pathway suppresses Nrf2/GPX4 axis; emodin relieves this suppression
Emodin may directly bind Wnt7a as upstream mechanism
papers.what_happened: Researchers demonstrated that emodin, a compound from Rhubarb, inhibited renal cyst progression in preclinical ADPKD models by modulating Wnt/beta-catenin and Nrf2/GPX4 pathways.
papers.why_it_matters: Identifies a new preclinical compound and pathway interaction (Wnt suppression of Nrf2/GPX4) that may be relevant to understanding cyst growth mechanisms.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical study only with no human data; ADPKD has a historically poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record; the specific animal and in vitro models used may not recapitulate human disease progression.

papers.title: SAR-Guided Scaffold Innovation of Selective V2R Antagonists: Therapeutic Frontiers in ADPKD
papers.abstract: The vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) is a class A G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) that plays a pivotal role in the regulation of renal water homeostasis and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) through sustained activation of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling. Pharmacological antagonism of V2R has emerged as a clinically validated strategy for attenuating cyst growth. However, the therapeutic application of currently available V2R antagonists remains constrained by safety liability and a relatively narrow chemical space. A recent study employed systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) analyses to expand existing design paradigms for V2R antagonists, leading to the identification and synthesis of a series of structurally diverse V2R antagonist analogues. Supported by multidimensional pharmacological evaluations, these findings provide an important framework for the rational design and optimization of next-generation therapeutics for ADPKD.
key_findings: SAR analysis expanded chemical space for V2R antagonists beyond existing scaffolds
New structurally diverse V2R antagonist analogues identified and synthesized
Aims to address safety limitations of current V2R antagonists like tolvaptan
papers.what_happened: A medicinal chemistry perspective reviewed SAR-guided efforts to design novel V2R antagonist scaffolds, expanding the chemical space beyond tolvaptan-like structures.
papers.why_it_matters: Relevant to the long-term pipeline for next-generation V2R antagonists that may have improved safety profiles over tolvaptan.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a narrative review/perspective with no new clinical or even in vivo data; the compounds described are early-stage with no demonstrated in vivo efficacy or safety advantage.

papers.title: WCN26-6011 Valve Burden-Related Cardiac Remodeling in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)

papers.title: The many faces of cholesterol in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease has some effects on cholesterol metabolism and cardiovascular disease that are shared with other chronic kidney diseases and others that are distinctive and directly caused by disruption of polycystins. The pravastatin clinical trial by Gitomer et al. does not support treatment with statins for the only purpose of delaying disease progression. Emergence of novel lipid-lowering therapies presents new therapeutic opportunities but also risks. Recent studies suggest that cholesterol is important for traffic to and function of polycystins in primary cilia.
key_findings: Editorial commentary on the Gitomer et al. pravastatin RCT (Kidney International 2025)
Concludes pravastatin data do not support statins for the sole purpose of delaying ADPKD progression
Notes emerging lipid-lowering therapies present both opportunities and risks given polycystin trafficking dependence on cholesterol
Reiterates cilial cholesterol is important for polycystin function

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Author is a prominent ADPKD investigator (Mayo Clinic); none apparent specific to cholesterol/statin products

papers.what_happened: Vicente Torres authored an editorial commentary in Kidney International framing the Gitomer pravastatin RCT as negative for disease-specific kidney protection and reviewing the broader role of cholesterol in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Torres's framing consolidates the field's interpretation that statins are not indicated for ADPKD progression alone, which aligns with guideline-level discussions.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a narrative editorial, not primary evidence; it reflects one senior expert's synthesis of existing trials.

papers.title: Trajectories of Kidney Function in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Patients Treated with Tolvaptan
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is the most common monogenic kidney disease, and the only approved pharmacological therapy shown to slow disease progression is tolvaptan. This study presents a long-term observation of ADPKD patients treated at our center, focusing on changes in eGFR approximately one year before and at least 1 year after the initiation of tolvaptan therapy. Materials and Methods: A retrospective analysis of a cohort of ADPKD patients who have received tolvaptan treatment in our center. Results: In total, 20 patients were enrolled in the analysis. Their median time of observation since tolvaptan introduction was 23.5 months. No statistically significant difference was noted in the median monthly decrease in eGFR between the time prior to tolvaptan introduction and during tolvaptan therapy. Analysis of trajectories of eGFR in particular patients enabled the division of the cohort into three subgroups: beneficiaries (n = 7, 35%), stable (n = 8, 40%), and progressors (n = 5, n = 25%). Conclusions: Despite the low number of patients, together with a relatively short observation period, which are the main limitations of our study, our results suggest that, in real-world settings, the efficacy of tolvaptan may be lower than previously reported. There is an urgent need to identify factors responsible for the suboptimal effect of the medicine.
key_findings: Single-center retrospective study of 20 ADPKD patients treated with tolvaptan, median 23.5 months follow-up
No statistically significant difference in median monthly eGFR decline before vs during tolvaptan
35% classified as beneficiaries, 40% stable, 25% progressors (classification by visual trajectory analysis)
Authors conclude real-world tolvaptan efficacy may be lower than reported in pivotal trials
papers.what_happened: A Polish single-center retrospective study (n=20) compared eGFR slope before and after tolvaptan initiation and found no statistically significant change.
papers.why_it_matters: Real-world tolvaptan response is heterogeneous and knowing the distribution of responders vs non-responders could inform patient selection.
papers.what_limits_confidence: n=20 with pre/post baseline-only design and short follow-up; severely underpowered to detect tolvaptan's modest (about 0.5-1.0 mL/min/1.73m2/year) slope benefit, and selection bias likely since patients had to qualify for tolvaptan.

papers.title: Octreotide long-acting release in the treatment of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Objective: To systematically evaluate the clinical features and effects of octreotide long-acting release in the treatment of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Methods: Databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating octreotide long-acting release (LAR) in ADPKD from inception to December 2024. Six RCTs were included. Results: Meta-analysis using a fixed-effects model showed no statistically significant difference in GFR between groups [SMD = -0.020 (-0.250, 0.210), P = 0.864]. Random-effects model showed no statistically significant difference in total kidney volume [SMD = -0.001 (-0.376, 0.374), P = 0.996]. Fixed-effects meta-analysis showed a statistically significant reduction in cystic kidney volume [RR = 1.127 (0.996, 1.276), P = 0.058]. Conclusions: Octreotide LAR shows no significant effect on GFR or TKV and does not increase adverse reactions.
key_findings: Meta-analysis of 6 RCTs of octreotide LAR in ADPKD
No statistically significant effect on GFR (SMD -0.020, p=0.864)
No statistically significant effect on total kidney volume (SMD -0.001, p=0.996)
Borderline signal for cystic kidney volume reduction (p=0.058)
No increased adverse event risk
papers.what_happened: A meta-analysis of 6 RCTs found no significant effect of octreotide long-acting release on eGFR or total kidney volume in ADPKD, with only a borderline signal for cystic volume.
papers.why_it_matters: Consolidates the negative signal across somatostatin analogue RCTs, aligning with the field's drift away from this drug class for ADPKD progression.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Quality of underlying RCTs and heterogeneity are not summarized in the abstract; cystic kidney volume p-value of 0.058 is borderline and endpoint is surrogate only.

papers.title: Association of Kidney Volume With Patient-Reported Outcomes in ADPKD
papers.abstract: Introduction: ADPKD may impose physical and emotional burdens, partly through enlarged kidneys. The association of HRQOL with TKV remains unclear. Methods: 456 ADPKD participants recruited 2017-2023. Associations of TKV, eGFR, and chronic kidney pain with SF-36 scores via multivariable regression. Factor analysis of mixed data clustered patients based on TKV/eGFR/pain. Results: Mean age 47, 47% male, median TKV 922 mL. SF-36 PCS scores were 53, 51, 51 across increasing TKV tertiles (p=0.02) after adjustment. MCS scores similar across tertiles. Lower eGFR and kidney pain associated with worse HRQOL. Mediation analysis showed an indirect association between TKV and MCS through kidney pain. Conclusion: TKV is associated with physical health independent of pain and function, and with mental health indirectly through kidney pain.
key_findings: 456 ADPKD participants (prospective recruitment 2017-2023)
TKV independently associated with SF-36 physical component score after adjusting for eGFR and pain
Mental component score mediated indirectly through kidney pain
Four phenotypic clusters identified based on severity x pain
papers.what_happened: A cross-sectional analysis of 456 ADPKD patients found larger TKV associated with worse SF-36 physical scores after adjusting for pain and eGFR, with mental health impacted indirectly via pain.
papers.why_it_matters: Supports the clinical relevance of TKV beyond renal prognosis, informing how clinicians counsel patients and prioritize interventions that reduce kidney enlargement.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional design cannot establish causality; TKV-PRO relationship may reflect reverse causation or shared drivers; PCS differences are modest (about 2 points).

papers.title: Feasibility study of empagliflozin in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: Design and baseline characteristics.
papers.abstract: Introduction: SGLT2 inhibitors slow kidney function decline in diabetic and non-diabetic proteinuric CKD, but potential benefits in ADPKD have not been assessed. Methods: Randomized, placebo-controlled, 1-year trial of empagliflozin (10-25mg/day) vs placebo in 50 non-diabetic ADPKD patients aged 18-55 with eGFR 30-90 mL/min/1.73m2 at two US sites (Colorado, Maryland). Primary outcomes: safety and tolerability of 25mg dose. Secondary outcomes: TKV, kidney function, aortic stiffness, copeptin, urinary KIM-1, PKD-specific HRQOL.
key_findings: Pilot RCT of empagliflozin 10-25 mg/day vs placebo in 50 non-diabetic ADPKD patients, 1-year duration
Primary endpoint: safety/tolerability in ADPKD population
Secondary: TKV, kidney function, aortic stiffness, copeptin, KIM-1, QoL
Baseline characteristics and trial design published; no efficacy results yet

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Trial design paper; sponsor disclosures not extracted from abstract

papers.what_happened: The design and baseline characteristics of a 50-patient, 1-year pilot RCT of empagliflozin vs placebo in non-diabetic ADPKD were published; the trial is powered primarily for safety/tolerability.
papers.why_it_matters: The first dedicated SGLT2i safety RCT in non-diabetic ADPKD; results will inform whether larger efficacy trials are warranted given the rest-of-CKD SGLT2i track record.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Pilot design with n=50 and 1-year duration can address safety but is underpowered for TKV or eGFR slope efficacy; no efficacy data yet.

papers.title: Incidence and clinicopathological analysis of portal vein and inferior vena cava thrombosis in autopsy cases of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Autopsy case analysis evaluating the incidence and clinicopathological features of portal vein thrombosis and inferior vena cava thrombosis in ADPKD; full abstract text not extracted from Semantic Scholar metadata.
key_findings: Autopsy-based retrospective analysis of portal vein and IVC thrombosis in ADPKD
Full sample size, incidence rates, and risk factors not extracted from available abstract metadata
papers.what_happened: A Japanese autopsy series analyzed portal vein and IVC thrombosis incidence in ADPKD decedents.
papers.why_it_matters: Venous thrombosis from mass effect of enlarged polycystic kidneys/liver may be under-recognized in advanced disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Autopsy series has strong selection bias (decedent population) and small sample; abstract-only metadata limits assessment of incidence estimates.

papers.title: Overweight and Obesity are Associated with Lower Renal Blood Flow in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We have previously reported that overweight and obesity are independently associated with more rapid disease progression in adults with ADPKD. In this study we perform a cross-sectional analysis to evaluate whether overweight and obesity are also associated with renal blood flow. METHODS: 134 non-diabetic adults with ADPKD and eGFR >=60 who participated in a pravastatin RCT were categorized as normal weight, overweight, or obese based on adjusted BMI. Renal blood flow (RBF) was measured by phase-contrast MRI and adjusted for BSA. RESULTS: Baseline RBF was 635+/-214 mL/min/1.73m2. BSA-adjusted RBF was lower in stepwise manner with increasing BMI. After adjustment overweight (beta -78.4) and obesity (beta -190.6) remained associated with lower RBF. For every one-unit increase in BMI, RBF was 10.4 mL/min/1.73m2 lower. CONCLUSION: Overweight and obesity are cross-sectionally associated with lower RBF in early-stage ADPKD; these findings reflect associations only.
key_findings: 134 non-diabetic adults with ADPKD and preserved eGFR from pravastatin RCT cohort
BSA-adjusted renal blood flow was stepwise lower across normal/overweight/obese categories
After multivariable adjustment including eGFR and htTKV, overweight (beta -78.4) and obesity (beta -190.6) remained associated with lower RBF
1-unit BMI increase associated with 10.4 mL/min/1.73m2 lower RBF
Authors explicitly note associations only, no causal inference

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Uses pravastatin RCT cohort; no commercial obesity-drug conflict apparent

papers.what_happened: In a cross-sectional analysis of 134 early-stage ADPKD patients, higher BMI was independently associated with lower phase-contrast MRI-measured renal blood flow.
papers.why_it_matters: Suggests a potential mechanism linking obesity to faster ADPKD progression, which could inform lifestyle intervention research priorities.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional association cannot establish causality; reverse causation or shared metabolic drivers remain plausible explanations; sample is early-stage ADPKD only.

papers.title: Emerging roles of ATP citrate lyase in kidney diseases: from pathogenic driver to therapeutic target.
papers.abstract: Narrative review positioning ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) as a metabolic-epigenetic node in kidney disease pathogenesis. Notes ACLY upregulation in polycystic kidney disease where inhibition attenuates cystic growth (citing bempedoic acid preclinical work). Discusses several ACLY inhibitors including bempedoic acid as repurposing candidates.
key_findings: Narrative review of ACLY roles in diabetic kidney disease, CKD, AKI, and polycystic kidney disease
Cites preclinical evidence that ACLY inhibition (e.g., bempedoic acid) attenuates cyst growth in PKD models
Positions ACLY as a potential therapeutic target across multiple renal pathologies
papers.novelty_assessment: Narrative review covering known preclinical evidence; no new data.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical implications for ADPKD; modest research-prioritization signal for ACLY as a target.
papers.what_happened: Narrative review of ATP-citrate lyase in kidney disease that covers polycystic kidney disease as one pathology where ACLY inhibition attenuates cyst growth preclinically.
papers.why_it_matters: Flags bempedoic acid and other ACLY inhibitors as repurposing candidates worth preclinical follow-up in PKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no new data; ADPKD section is brief and references existing preclinical work.

papers.title: Relationship between Total Kidney Volume and eGFR in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: Within each Mayo Imaging Class, log(TKV) and eGFR showed a consistent linear intraindividual relationship using CRISP and HALT-PKD Study A data. For Mayo classes 1C-1E, a 1 percentage-point/year reduction in TKV growth rate predicts 0.40-0.52 mL/min/1.73m2/year slowing in eGFR decline. Authors propose this framework to define the magnitude of TKV treatment effect needed to support accelerated drug approval in ADPKD.
key_findings: Intraindividual log(TKV)-eGFR relationship is linear within each Mayo Imaging Class
1% per year reduction in TKV growth rate predicts ~0.4-0.5 mL/min/1.73m2/year slower eGFR decline (classes 1C-1E)
Provides quantitative framework linking TKV treatment effect magnitude to expected eGFR benefit
Explicitly intended to support FDA accelerated approval decision-making for ADPKD drugs
papers.novelty_assessment: Novel intraindividual modeling approach that translates TKV effect sizes into expected eGFR benefit — a key regulatory science gap for ADPKD drug approval.
papers.clinical_implications: Not directly clinical; informs regulatory pathway and trial design for ADPKD drug developers and biomarker qualifiers.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Likely industry interactions given FDA-facing framing; not fully audited here

papers.what_happened: Authors built an intraindividual mixed-effects model from CRISP and HALT-PKD Study A data relating log(TKV) to eGFR by Mayo Imaging Class, producing quantitative estimates of the eGFR benefit expected from a given TKV treatment effect.
papers.why_it_matters: This is directly relevant to whether FDA will accept TKV reduction as a surrogate endpoint for accelerated approval of ADPKD drugs, affecting the entire pipeline (VX-407, ABBV-CLS-628, PYC-003, JMKX003142, farabursen).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Observational intraindividual modeling rather than trial-based validation; generalization to novel mechanisms and advanced classes (2, 1E late) remains uncertain; inter-study heterogeneity not fully characterized.

papers.title: Tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: Real-world insights from a propensity score weighted retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Single-centre retrospective cohort of 327 ADPKD patients (119 tolvaptan-treated, 208 untreated). After propensity-score overlap weighting, tolvaptan was associated with a non-significant +0.45 mL/min/1.73m2/year slowing in chronic eGFR slope (95% CI -0.37 to +1.18). 52.1% of tolvaptan patients discontinued within 12 months, primarily due to aquaretic side effects. Subgroup analyses in patients treated ≥1 year (+0.58) or responders treated ≥2 years (+0.78) showed larger point estimates. Mean follow-up 61.4 months.
key_findings: N=327 (119 tolvaptan vs 208 untreated), mean follow-up 61.4 months
Primary analysis: +0.45 mL/min/1.73m2/year (95% CI -0.37 to +1.18) — not statistically significant; CI compatible with no effect
52.1% discontinued within 12 months, predominantly for aquaretic side effects
Subgroup estimates larger in long-term treated/responders (+0.58 to +0.78), but subject to survivor bias
Directionally consistent across complete-case, overlap-weighted, and multiple imputation analyses
papers.novelty_assessment: Real-world evidence for tolvaptan with smaller effect than TEMPO 3:4 and very high discontinuation rate; one of several RWE datasets emerging in 2026.
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces that real-world tolvaptan benefit may be smaller than trial estimates, largely due to treatment discontinuation; supports counseling expectations around tolerability.
papers.what_happened: Single-centre retrospective propensity-weighted cohort (n=327) found a non-significant +0.45 mL/min/1.73m2/year eGFR slope improvement with tolvaptan and 52% 1-year discontinuation.
papers.why_it_matters: Real-world tolvaptan effectiveness appears smaller than TEMPO 3:4 estimates, largely driven by high early discontinuation; relevant for patient counseling and implementation.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-centre retrospective design; confounding by indication, informative censoring, survivor bias in long-term subgroups; primary CI includes null.

papers.title: Evolution of Clinical Trial Design in ADPKD.
papers.abstract: Narrative review of how ADPKD trial design has evolved from eGFR/kidney-failure endpoints to TKV as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint. Covers CRISP validation, HALT-PKD, TEMPO 3:4, and discusses limitations of the TKV-GFR relationship. Proposes adaptive designs, master protocols (platform/umbrella), and target trial emulation as next-generation approaches.
key_findings: Reviews transition from functional endpoints to TKV as reasonably likely surrogate in ADPKD
Notes limitations of TKV-GFR translation
Advocates for adaptive designs, platform/umbrella trials, and target trial emulation in ADPKD pipeline
papers.novelty_assessment: Review with no new data; synthesis of trial-design evolution for pipeline stakeholders.
papers.clinical_implications: Informs researchers and sponsors on trial-design options for ADPKD drug development.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Authors are ADPKD academic/clinical trialists; likely pharma interactions

papers.what_happened: Narrative review synthesizing the evolution of ADPKD clinical trial design, covering TKV validation history and proposing adaptive/platform/target-trial-emulation approaches.
papers.why_it_matters: Complements Yu et al's TKV-eGFR framework and provides a design roadmap for the expanding ADPKD pipeline (VX-407, ABBV-CLS-628, PYC-003, farabursen, JMKX003142).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no original data; proposed approaches are aspirational and not yet widely implemented in ADPKD trials.

papers.title: Clinical Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Review of AI applications in ADPKD including AI-powered TKV measurement, ML integration of genetic/imaging/clinical data for progression prediction, AI-assisted genotype-phenotype refinement, longitudinal MRI/CT tracking, and optimization of trial patient selection and safety monitoring.
key_findings: AI-based TKV measurement reduces manual segmentation burden and may improve consistency
ML integration of multimodal data for progression risk stratification
AI-assisted trial design applications (enrichment, safety monitoring)
Authors note implementation challenges and validation gaps
papers.novelty_assessment: Review synthesizing current AI applications; no new data but useful field snapshot.
papers.clinical_implications: Informs researchers and clinicians about emerging AI tools that may support ADPKD monitoring and trial design.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Chebib is a major ADPKD clinician-researcher with industry interactions

papers.what_happened: Narrative review of current and potential AI/ML applications in ADPKD across imaging, genotype-phenotype, and trial design.
papers.why_it_matters: AI-assisted TKV and progression modeling are increasingly relevant as regulatory and clinical frameworks expand around surrogate endpoints.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Review only; many cited AI applications lack prospective validation or regulatory clearance.

papers.title: Long-Term Tolvaptan Administration in Chinese Patients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Study in Real Clinical Practice.
papers.abstract: Multicenter retrospective cohort of 83 Chinese ADPKD patients (40 tolvaptan 15 mg BID vs 43 unmedicated) showing htTKV% growth reductions of -5.58 at year 1 and -9.75 at year 2, and +6.79 mL/min/1.73m2 eGFR difference at year 2 (all p<0.001). SF-36 PCS improved in treated group. Aquaretic AEs substantially more frequent in tolvaptan group.
key_findings: N=83 (40 tolvaptan 15 mg BID vs 43 unmedicated), retrospective
htTKV growth -5.58 at year 1, -9.75 at year 2 (95% CIs do not cross zero)
eGFR difference +6.79 mL/min/1.73m2 at year 2
SF-36 physical component improved in treated group
Aquaretic AEs (thirst, polyuria, urinary frequency) significantly higher in tolvaptan group
papers.novelty_assessment: First Chinese real-world cohort; effect sizes broadly consistent with TEMPO 3:4 but low n and retrospective design.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports extending tolvaptan effectiveness observations to Chinese ADPKD patients.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not assessed here; Otsuka likely funds China tolvaptan research

papers.what_happened: Small multicenter Chinese retrospective cohort reported htTKV and eGFR benefits favoring tolvaptan consistent with TEMPO 3:4, plus expected aquaretic side effects.
papers.why_it_matters: Extends tolvaptan observational evidence to a Chinese population and documents persistence of aquaretic AEs in real-world use.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective, small n=83, no propensity adjustment described, no randomization; confounding by indication likely; conclusions of 'effectiveness' from observational data are overstated.

papers.title: Somatostatin analog therapy in delaying progression of polycystic liver disease: A meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis.
papers.abstract: Meta-analysis of RCTs (through May 2025) evaluating somatostatin analogs in polycystic liver disease. Primary endpoints: % change from baseline in total liver volume, total kidney volume, and eGFR. Trial sequential analysis performed for all three.
key_findings: Meta-analysis of RCTs through May 2025 on somatostatin analogs for PLD
Evaluates total liver volume, TKV, and eGFR
Uses trial sequential analysis to assess whether evidence is conclusive
Complements the Jin et al octreotide LAR ADPKD meta-analysis (pm_41647114) by focusing on liver endpoints
papers.novelty_assessment: Meta-analysis that complements Jin et al 2026 ADPKD-focused octreotide meta; liver endpoints are the primary focus here.
papers.clinical_implications: Informs somatostatin-analog decision-making for patients with symptomatic polycystic liver disease.
papers.what_happened: Meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis of RCTs evaluating somatostatin analogs in polycystic liver disease with liver, kidney volume, and eGFR endpoints.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides PLD-focused evidence synthesis relevant for symptomatic ADPKD patients with major liver involvement where CAM2029 Phase 2/3 is ongoing (NCT05281328).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Full results/conclusions not available in fetched abstract; small number of underlying PLD RCTs; endpoints are surrogate (volume) rather than symptom-based.

papers.title: PAX gene expression in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease contributes to cyst expansion and regulates a gene network associated with cyst growth.
papers.abstract: PAX2 (nuclear) and PAX8 (cytoplasmic) were found upregulated in cyst-lining epithelia from human ADPKD kidneys. siRNA knockdown of either reduced 3D spheroid growth in MDCK and WT9-7/9-12 cell models. RNA-seq revealed PAX2 regulates embryonic development/ER stress/cilia pathways; PAX8 regulates cell cycle/adhesion; combined knockdown affects ECM organization. Shared downstream targets included AGO2 and WWTR1. Authors propose PAX2/PAX8 as therapeutic targets.
key_findings: PAX2 and PAX8 upregulated in human ADPKD cyst-lining cells
siRNA knockdown reduces 3D spheroid growth in renal epithelial cell lines
Distinct pathway regulation (PAX2: development/ER stress/cilia; PAX8: cell cycle/adhesion)
Combined knockdown impacts ECM organization
AGO2, WWTR1 identified as shared targets
papers.novelty_assessment: New mechanistic hypothesis implicating PAX2/PAX8 in ADPKD cystogenesis; in vitro only.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical translation; identifies candidate targets for preclinical development.
papers.what_happened: In vitro study showing PAX2/PAX8 upregulation in ADPKD cyst epithelium and that siRNA knockdown reduces cystic spheroid growth with distinct downstream gene networks.
papers.why_it_matters: Identifies new candidate pathways/targets for preclinical ADPKD drug development, though clinical translation remains distant.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro only, no animal or human validation; ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: Quantitative dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging for renal perfusion measurement in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.journal: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery
papers.abstract: Evaluation of quantitative DCE-MRI as a complementary functional imaging biomarker to TKV in ADPKD, with a focus on distinguishing mild vs rapidly progressive disease activity. TKV indices reflect cumulative change and may lag current disease activity; DCE-MRI assesses renal perfusion as a functional counterpart.
key_findings: DCE-MRI evaluated as a biomarker complementary to TKV for current disease activity
Applied to mild and rapidly progressive ADPKD cohorts
Full results not available in fetched abstract
papers.novelty_assessment: Functional imaging biomarker approach complementary to anatomical TKV; early-stage biomarker research.
papers.clinical_implications: Could inform future biomarker strategy; not clinically actionable yet.
papers.what_happened: Biomarker study evaluating quantitative DCE-MRI renal perfusion in mild vs rapidly progressive ADPKD as a complement to anatomical TKV.
papers.why_it_matters: Functional imaging biomarkers could improve detection of current disease activity and enrich clinical trial populations.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Full results/conclusions not available in fetched abstract; DCE-MRI validation as ADPKD biomarker remains early-stage.

papers.title: Disruption of a six-nucleotide miRNA motif improves PKD1 dosage and ameliorates polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Preclinical study showing that disrupting a six-nucleotide miRNA regulatory motif increases PKD1 mRNA/protein dosage and ameliorates cystic disease in a polycystic kidney disease mouse model. Now indexed in PubMed alongside the peer-reviewed Lakhia NAR 2026 paper (pm_41558825/ss_a8f827f).
key_findings: Preclinical bioRxiv preprint later published in NAR 2026
Disruption of a six-nucleotide miRNA motif increases PKD1 dosage
Ameliorates cystic disease in mouse model
Companion/duplicate of the peer-reviewed Lakhia et al NAR 2026 publication
papers.novelty_assessment: Early mechanistic demonstration that small-molecule or ASO disruption of PKD1 miRNA regulation could be a therapeutic strategy; complements farabursen (miR-17) development.
papers.clinical_implications: None directly; strategic pipeline relevance given Regulus/Novartis farabursen program.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not assessed here; may overlap with Regulus/farabursen development interests

papers.what_happened: bioRxiv preprint (since published in NAR 2026) demonstrating that disrupting a PKD1 miRNA regulatory motif increases polycystin-1 expression and ameliorates disease in a PKD mouse model.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides mechanistic support for the miRNA-targeting therapeutic strategy already in clinical development (farabursen).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical model only; ADPKD has poor preclinical-to-clinical translation; preprint status of this index entry (peer-reviewed version exists separately).

papers.title: An intronic micro-deletion impacts the transcription and translation of PKD1 gene.
papers.abstract: Case/molecular study characterizing a novel intronic PKD1 micro-deletion and its effects on PKD1 mRNA splicing/translation — relevant for non-coding variant interpretation in ADPKD molecular diagnosis.
key_findings: Novel intronic PKD1 micro-deletion identified
Affects PKD1 transcription and translation
Expands catalog of non-coding ADPKD-causing variants
papers.novelty_assessment: Incremental variant characterization; useful for diagnostic labs but low clinical-decision impact.
papers.clinical_implications: May assist interpretation of otherwise 'unsolved' ADPKD genetic testing with intronic PKD1 variants.
papers.what_happened: Report of a novel intronic PKD1 micro-deletion shown to disrupt PKD1 transcription and translation.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to the catalog of non-coding ADPKD variants and supports wider intronic screening in molecular diagnostics.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-variant characterization; no large cohort evaluation of frequency or phenotype.

papers.title: Evaluating gene variations in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease patients using whole exome sequencing and phenotype to genotype analysis.
papers.abstract: Whole exome sequencing cohort study of ADPKD patients with phenotype-to-genotype analysis.
key_findings: WES cohort characterization of ADPKD variants
Phenotype-genotype correlation analysis
papers.novelty_assessment: Incremental addition to ADPKD genotype-phenotype literature.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports broader WES-based genetic testing in ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective WES cohort study characterizing PKD1/PKD2 and related variants and their phenotypic correlates in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to genotype-phenotype reference data for ADPKD.

papers.title: Effect of tolvaptan on the prognosis of patients with rapidly progressive autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a prospective open-label study
papers.abstract: Prospective open-label study evaluating tolvaptan effect on prognosis in rapidly progressive ADPKD. Full methods and results not available in the SS metadata.

Full study details not available from metadata only

papers.title: Heterogeneous regulation of fibroblast growth factor 23 in acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, and polycystic kidney disease: mechanisms, diagnostic utility, and clinical implications.

papers.title: The Prevalence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Significance of Inferior Vena Cava Compression in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study Based on TriNetX.

papers.title: Perioperative complications in native nephrectomy as a therapeutic approach for symptomatic polycystic kidney disease: a comprehensive study.
papers.abstract: Retrospective single-center analysis of 124 native nephrectomy episodes in ADPKD (2012-2022). Perioperative complications occurred in 73/124 (58.9%); major (Clavien-Dindo III+) in 31 (25%). Lower preoperative hemoglobin (OR 0.74 per g/dL) predicted overall complications; left-sided nephrectomy had lower complication risk; diverticulosis predicted major complications (OR 5.03). Simultaneous bilateral nephrectomy had highest complication rate (69.7%). MIS not independently associated with lower complication risk after adjustment for kidney size.
key_findings: Native nephrectomy in ADPKD carries 58.9% overall and 25% major perioperative complication rate
Lower preoperative hemoglobin and right-sided nephrectomy independently increase complication risk
Simultaneous bilateral nephrectomy has the highest complication burden
Minimally invasive surgery does not independently reduce complications once specimen size is accounted for
papers.novelty_assessment: Single-center retrospective with usable risk-factor signal; not a new clinical question, but adds modern volume data on a procedure restricted to severe symptomatic disease.
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces selective use of native nephrectomy and supports caution with simultaneous bilateral procedures and patients with low preoperative hemoglobin.
papers.what_happened: Single-center retrospective review of 124 ADPKD native nephrectomy episodes reports 58.9% overall and 25% major perioperative complications, with low hemoglobin, right-sided procedures, diverticulosis, and simultaneous bilateral surgery as the main risk drivers.
papers.why_it_matters: Patients evaluating native nephrectomy for symptomatic disease or transplant preparation now have a contemporary single-center benchmark for complication frequency and modifiable risk factors.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center, retrospective, no comparator group, with selection bias toward surgical candidates; minimally invasive vs open comparisons confounded by markedly different specimen sizes.

papers.title: Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on KDIGO 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: CARI Guidelines Working Group regional commentary on KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline for Australia and New Zealand. Highlights implementation barriers including public subsidy limitations for genetic testing and tolvaptan, and rural/remote equity issues. Does not introduce new evidence; contextualizes international guidance for AU/NZ practice.
key_findings: Regional adaptation of KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guidance for AU/NZ context
Identifies public subsidy gaps for genetic testing and tolvaptan as implementation barriers
Highlights rural/remote and Indigenous equity considerations not addressed in KDIGO

papers.clinical_implications: Useful for AU/NZ clinicians navigating local reimbursement and equity issues; limited generalizability outside region.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Likely group authorship with mixed academic/clinical affiliations; not fully audited

papers.what_happened: The CARI working group published a regional commentary on the KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline tailored to Australian and New Zealand practice, focusing on public subsidy and equity gaps.
papers.why_it_matters: AU/NZ clinicians implementing KDIGO 2025 now have a region-specific overlay flagging tolvaptan and genetic testing access barriers and rural/Indigenous equity considerations.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Commentary, not new evidence; recommendations are jurisdiction-specific and depend on payer policy that may shift independently of guidance.

papers.title: Clinical Utility of Standardized Genetic Testing in Kidney Transplant Candidate Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Observational cohort of 270 KT candidates undergoing standardized genetic testing (Jan 2021-Nov 2024). 38.5% positive yield; family history independently predicted positive results. Diagnostic reclassification, donor evaluation, and counseling implications assessed. ADPKD is one of several inherited kidney diseases captured; not the primary focus.
key_findings: Standardized genetic testing in 270 KT candidates yielded 38.5% positive results
Family history was an independent predictor (aOR 1.91)
Indications included family history, hypertension-attributed ESKD without biopsy, and unknown ESKD etiology
papers.novelty_assessment: ADPKD-relevant only as one component of broader transplant genetic testing yield analysis; informs counseling/donor selection but not ADPKD-specific decision making.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports genetic testing as part of pre-transplant evaluation, particularly when family history present; relevance to ADPKD limited to confirmation of diagnosis and family donor screening.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not fully audited; multi-author transplant centre study

papers.what_happened: Observational cohort of 270 kidney transplant candidates undergoing standardized genetic testing reported a 38.5% positive yield, with family history as the strongest predictor.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds modern data on the diagnostic yield of pre-transplant genetic testing, which is relevant to ADPKD case confirmation and living-donor screening among at-risk relatives.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-program cohort, no concurrent untested comparator, ADPKD subset and outcomes not separately analyzed in this report.

papers.title: A C. elegans model for functional analysis of ADPKD variants in cilia, extracellular vesicles, and sensory signaling
papers.abstract: Preprint describing a Caenorhabditis elegans model engineered to functionally characterize ADPKD-associated PKD1/PKD2 variants in cilia, extracellular vesicle biology, and sensory signaling. Intended as a higher-throughput VUS reclassification platform.
key_findings: C. elegans-based functional assay platform for ADPKD variants
Targets cilia, extracellular vesicle, and sensory signaling readouts
Aims to support classification of variants of uncertain significance

papers.clinical_implications: None today; potential downstream value if validated against curated variant truth sets.
papers.what_happened: A bioRxiv preprint describes a C. elegans-based functional assay platform intended to help reclassify ADPKD PKD1/PKD2 variants of uncertain significance.
papers.why_it_matters: If validated, model organism functional assays could complement in silico tools for resolving ADPKD variant classifications relevant to family screening.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, no peer review, abstract-level visibility, model-organism findings have weak translational track record in ADPKD.

papers.title: Treatment of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: Narrative review on ADPKD management focused on facilitating implementation of contemporary guidelines. Integrates evidence on disease-modifying therapy (tolvaptan), risk stratification, real-world effectiveness, and patient perspectives. Discusses barriers to individualized care.
key_findings: Synthesizes tolvaptan use, risk stratification, and individualized care barriers
Aimed at supporting practical implementation of KDIGO/KDOQI guidelines
Integrates patient perspective and real-world effectiveness data

papers.clinical_implications: Useful summary for clinicians implementing 2025 guidelines; strength is teaching/synthesis, not new data.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Likely industry interactions for review authors; not fully audited

papers.what_happened: A JASN narrative review summarizes contemporary ADPKD treatment, risk stratification, real-world tolvaptan effectiveness, and barriers to individualized care.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a state-of-the-art synthesis suitable for clinicians and trainees implementing the 2025 ADPKD guideline updates.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no new data; selection of supporting evidence is at author discretion.

papers.title: Eight Years of Canadian Real-World Assessment of Tolvaptan in Patients With Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: The C-MAJOR Registry.
papers.journal: Canadian Journal of Kidney Health and Disease
papers.abstract: C-MAJOR is a non-interventional multicenter Canadian registry of ADPKD patients on tolvaptan, mandated by Health Canada in 2015. This baseline-characteristics paper describes 470 patients enrolled across 24 sites (data through Dec 2023). Mean age at diagnosis 29.8 y, at tolvaptan initiation 44.4 y. Primary objective is HRQoL via PROs; secondary outcomes include time to KRT, mortality, kidney function, adherence, discontinuation, and AEs. Follow-up data not yet reported in this baseline paper.
key_findings: 470 ADPKD patients on tolvaptan enrolled across 24 Canadian centers
Mean tolvaptan initiation age 44.4 years; baseline TKV and eGFR distribution described
Long-term HRQoL, KRT, and AE outcomes will follow in subsequent reports
papers.novelty_assessment: Baseline / methodology paper for an ongoing registry; the corresponding WCN26-4375 conference abstract reports preliminary PRO data. No outcome results yet.
papers.clinical_implications: Establishes infrastructure for long-term real-world tolvaptan outcome data in Canada; no immediate practice change.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Otsuka-related registry mandated by Health Canada; commercial sponsor

papers.what_happened: Baseline characteristics and study design publication for the Canadian C-MAJOR ADPKD tolvaptan registry (n=470 across 24 sites, data through December 2023).
papers.why_it_matters: C-MAJOR is one of the largest national real-world tolvaptan datasets and will provide long-term HRQoL, KRT, and safety outcomes that complement TEMPO/REPRISE.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-arm sponsor-mandated registry without an untreated comparator; outcomes data not yet available; selection bias toward eligible/persisting tolvaptan users.

papers.title: WCN26-4375 EIGHT YEARS OF CANADIAN REAL-WORLD ASSESSMENT OF TOLVAPTAN IN ADPKD: PATIENT REPORTED OUTCOMES FROM THE C-MAJOR STUDY
papers.abstract: WCN 2026 conference abstract. Patient-reported outcome data from the Canadian C-MAJOR tolvaptan registry. Companion to PMID 41541406 baseline paper.

Companion to baseline registry paper (PMID 41541406)
