papers.what_limits_confidence: Conference abstract only with no detailed methods or full PRO data tables; sponsor-mandated single-arm design.

papers.title: The Relationship of Osmolality and Kidney Outcomes in Patients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Prospective Hong Kong CysticHK cohort of 311 tolvaptan-naive ADPKD patients with serial serum and urine osmolality measurements every 6 months over 5 years. Primary outcome 40% eGFR decline. Patients in the highest serum osmolality quartile had 5.91x higher risk of 40% eGFR decline vs lowest (p=0.018). Serum osmolality AUC 0.81 for predicting kidney decline; urine osmolality not predictive (AUC 0.35).
key_findings: Higher serum osmolality predicted faster eGFR decline (HR ~5.9 between top vs bottom quartile)
Serum osmolality AUC 0.81 for 40% eGFR decline prediction; urine osmolality not predictive
Prospective serial measurements over 5 years in tolvaptan-naive ADPKD (n=311)
papers.novelty_assessment: Prospective cohort with serial osmolality and clinically relevant kidney endpoint; informative for biomarker monitoring but observational.
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests serum osmolality as a candidate prognostic marker; does not establish that lowering osmolality (e.g., increased water intake) improves outcomes.
papers.what_happened: Prospective Hong Kong CysticHK cohort of 311 tolvaptan-naive ADPKD patients with 5 years of serial serum/urine osmolality found higher serum osmolality strongly associated with 40% eGFR decline.
papers.why_it_matters: Identifies serum osmolality as a candidate inexpensive prognostic marker in tolvaptan-naive ADPKD; complements existing TKV-based risk tools.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Observational, no intervention arm; cannot establish that increasing water intake to lower osmolality slows disease; tolvaptan-naive cohort limits generalizability to treated patients.

papers.title: BICC1 interacts with PKD1 and PKD2 to drive cystogenesis in ADPKD.
papers.abstract: Mechanistic study showing BICC1 protein physically interacts with PKD1 and PKD2 and contributes to cystogenesis in ADPKD models. Adds molecular detail to the polycystin signaling network and posits BICC1 as a candidate modifier of cyst growth.
key_findings: BICC1 physically interacts with polycystins PKD1 and PKD2
BICC1 disruption modifies cystogenesis in ADPKD models
Suggests BICC1 as candidate node for polycystin pathway modulation
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds mechanistic depth to polycystin biology; potentially nominates a new modifier locus, but no clinical or pharmacologic translation here.
papers.clinical_implications: None today; mechanistic plausibility only.
papers.what_happened: Mechanistic eLife paper reports that BICC1 physically interacts with PKD1 and PKD2 and contributes to cystogenesis in ADPKD models.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds a new molecular partner to the polycystin signaling network and nominates BICC1 as a possible therapeutic node.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical mechanistic study only; ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation track record, and no drug-like modulators of BICC1 are described here.

papers.title: Prevalence and Genetic Spectrum of Inherited Kidney Diseases
papers.abstract: Exome sequencing of 290 patients (261 families) with kidney disease of unknown etiology in two Chinese centers. Diagnostic yield 31% (82/261). PKD1, PKD2, COL4A3-A5, and UMOD accounted for 50% of diagnoses. Ciliopathies most common subtype. Higher diagnostic yield in age groups <=20 (63%) and >=41 (39%).
key_findings: 31% diagnostic yield for ES in unexplained kidney disease (n=290)
PKD1/PKD2 plus COL4A3-A5 and UMOD account for half of diagnoses
Ciliopathies most prevalent inherited subtype in this Chinese cohort
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds Chinese-population genetic landscape data; PKD1/PKD2 prominence consistent with prior literature.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports broad ES use in unexplained CKD; not ADPKD-specific decision making.
papers.what_happened: Two-center Chinese ES study of 290 patients with unexplained kidney disease reports a 31% diagnostic yield, with PKD1/PKD2 among the leading genes.
papers.why_it_matters: Confirms PKD genes as dominant contributors to inherited kidney disease in another major population, supporting broad pre-test counseling and family cascade screening.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Selected referral cohort with known enrichment for genetic disease; not ADPKD-specific outcome data.

papers.title: Phosphaturia Exacerbates Tubular Injury and Cyst Formation in Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Pkd1RC/RC mice fed high phosphate diet showed accelerated cyst growth, fibrosis activation, and phosphate-based crystal deposition co-localized with macrophages. Phosphaturic Slc34a1-/- mice developed nephrocalcinosis, tubular microcyst formation, and early kidney injury. Compound Pkd1RC/RC; Slc34a1-/- mutants had increased cyst burden and reduced kidney function vs Pkd1RC/RC controls. Trace mineral analysis of human PKD vs control kidneys revealed consistent calcium-phosphate microcrystal deposition. Authors propose urinary phosphate excretion and tubular mineral solubility as candidate therapeutic targets.
key_findings: High dietary phosphate accelerated cyst growth and induced phosphate crystal deposition in Pkd1RC/RC mice
Phosphaturic Slc34a1-/- mice developed tubular microcysts and nephrocalcinosis without a Pkd1 mutation
Compound Pkd1RC/RC; Slc34a1-/- mutants had worse cyst burden and kidney function than Pkd1 mutants alone
Human PKD kidneys consistently showed calcium-phosphate microcrystal deposits on imaging and trace mineral analysis
papers.novelty_assessment: Novel mechanistic angle linking urinary phosphate handling to PKD progression in animal models with corroborating human imaging; preclinical only.
papers.clinical_implications: No immediate clinical action; raises a research hypothesis that phosphate management could modulate cyst progression, but ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation track record.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in abstract; multi-author Kansas-based PKD research group

papers.what_happened: Mouse genetic and dietary experiments suggest urinary phosphate excretion drives tubular injury and accelerates cyst growth in a Pkd1 model, with parallel evidence of calcium-phosphate microcrystal deposition in human PKD kidneys.
papers.why_it_matters: Phosphate handling is a modifiable variable in CKD care, so a mechanistic link to PKD progression could open a new disease-modifying angle if it survives clinical testing.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical mouse genetics with descriptive human imaging only — no patient outcomes, no controlled trial of phosphate-targeted intervention, and ADPKD preclinical signals have historically translated poorly.

papers.title: Novel roles of GPCRs in the renal collecting duct.
papers.abstract: Narrative review on GPCR signaling in the renal collecting duct. Discusses classical V2R biology and emerging roles for GPR39, ADGRF5, ADGRG3, plus atypical GPCR-related signaling involving PKD1 and MAGED2. Frames PKD1 within an expanded GPCR conceptual framework relevant to collecting duct physiology and disease.
key_findings: Reviews V2R as the established collecting-duct GPCR and links to vasopressin antagonist therapy
Positions PKD1 within an expanded GPCR conceptual framework for collecting duct physiology
Highlights underexplored GPCRs (GPR39, ADGRF5, ADGRG3) as candidate therapeutic targets
papers.novelty_assessment: Narrative review with PKD1 as one of several examples; not new ADPKD data, but useful conceptual context for V2R-adjacent signaling.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct implications; supplies background for thinking about V2R-class targets and tolvaptan-adjacent biology.
papers.what_happened: Narrative review covers GPCR biology in the renal collecting duct, including V2R and an expanded GPCR framework that incorporates PKD1.
papers.why_it_matters: Connects V2R/vasopressin biology underlying tolvaptan to a broader catalog of collecting-duct GPCRs that may be future targets.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review; PKD1 is one of several examples and the article presents no new ADPKD-specific data.

papers.title: Association of 24-hour urinary parameters with renal function and other comorbidities in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Retrospective single-center study of 42 ADPKD patients stratified by eGFR. Reduced 24-h urinary calcium (44 vs 94.5 mg/day), uric acid (307 vs 492.3 mg/day), and citrate (110 vs 550 mg/day) all associated with eGFR <60. Authors note the urinary changes parallel those seen in general CKD and likely reflect declining kidney function rather than ADPKD-specific metabolism.
papers.novelty_assessment: Small descriptive observational study; findings echo general CKD literature rather than identifying ADPKD-specific signal.
key_findings: 24-h urinary calcium, uric acid, and citrate excretion were lower in ADPKD patients with eGFR <60 vs ≥60
Low citrate excretion was associated with prior nephrolithiasis history
Pattern parallels general CKD, suggesting changes are driven by GFR loss not disease-specific
papers.clinical_implications: No immediate clinical action; reinforces existing CKD-stage-based monitoring.
papers.what_happened: Single-center Turkish retrospective study (n=42 ADPKD) reports lower urinary calcium, uric acid, and citrate excretion among patients with eGFR <60.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds incremental data to ADPKD metabolic phenotyping but largely recapitulates general CKD mineral handling.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small n, retrospective single-center design, no longitudinal follow-up, and no ADPKD-vs-non-ADPKD CKD comparator means findings cannot be attributed to ADPKD-specific biology.

papers.title: Bone Phenotype in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Bone phenotype ADPKD authors (full list in PubMed)
papers.abstract: Cross-sectional study of 81 ADPKD patients, 15 non-ADPKD CKD, and 21 healthy controls. Measured bone metabolism/turnover biomarkers, DXA with TBS, and bone material strength via microindentation (BMSi). ADPKD patients showed lower bone turnover (PINP, BALP in CKD G1-2) but BMSi, BMD, and TBS were comparable to healthy individuals. Mineral abnormalities tracked CKD stage rather than Mayo Imaging Classification, suggesting bone phenotype follows kidney function decline rather than cyst burden.
papers.novelty_assessment: First comprehensive multi-domain bone phenotyping in ADPKD; descriptive characterization without therapeutic implications.
key_findings: ADPKD shows lower bone turnover but preserved bone mass/microarchitecture
Bone alterations track CKD stage rather than Mayo Imaging Classification
BMSi did not reveal a distinctive ADPKD pattern
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces CKD-MBD framework; no specific bone-protective intervention indicated for ADPKD beyond standard CKD care.
papers.what_happened: Cross-sectional bone phenotyping in 81 ADPKD patients showed lower bone turnover but preserved bone mass; alterations tracked CKD stage not cyst burden.
papers.why_it_matters: Clarifies that ADPKD bone disease is largely an extension of CKD-MBD rather than a polycystin-specific bone phenotype.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional, modest sample sizes per CKD stratum, no longitudinal fracture or hard outcome data, and findings published 3 months ago (stale for current digest window).

papers.title: Reversible cystogenesis in juvenile primate ADPKD models: evidence from PKD1 heterozygous monkeys.
authors: Primate ADPKD authors (full list in PubMed)
papers.abstract: Longitudinal study of PKD1 heterozygous cynomolgus monkeys with serial renal ultrasonography from birth to 5 years. Heterozygous animals showed progressive cyst formation with apparent spontaneous regression of smaller cysts. PKD1 mosaic monkeys showed similar patterns; biallelic loss-of-function animals developed severe cystic disease, kidney enlargement, hepatic cysts, and elevated creatinine. Authors propose early-stage cysts may have intrinsic plasticity, suggesting a therapeutic window in juveniles.
papers.novelty_assessment: Novel non-rodent ADPKD model; cyst regression observation is provocative but rests on imaging in a small primate cohort.
key_findings: PKD1+/- cynomolgus monkeys develop progressive cysts unlike PKD1+/- mice
Smaller cysts showed apparent spontaneous regression on serial ultrasound
Biallelic PKD1 LOF produces severe cystic + hepatic disease
papers.clinical_implications: None today; framework for testing early-intervention agents in a more human-like preclinical model.
papers.what_happened: Serial renal ultrasonography in PKD1 heterozygous cynomolgus monkeys from birth to 5 years documented cyst growth and apparent regression of smaller cysts.
papers.why_it_matters: If reproducible, a primate ADPKD model that recapitulates juvenile cystogenesis would be useful for testing early-intervention therapeutics; the cyst-plasticity observation, if validated, would refine current dogma.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Sample sizes not in abstract, ultrasound-based measurement, ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation has historically been weak, and the 'reversibility' framing may overstate what serial 2D imaging can establish.

papers.title: Glycolytic alterations as biomarkers in polycystic kidney disease: A study using a PKD1 knockout model in NRK-52E rat kidney epithelial cells.
authors: Glycolytic biomarkers PKD1 KO authors (full list in PubMed)
papers.abstract: Investigation of glycolytic metabolism in PKD1 knockout NRK-52E rat kidney epithelial cells using DNP-enhanced hyperpolarized 13C MRS. Aimed at identifying metabolic biomarker candidates of PKD1 loss in vitro.
papers.novelty_assessment: Cell-line metabolic profiling; mechanistically interesting but distant from clinical biomarker validation.
key_findings: PKD1 knockout alters glycolytic readouts detectable by hyperpolarized MRS
Proposed as candidate metabolic biomarker pathway
papers.clinical_implications: None today; validation in animal models and human samples required before considering as biomarker.
papers.what_happened: PKD1 knockout in NRK-52E rat tubular cells altered glycolytic metabolism on hyperpolarized 13C MRS.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to the metabolic-reprogramming hypothesis in PKD; relevant for tracking ketogenic diet and glycolysis-targeting research lines.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro rat cell line only, no translation to in vivo or human samples, abstract truncated in our retrieval.

papers.title: Activation of farnesoid X receptor inhibits TMEM16A-mediated chloride secretion in renal collecting duct cells and retards renal cyst progression.
authors: FXR TMEM16A authors (full list in PubMed)
papers.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Renal Physiology
papers.abstract: FXR activation inhibits TMEM16A-mediated chloride secretion in renal collecting duct cells and retards renal cyst progression. Builds on prior work showing FXR activation also inhibited CFTR-mediated Cl- secretion.
papers.novelty_assessment: Mechanistic preclinical paper extending FXR/Cl-channel axis as a candidate target for cyst growth.
key_findings: FXR activation inhibits TMEM16A-mediated Cl secretion
Retards cyst progression in preclinical models
Complements prior FXR/CFTR inhibition findings
papers.clinical_implications: None today; supports research priority for FXR agonists or TMEM16A inhibitors as cyst-growth modulators.
papers.what_happened: Preclinical study reports FXR activation inhibits TMEM16A-mediated chloride secretion in collecting duct cells and slows cyst progression.
papers.why_it_matters: Reinforces chloride-secretion blockade as a candidate disease-modifying mechanism in ADPKD beyond the CFTR axis.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical only, ADPKD has weak preclinical-to-clinical translation, no abstract details on quantitative effect size.

papers.title: Apelin inhibits cyst growth and improves kidney function in mice with polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: bioRxiv preprint reporting that the apelin pathway inhibits cyst growth and improves kidney function in a mouse PKD model. Abstract not yet available in indexed sources.
papers.novelty_assessment: Preprint, novel target in ADPKD; preclinical and not peer-reviewed.
key_findings: Apelin pathway reduces cyst growth in mouse PKD
Reported improvement in kidney function readouts
papers.clinical_implications: None today; mechanistic candidate for further preclinical work.
papers.what_happened: bioRxiv preprint claims apelin signaling inhibits cyst growth and improves kidney function in mouse PKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds apelin to the list of candidate pathways for cyst-growth modulation; testable in additional preclinical models.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint without indexed abstract or methods, not peer-reviewed, ADPKD has weak preclinical-to-clinical translation, single-target claim.

papers.title: miRNA profiling of a mutation-negative PKD cohort reveals PKD1/PKD2 ADPKD shared signatures and differences
papers.abstract: miRNA profiling study examining ADPKD patients without identified PKD1/PKD2 pathogenic variants, reporting shared signatures with PKD1 and PKD2 ADPKD plus differences specific to mutation-negative disease.
papers.novelty_assessment: Examines the clinically relevant mutation-negative ADPKD subgroup using transcriptomic profiling; could inform classification but unlikely to change practice now.
key_findings: Mutation-negative ADPKD shows miRNA signatures overlapping PKD1/PKD2 disease
Differences from PKD1/PKD2 cases also reported
papers.clinical_implications: Research only; supports continued effort to characterize the no-mutation-found ADPKD subgroup.
papers.what_happened: miRNA profiling study reports shared and distinct signatures in mutation-negative ADPKD versus PKD1/PKD2 cases.
papers.why_it_matters: Mutation-negative ADPKD remains a clinically tricky subgroup; molecular characterization may inform future risk-stratification.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract details limited, sample size and validation cohorts unclear, miRNA studies frequently fail to replicate.

papers.title: Segmental Caroli's Disease in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Rare Association
papers.journal: Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research
papers.abstract: Case report of a 40-year-old man with known ADPKD found incidentally during MRI volumetry to have segmental Caroli's disease in hepatic segments V and VI, with the characteristic 'central dot sign'. Highlights rare phenotypic overlap between ciliopathies.
papers.novelty_assessment: Case report of rare ciliopathy overlap; tracker maintenance only.
key_findings: Single case of segmental Caroli's disease in ADPKD
Identified incidentally on MRI volumetry
papers.clinical_implications: Reminder to consider biliary ciliopathy overlap when ADPKD imaging shows atypical hepatic findings.
papers.what_happened: Case report of a 40-year-old ADPKD patient with incidentally discovered segmental Caroli's disease.
papers.why_it_matters: Documents another rare ciliopathy phenotype overlap with ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case, no generalizable inference, not practice-changing.

papers.title: Wnts are endothelial cell-derived PKD1/PKD2-dependent autocrine/paracrine vasodilators
papers.abstract: bioRxiv preprint proposing that Wnts secreted from endothelial cells act as PKD1/PKD2-dependent autocrine/paracrine vasodilators. Suggests a mechanism whereby loss of polycystin-1/2 in endothelium contributes to vascular dysregulation in ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: Preprint proposing a vascular mechanism for ADPKD-related hypertension; not peer-reviewed.
key_findings: Endothelial PKD1/PKD2 may regulate Wnt-mediated vasodilation
Mechanism candidate for hypertension in ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: None today; mechanistic hypothesis for vascular dysregulation in ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: bioRxiv preprint proposes Wnts as PKD1/PKD2-dependent endothelial-derived vasodilators.
papers.why_it_matters: Could mechanistically connect polycystin function to ADPKD vascular dysregulation including hypertension.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, abstract not yet indexed, mechanism inferred from preclinical models.

papers.title: Tolvaptan Improves the Diurnal Blood Pressure Profile in Patients with Hypertension and Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Retrospective single-center pre/post study of 23 ADPKD patients with hypertension. After tolvaptan initiation, nocturnal systolic dipping increased 9.61%->14.0% and diastolic 10.48%->14.66%; non-dipper prevalence fell 57%->29%. Annual TKV growth fell 13.6%->1.61%; eGFR slope improved -4.46->-2.26 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr. No control arm.
papers.novelty_assessment: First focused report on diurnal BP effects of tolvaptan in ADPKD; hypothesis-generating only given uncontrolled pre/post design and small n=23.
key_findings: Non-dipper hypertension prevalence fell from 57% to 29% after tolvaptan initiation in n=23
Reported annual TKV growth dropped from 13.6% to 1.61% — magnitude implausibly large for a pre/post observational design and likely reflects regression to the mean and selection
Reported eGFR slope improved from -4.46 to -2.26 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr in the same cohort
papers.clinical_implications: Cannot inform practice; tolvaptan's BP effects warrant prospective controlled study before any inference about cardiovascular benefit.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective n=23 single-center pre/post study reports tolvaptan associated with improved nocturnal BP dipping and steep reductions in TKV growth and eGFR decline in ADPKD with hypertension.
papers.why_it_matters: Suggests tolvaptan may favorably alter circadian BP profile beyond known TKV effects, but the magnitude of TKV/eGFR changes is biologically implausible for an uncontrolled n=23 design.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-arm pre/post design with n=23, no control or comparator, surrogate endpoints only, and unrealistically large effect sizes consistent with regression to the mean and patient selection rather than pharmacological effect.

papers.title: Attribute-based cross-classification reveals sex- and age-specific prognostic impact of anemia in ADPKD.
papers.abstract: Single-center Japanese retrospective cohort of 552 ADPKD patients. Lower hemoglobin associated with worse renal outcome (>=30% eGFR decline or RRT); HR per 1 g/dL Hb increase = 0.83. Sex/age-stratified: anemia (Hb<13 g/dL) HR 2.92 (young men) and 3.84 (older men); women anemia (Hb<12 g/dL) HR ~2 in both age strata.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds sex- and age-stratified anemia signal to existing ADPKD prognostic literature; useful exploratory hypothesis but requires external replication.
key_findings: Lower Hb independently associated with >=30% eGFR decline or RRT (HR 0.83 per 1 g/dL increase)
Anemia confers larger relative risk in men than in women, with sex-specific Hb thresholds
Single-center Japanese cohort limits generalizability
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests anemia may carry sex-specific prognostic weight in ADPKD; insufficient to change Hb monitoring or treatment thresholds.
papers.what_happened: Single-center Japanese retrospective cohort of 552 ADPKD patients reports anemia is associated with kidney outcome decline, with sex- and age-specific risk patterns.
papers.why_it_matters: Sex-stratified anemia thresholds could refine ADPKD risk stratification if replicated, but observational design cannot establish causal benefit of anemia correction.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center retrospective cohort, no anemia treatment intervention, residual confounding (especially by underlying CKD severity) cannot be excluded, and Japanese-only population limits generalizability.

papers.title: Pregnancy complicated by left ventricular mural thrombus in a hypertensive patient with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and previous myocardial infarction.
papers.abstract: Case report of a multiparous woman in her late 30s with ADPKD, chronic hypertension, and prior anterior wall myocardial infarction who developed a left ventricular mural thrombus at 12 weeks' gestation. Managed with anticoagulation and pregnancy-adjusted antihypertensives; emergency C-section at 35 weeks for IUGR. Mother and infant did well.
papers.novelty_assessment: Single case description of a rare cardiovascular complication during pregnancy in ADPKD; illustrative only.
key_findings: Successful multidisciplinary management of LV mural thrombus in pregnancy with ADPKD comorbidity
Highlights need for individualized anticoagulation and BP control
papers.clinical_implications: Illustrative; no generalizable practice change.
papers.what_happened: Case report of pregnancy with LV mural thrombus in a woman with ADPKD, hypertension, and prior MI managed successfully with multidisciplinary care.
papers.why_it_matters: Illustrates the complexity of pregnancy in ADPKD with cardiovascular comorbidity but is n=1.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient case report with no comparator and no generalizable inference.

papers.title: International Society of Urological Pathology Consensus on Cancer Precursor Lesions: Working Group 3 Preneoplastic and Precursor Lesions of the Kidney.
papers.abstract: ISUP 2024 Florence consensus on renal precursor lesions. Proposes terms 'cyst with epithelial proliferation' for ACKD and 'papillary hyperplasia' for tufting of cyst lining in ADPKD. Mostly focused on papillary adenoma, VHL, and ACKD. ADPKD touched only briefly.
papers.novelty_assessment: ISUP consensus terminology likely to standardize pathology reports; ADPKD content limited to a nomenclature recommendation.
key_findings: Consensus introduces 'papillary hyperplasia' term for cyst-lining tufting in ADPKD
Document does not assert that ADPKD cyst-lining hyperplasia is a confirmed RCC precursor
papers.clinical_implications: May standardize pathology reporting language; no direct practice change for ADPKD nephrology.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Society consensus; sponsorship disclosures not in abstract

papers.what_happened: ISUP 2024 consensus working group publishes terminology for renal precursor lesions, including a recommended term 'papillary hyperplasia' for tufting of ADPKD cyst lining.
papers.why_it_matters: Pathology nomenclature standardization may improve consistency in describing ADPKD cyst-lining changes seen at nephrectomy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Document is consensus-based, mostly addresses non-ADPKD entities, and does not establish whether the proposed ADPKD lesion has malignant potential.

papers.title: ESKD from primary glomerulonephritis: Incidence and post KRT survival: A national cohort study in the UK.
papers.abstract: UK Renal Registry analysis of adults initiating KRT 1999-2019 with follow-up to 2021. ADPKD cohort (n=8,302) used as reference comparator vs primary glomerulonephritis (n=10,308). KRT incidence 9.8 (men) and 8.2 (women) pmp for ADPKD. Main analysis is about pGN, not ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: ADPKD here is a reference cohort, not the focus; provides updated UK incidence figures only.
key_findings: ADPKD KRT incidence ~9 pmp in UK over 1999-2019
Findings primarily inform pGN epidemiology, not ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: Useful descriptive epidemiology; does not change ADPKD management.
papers.what_happened: UK Renal Registry national cohort (1999-2019) reports ESKD incidence and post-KRT survival for primary glomerulonephritis using ADPKD as a reference disease cohort.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides updated UK background incidence figures for ADPKD-related KRT but the paper itself is not an ADPKD study.
papers.what_limits_confidence: ADPKD is only a comparator cohort; no ADPKD-specific outcomes, treatment, or genotype data are analyzed.

papers.title: TLR4 knockout ameliorates acute LPS-sensitized tolvaptan-induced idiosyncratic liver injury by disrupting drug metabolism, inflammation, and bile acid homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Preclinical TLR4 knockout mouse and primary hepatocyte study of LPS-sensitized tolvaptan-induced liver injury. TLR4-KO reversed CYP3A11 downregulation, normalized tolvaptan PK, attenuated transaminase elevation and histopathology, and reduced bile acid accumulation.
papers.novelty_assessment: Mechanistic preclinical work into tolvaptan idiosyncratic liver injury; novel pathway link but far from clinical translation.
key_findings: TLR4 knockout protected mice from LPS/tolvaptan-induced hepatotoxicity
Mechanism involves restoration of CYP3A11 and reduced bile acid accumulation
No human or in vivo translation
papers.clinical_implications: Mechanistic insight only; no near-term implication for tolvaptan monitoring.
papers.what_happened: Mouse and hepatocyte study reports TLR4 knockout reduces LPS-sensitized tolvaptan idiosyncratic liver injury via CYP3A11 restoration and bile acid normalization.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds candidate mechanism for tolvaptan idiosyncratic DILI, an open clinical safety question.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical mouse and in vitro only; LPS-sensitization model does not directly model human idiosyncratic DILI; no human data.

papers.title: Identification of Pathogenic PKHD1 Variants in Six Omani Families With Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: ARPKD (not ADPKD) case series of six Omani families with antenatal-diagnosed ARPKD and postnatal deaths. NGS+Sanger identified five distinct homozygous PKHD1 variants. ARPKD only.
papers.novelty_assessment: ARPKD-only paper; minimal direct relevance to ADPKD.
key_findings: Five homozygous PKHD1 variants identified in six Omani ARPKD families
All neonatal deaths
papers.clinical_implications: Local genetic counseling relevance only; not ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: ARPKD (not ADPKD) case series in six Omani families identifies five homozygous PKHD1 variants associated with neonatal demise.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds local PKHD1 variant data; ADPKD relevance is minimal.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Disease is ARPKD, not ADPKD; small case series with no functional validation.

papers.title: G-257 IFT140-Associated Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
papers.abstract: NKF SCM 2026 abstract on IFT140-associated ADPKD. Full abstract text not retrieved; AJKD supplement listing.
papers.novelty_assessment: Conference-abstract disclosure of IFT140-associated ADPKD case material; IFT140 is a known atypical ADPKD gene with a milder phenotype.
key_findings: Conference abstract listing on IFT140-associated ADPKD at NKF SCM 2026
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces awareness of IFT140 as an ADPKD gene; nothing actionable from a poster listing.
papers.what_happened: NKF SCM 2026 conference abstract describes IFT140-associated ADPKD; full content not yet retrieved.
papers.why_it_matters: IFT140 represents an atypical ADPKD genotype with implications for risk stratification and clinical recognition.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Conference abstract only with no methods, sample size, or full results available.

papers.title: G-294 Confounding of TKV-Based Prognosis in ADPKD by Unilateral Renal Artery Stenosis
papers.abstract: NKF SCM 2026 abstract noting that unilateral renal artery stenosis can confound TKV-based prognostication in ADPKD. Full abstract not retrieved.
papers.novelty_assessment: Useful clinical caveat about a recognized but underdiscussed source of TKV asymmetry; abstract-only.
key_findings: Conference abstract argues unilateral renal artery stenosis can distort TKV-based risk stratification in ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: Reasonable reminder for clinicians using Mayo Imaging Classification to consider RAS in asymmetric ADPKD; not yet evidence-based guidance.
papers.what_happened: Conference abstract observes that unilateral renal artery stenosis can confound TKV-based prognosis in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Mayo Imaging Classification depends on TKV; vascular asymmetry could mislead prognostication if unrecognized.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Conference abstract only; no cohort size, methods, or generalizability evidence available.

papers.title: Polycystin-1 Controls Cell Cycle Kinetics, Cell Cycle Exit, and Differentiation of Neural Progenitor Cells
papers.abstract: Cell-based loss-of-function study showing PC1 (and to lesser extent PC2) reduction lengthens S-phase and delays neuronal differentiation in neural progenitor cells. Authors suggest implications for ADPKD pathophysiology.
papers.novelty_assessment: Mechanistic in-vitro work in neural cells extends polycystin biology beyond kidney; clinical relevance for ADPKD is indirect.
key_findings: Reduced PC1 expression lengthens S-phase and delays neuronal differentiation in NPCs
Similar trend with PC2 reduction
papers.clinical_implications: Cell-biology insight; no near-term clinical implication.
papers.what_happened: In-vitro study reports that reducing polycystin-1 (and to lesser extent polycystin-2) lengthens S-phase and delays neuronal differentiation in neural progenitor cells.
papers.why_it_matters: Extends polycystin biology to non-renal cell-cycle regulation; may inform mechanism but not clinical practice.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cell-based loss-of-function study with no in vivo validation and only indirect ADPKD pathophysiology relevance.

papers.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA) of 8 studies (n=3,180): 1 RCT, 1 target trial emulation, 6 retrospective observational. SGLT2i associated with attenuated eGFR decline (pooled MD 1.344 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr; 95% CI 0.836-1.852) and Hb increase. Subgroup signal of larger eGFR benefit in non-diabetic ADPKD (not statistically significant). Authors note initial eGFR dip is class effect, supports prospective RCT.
papers.novelty_assessment: First published meta-analysis pooling SGLT2i evidence in ADPKD; signal direction consistent with SGLT2i biology in CKD broadly, but the underlying evidence base is dominated by retrospective observational data.
key_findings: Pooled eGFR decline attenuation 1.344 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr (8 studies, n=3,180)
Hemoglobin increased modestly with SGLT2i in ADPKD
Initial eGFR dip judged class-effect rather than ADPKD-specific harm
Greater non-diabetic eGFR benefit in subgroup analysis but not statistically significant
papers.clinical_implications: Strengthens the case for prospective RCTs in non-diabetic ADPKD (e.g., STOP-PKD, EMPA-PKD, Seliger feasibility); does not establish disease-modifying benefit and should not change practice yet.
papers.what_happened: Cureus meta-analysis pools 8 SGLT2i-in-ADPKD studies (1 RCT, 1 target trial emulation, 6 retrospective; n=3,180) and finds an associated attenuation of eGFR decline (pooled MD 1.34 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr) and modest Hb increase.
papers.why_it_matters: First quantitative synthesis of SGLT2i in ADPKD; supports prioritization of dedicated prospective RCTs (STOP-PKD, EMPA-PKD) and the hypothesis that SGLT2i are not harmful in non-diabetic ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Predominantly retrospective inputs, heterogeneity across designs and populations, surrogate eGFR slope endpoint, low-prestige journal (Cureus), and no patient-important outcomes — practice should still await ongoing RCTs.

papers.title: Development and Validation of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Kidney Failure in Early Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: CRISP/HALT-A development cohort (n=759, baseline eGFR 91 mL/min/1.73 m2, median 10.2y FU); externally validated in Mayo registry (ADPKD ages 15-49, eGFR>=60). Cox prognostic models for kidney failure (eGFR<15, dialysis, transplant) using age, sex, eGFR, ADPKD genotype, and Mayo Imaging Class. Risk predictions had good discrimination and calibration over a 15-year horizon.
papers.novelty_assessment: Largest, externally-validated multivariable prediction model for kidney failure in early ADPKD; extends Mayo Imaging Class with routine clinical inputs.
key_findings: Development cohort n=759 with median 10.2y follow-up; outcome was eGFR<15, dialysis, or transplant
Predictors include age, sex, eGFR, ADPKD genotype, and Mayo Imaging Class
Good discrimination and calibration for kidney failure over 15-year horizon
External Mayo validation supports generalizability in early-stage ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: If discrimination/calibration metrics translate, this could inform tolvaptan eligibility, trial enrichment, and patient counseling beyond Mayo Imaging Class alone — particularly in early-stage ADPKD where risk stratification is currently weakest.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Some authors with industry ties (Otsuka, Sanofi) common in ADPKD literature; not reviewed in detail

papers.what_happened: JASN reports a multivariable Cox prediction model for kidney failure in early ADPKD developed in CRISP+HALT-A (n=759, median 10.2y FU) and externally validated in the Mayo registry, using age, sex, eGFR, ADPKD genotype, and Mayo Imaging Class.
papers.why_it_matters: Improving early risk prediction in ADPKD is a long-standing unmet need for tolvaptan eligibility, trial enrichment, and counseling; this is the largest, externally-validated effort to combine routine clinical data with Mayo Imaging Class for the patient-important outcome of kidney failure.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Observational design with no intervention arm; external validation cohort restricted to ages 15-49 with preserved eGFR; clinical impact requires prospective use and recalibration in non-Caucasian and non-research populations.

papers.title: Improving Early Risk Prediction for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: (Editorial accompanying the Ravichandran et al. multivariable prediction model in early ADPKD; full text not available in NLM abstract feed.)
papers.novelty_assessment: Editorial commentary on Ravichandran et al.; useful contextual framing but not new evidence.
key_findings: Editorial commentary; no new data
papers.clinical_implications: Reading-list companion to the Ravichandran model paper.
papers.what_happened: JASN editorial commentary accompanying the Ravichandran et al. multivariable prediction model paper.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides editor framing for the new prediction model; useful as a reading companion.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Editorial only; no original data; abstract not provided in PubMed feed.

papers.title: Automatically Measuring Kidney, Liver, and Cyst Volumes in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: TraceOrg, a web-based 3D U-Net+transformer deep-learning tool, automatically segments kidneys, liver, and cysts on MRI/CT in ADPKD and outputs volumes plus Mayo Imaging Class. Trained on 611 ADPKD scans and 109 controls; externally validated on CRISP and PKD-RRC datasets; available at www.traceorg.com.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds an externally-validated, web-based automated TKV/cyst tool that handles multiple pulse sequences and outputs Mayo Imaging Class — incremental but practically useful.
key_findings: Hybrid 3D U-Net + transformer model trained on 611 ADPKD + 109 control MRI/CT
External validation on CRISP, PKD-RRC, and other external datasets
Web tool reports kidney/liver/cyst volumes and Mayo Imaging Classification
Browser-side DICOM anonymization for privacy
papers.clinical_implications: Reduces friction of TKV measurement in clinics without local PACS-integrated tools; could broaden access to Mayo Imaging Classification for tolvaptan eligibility decisions.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Cornell ADPKD imaging group; tool hosted at traceorg.com (academic)

papers.what_happened: JASN publishes TraceOrg, an externally-validated web-based deep-learning tool that automatically segments and reports ADPKD kidney/liver/cyst volumes plus Mayo Imaging Class.
papers.why_it_matters: TKV measurement is a documented bottleneck for ADPKD risk stratification and tolvaptan eligibility; an open, web-accessible automated tool lowers that barrier.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Methods paper without prospective clinical impact data; agreement against expert manual segmentation is what's measured, not downstream patient outcomes; long-term reproducibility under varied scanner protocols still to be confirmed in routine use.

papers.title: KDIGO 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline for ADPKD: a commentary on intracranial aneurysms and other vascular manifestations from the ERA Working Group Genes & Kidney.
papers.abstract: ERA Working Group Genes & Kidney commentary on the 2025 KDIGO ADPKD guideline focused on intracranial aneurysms (ICAs) and other vascular manifestations. Restates 4-5x increased ICA risk (~12.9% prevalence) but low absolute rupture rate (0.57/1000 person-years), supports risk-stratified screening centered on family history, smoking, and BP control, contrast-free MRA as preferred modality, and 5-10 year rescreening in high-risk individuals. Highlights thoracic aortic aneurysm association warranting family screening; abdominal aortic aneurysms not increased.
papers.novelty_assessment: European commentary on KDIGO 2025 ICA section; consolidates rather than changes guidance, but is the first formal regional reading and implementation framing.
key_findings: Endorses risk-stratified ICA screening based on family history of ICA/SAH/sudden death, smoking, and BP control
Contrast-free MRA preferred imaging modality
5-10 year rescreening in high-risk individuals with negative initial scan
Thoracic aortic aneurysm clearly associated with ADPKD; family screening warranted
Abdominal aortic aneurysm not increased in ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces selective rather than universal ICA screening in ADPKD; clarifies thoracic vs abdominal aortic aneurysm distinction for clinic counseling; should help align European centers with KDIGO 2025.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: ERA working group; not detailed in abstract

papers.what_happened: ERA Working Group Genes & Kidney issues a NDT commentary on the KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline section addressing intracranial aneurysms and other vascular manifestations.
papers.why_it_matters: ICA screening practice in ADPKD remains heterogeneous in Europe; a regional commentary on KDIGO supports more uniform risk-stratified, contrast-free MRA screening and clarifies aortic aneurysm screening.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Commentary on existing guideline rather than new data; prevalence and rupture-rate estimates inherit limitations of underlying observational literature.

papers.title: Integrin α1β1 Promotes Interstitial Fibrosis and Cyst Growth in a Mouse Model of Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: Multiomic analysis of Pkd1nl/nl mouse and human ADPKD tissue showed upregulation of integrin α1; global Itga1 knockout in Pkd1nl/nl mice reduced kidney cyst size and preserved kidney function, with reduced interstitial fibrosis attributed to lower fibroblast proliferation.
papers.novelty_assessment: Identifies integrin α1β1 as a fibrosis/cyst-growth modifier in a slow ADPKD mouse model; potential drug target but early-stage.
key_findings: Itga1 KO reduces cyst size and preserves function in Pkd1nl/nl mice
ITGA1 upregulated in human ADPKD tissue scRNA datasets
papers.clinical_implications: Adds integrin α1β1 to the list of fibrosis-related ADPKD targets; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation has historically been weak.
papers.what_happened: JASN reports that genetic deletion of integrin α1 reduces cyst size, preserves kidney function, and lowers interstitial fibrosis in the Pkd1nl/nl ADPKD mouse model.
papers.why_it_matters: Suggests integrin α1β1 as a potential anti-fibrotic target in ADPKD distinct from cyst-fluid secretion pathways.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse genetic deletion only; no pharmacological inhibitor tested; ADPKD preclinical models have a poor translation track record.

papers.title: α-Klotho Promotes Cell Death and Suppresses Inflammation through TNF-Cellular Inhibitor of Apoptosis Protein 1 Signaling in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: Soluble serum α-Klotho lower in ADPKD patients. Transgenic α-Klotho and recombinant α-Klotho delayed cyst growth in Pkd1 mutant mice via cIAP1 destabilization, increasing apoptosis of cystic epithelium and reducing inflammation.
papers.novelty_assessment: Mechanistic mouse data adding α-Klotho to ADPKD anti-cystogenic candidate list; clinically remote.
key_findings: Transgenic and recombinant α-Klotho delay cyst growth in Pkd1 mutant mice
Mechanism via cIAP1 destabilization, increasing apoptosis
papers.clinical_implications: Potential biomarker and target rationale for α-Klotho in ADPKD; far from clinical translation.
papers.what_happened: JASN reports that transgenic and recombinant α-Klotho delay cyst growth in Pkd1 mutant mice through TNF-cIAP1 signaling, with serum α-Klotho lower in ADPKD patients.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds α-Klotho to the candidate list of anti-cystogenic mechanisms and biomarkers in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse-only mechanistic study; no human intervention; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation has been historically weak.

papers.title: A Ciliary Phosphoinositide Pathway Regulates the Dosage of Polycystins in Primary Cilia.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: INPP5E and PIPKIγ coordinate PI4P/PI(4,5)P2 homeostasis in primary cilia; modulating their activity changes PC1 and PC2 levels in cilia. INPP5E inhibition increased the hypomorphic PC1-R3277C variant in cilia and reduced cystogenesis in vitro.
papers.novelty_assessment: New mechanistic angle for boosting ciliary polycystin dosage in hypomorphic variants; conceptually aligned with Vertex/PYC chaperone/dosage strategies.
key_findings: INPP5E and PIPKIγ regulate ciliary PI4P/PI(4,5)P2 balance
Modulating these enzymes changes PC1/PC2 ciliary levels
INPP5E inhibition rescued PC1-R3277C ciliary localization and reduced cystogenesis in 3D Matrigel models
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces 'rescue PC1 dosage' as a tractable strategy; orthogonal to Vertex VX-407 corrector approach but in vitro only.
papers.what_happened: JASN reports a phosphoinositide-based ciliary mechanism (INPP5E, PIPKIγ) that regulates polycystin levels in cilia; INPP5E inhibition rescued PC1-R3277C and reduced cystogenesis in vitro.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a druggable lever for boosting ciliary polycystin dosage in hypomorphic PKD1 variants, complementary to chaperone/corrector strategies (Vertex VX-407, PYC-003).
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro only; no animal or human data; clinical translation from ciliary biology to ADPKD therapy has been slow.

papers.title: Evolving Understanding of RNA Biology in Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: (Narrative review on RNA biology relevant to kidney disease; ADPKD discussed in context of antisense oligonucleotides, miRNA inhibitors, and gene-dosage modulation. Abstract not provided in NLM feed.)
papers.novelty_assessment: Narrative review; useful synthesis but no new data.
key_findings: Narrative review only
papers.clinical_implications: Background reading for the ADPKD RNA-therapeutics pipeline.
papers.what_happened: JASN review on RNA biology in kidney disease, including ADPKD-relevant ASO and miRNA approaches.
papers.why_it_matters: Useful background for the farabursen / RGLS4326 / RGLS8429 ADPKD RNA pipeline.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review; no new evidence; full text not available in feed.

papers.title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease Clinical Trial Simulator: Case Reports of Model-Informed Drug Development.
papers.abstract: Web-based clinical trial simulation tool for ADTKD (UMOD/MUC1 variants) using Wake Forest natural history data. Not ADPKD; tracked because of methodological relevance to surrogate endpoints in slowly progressive monogenic kidney disease.
papers.novelty_assessment: Methodologically interesting trial simulation framework; ADTKD not ADPKD — included for taxonomy completeness.
key_findings: NLME models for UMOD/MUC1 eGFR decline drive a CTS tool at app.cop.ufl.edu/adtkd/
papers.clinical_implications: Demonstrates how natural-history-based simulation can support trial design for ultra-rare slowly progressive kidney diseases; transferable framing for sub-ADPKD genotype trials.
papers.what_happened: CPT:PSP publishes an open ADTKD clinical trial simulation tool built on Wake Forest natural history data for UMOD and MUC1 variants.
papers.why_it_matters: Not ADPKD — but a methodologic blueprint for natural-history-driven trial design in slowly progressive monogenic kidney disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: ADTKD, not ADPKD; tracked here only for taxonomy completeness.

papers.title: From data to drug: the translational impact of RaDaR, the UK national registry of rare kidney diseases.
papers.abstract: Review of the UK National Registry of Rare Kidney Diseases (RaDaR; >37,000 participants, 100+ UK sites): epidemiology, surrogate endpoints, biomarker/genomic research, trial feasibility, NICE appraisals. ADPKD covered as one of the major rare kidney diseases tracked; surrogate endpoint validation work has supported regulatory acceptance.
papers.novelty_assessment: Review of an existing registry; useful framing for how UK trial infrastructure feeds ADPKD pipeline data (Marshall, McFarlane-style real-world tolvaptan analyses).
key_findings: RaDaR has >37,000 participants across 100+ UK sites
Has supported proteinuria as a surrogate endpoint for IgA nephropathy regulatory approval
Used in NICE appraisals and as trial recruitment pipeline
papers.clinical_implications: Explains the infrastructure behind UK ADPKD real-world tolvaptan analyses; relevant for interpreting future UK ADPKD trial readouts.
papers.what_happened: NDT review of the UK RaDaR rare kidney disease registry, summarizing its scope, infrastructure, and translational impact through 2026.
papers.why_it_matters: RaDaR underlies multiple ADPKD UK real-world studies (Marshall tolvaptan, KDIGO surrogate work) and signals the maturity of UK trial infrastructure for rare kidney disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review; ADPKD not the central focus; written by registry-affiliated authors.

papers.title: Disruption of the human cystin-1 myristoyl-electrostatic switch causes polycystic kidney disease that phenocopies autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Two families with CYS1 variants (a 24-kb deletion encompassing the regulatory region+exon 1; and a homozygous c.4G>A p.Gly2Ser disrupting N-terminal myristoylation) presented with ARPKD-like kidney disease. Functional studies show the variant disrupts a conserved myristoyl-electrostatic switch regulated by Ser-17 phosphorylation, impacting subcellular localization, ciliary trafficking, and cAMP-driven cystogenesis.
papers.novelty_assessment: Confirms CYS1 as a human polycystic kidney disease gene; phenocopies ARPKD rather than ADPKD — peripheral to typical ADPKD.
key_findings: Two unrelated families with CYS1 disruption produce ARPKD-like phenotype
Myristoyl-electrostatic switch regulated by Ser-17 phosphorylation governs ciliary trafficking
papers.clinical_implications: Genetic counseling implication: include CYS1 in panels for ARPKD-like presentations without PKHD1 variant.
papers.what_happened: KI publishes two-family genotype-phenotype + functional study showing that CYS1 variants disrupting an N-terminal myristoyl-electrostatic switch produce ARPKD-like kidney disease in humans.
papers.why_it_matters: Confirms CYS1 as a rare cause of polycystic kidney disease and clarifies functional pathway (ciliary trafficking via myristoylation switch).
papers.what_limits_confidence: ARPKD-like phenotype, not ADPKD; only two families; mostly genetic counseling implication for unsolved ARPKD-like cases.

papers.title: Genetic analysis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in Iranian families: a combined Sanger and next-generation sequencing study.
papers.abstract: 18 Iranian ADPKD families analyzed by Sanger + NGS panel + WES. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 13/18 families (72.2%): 9 PKD1, 4 PKD2; five novel variants; one PKD1 frameshift identified by WES after Sanger missed it (allelic dropout).
papers.novelty_assessment: Small ethnic-cohort genetic analysis; expands the variant spectrum but methodologically routine.
key_findings: 13/18 (72.2%) Iranian ADPKD families had pathogenic/likely pathogenic PKD1/PKD2 variants
Five novel variants identified
WES rescued one Sanger-missed PKD1 frameshift
papers.clinical_implications: Adds variants to the curated PKD1/PKD2 spectrum; reinforces NGS+WES superiority over Sanger alone.
papers.what_happened: J Appl Genet reports a small Iranian ADPKD genetic study (n=18 families) using Sanger + NGS panel + WES, finding 72.2% diagnostic yield and 5 novel PKD1/PKD2 variants.
papers.why_it_matters: Expands geographic representation in PKD1/PKD2 variant catalogs and reaffirms NGS sensitivity over Sanger.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Very small cohort (n=18 families); methodological replication of established findings.

papers.title: Carbon dioxide contrast angiography- and computed tomography-guided percutaneous embolization of the renal allograft artery in a patient with graft intolerance syndrome and iodinated contrast allergy: a case report.
papers.abstract: Case report: 66yo woman with ADPKD post-LDKT developed graft intolerance syndrome with iodinated contrast allergy; treated with percutaneous renal allograft artery embolization using CO2 angiography + CT guidance. ADPKD is incidental.
papers.novelty_assessment: Case report; ADPKD incidental.
key_findings: Single-case CO2-guided embolization
papers.clinical_implications: Procedural option in patients with iodinated contrast allergy; not ADPKD-specific.
papers.what_happened: CEN Case Reports describes CO2-guided embolization for graft intolerance syndrome in a post-transplant ADPKD patient with iodinated contrast allergy.
papers.why_it_matters: Procedural-technique case; ADPKD only incidentally.
papers.what_limits_confidence: N=1 case report; ADPKD incidental.

papers.title: Optimizing Next Generation Sequencing for Genetic Diagnosis in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Exome sequencing on 203 ADPKD patients (171 families) from CRISP with prior 'gold-standard' results (n=157 PKD1, n=27 PKD2, n=19 unsolved). Optimized ES detected 95.5% of defined PKD1 pathogenic variants and all PKD2 variants; standard pipelines miss ≥22 PKD1 variants (GATK HardFiltering / pseudogene alignment); higher-depth ES achieves 100% PKD1 detection; GS solved a balanced translocation. ES+GS solved 96% of well-phenotyped ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: Stronger evidence base for NGS-as-replacement-for-Sanger in ADPKD; identifies specific pipeline pitfalls (HardFiltering, pseudogene alignment) and quantifies higher-depth ES gain.
key_findings: Optimized ES detects 95.5% of PKD1 pathogenic variants and 100% of PKD2 variants
Standard pipelines miss ≥22 PKD1 variants due to GATK HardFiltering and pseudogene alignment
Higher-depth ES achieves 100% PKD1 detection
ES+GS solves 96% of well-phenotyped ADPKD cases
GS identified a balanced translocation t(1;16)(q31.1;p13.3)
papers.clinical_implications: Practical playbook for diagnostic labs replacing Sanger with NGS for ADPKD; quantifies pseudogene-handling pipeline impact.
papers.what_happened: Genetics in Medicine reports an optimized exome+genome sequencing pipeline for ADPKD on 203 CRISP patients, detecting 95.5% of PKD1 and 100% of PKD2 variants and quantifying standard-pipeline failure modes.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete NGS playbook (depth, pseudogene alignment, GS rescue) that diagnostic labs can adopt to replace Sanger long-range PCR for ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single research cohort with prior gold-standard genotypes; not a prospective real-world diagnostic comparison; surfaced this week but published Feb 2026.

papers.title: The Importance of Molecular Testing in the Diagnosis of Genetic Syndromes with Chronic Kidney Disease: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations.
papers.abstract: Targeted gene panels + WES in 10 patients with suspected genetic syndromic CKD: 3 PKD1, 1 PKD2, 4 Alport, 1 MODY5/HNF1B, 1 Bartter type 1. Genotype-phenotype correlations described.
papers.novelty_assessment: Very small case series across mixed genetic kidney disease; minimal ADPKD-specific contribution.
key_findings: 10-patient mixed-genotype case series; 4/10 had PKD1/PKD2 variants
papers.clinical_implications: Anecdotal reinforcement of NGS-based testing in syndromic CKD.
papers.what_happened: IJMS reports a 10-patient mixed-genotype case series of genetic syndromic CKD diagnosed by panel+WES, including 4 ADPKD cases.
papers.why_it_matters: Anecdotal support for NGS-based testing in syndromic CKD; minimal ADPKD-specific learning.
papers.what_limits_confidence: N=10 mixed-genotype case series; predominantly known variants; ADPKD not the focus.

papers.title: ALG8-Driven Metabolic Reprogramming in Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Synthesis of Evidence Linking Glycosylation Defects to Metabolic Signaling.
papers.abstract: Narrative synthesis arguing ALG8 (ER glycosyltransferase) is a metabolic checkpoint in ADPKD: population data show ALG8 variant enrichment in ADPKD (OR 9.75); ALG8 LOF interacts with PKD1; glycosylation defects disrupt PC1 trafficking and shift metabolism toward Warburg-like aerobic glycolysis. Chemical chaperones and glycosylation inhibitors suppressed cysts in ALG8/PKD1-deficient organoids.
papers.novelty_assessment: Synthesis review framing ALG8 as a druggable metabolic checkpoint; mechanistically appealing but extrapolation to clinical ADPKD remains speculative.
key_findings: ALG8 variant enrichment in ADPKD cohorts (OR 9.75)
ALG8 LOF + PKD1 interaction accelerates cystogenesis
Chemical chaperones / glycosylation inhibitors suppress cysts in ALG8/PKD1 organoids
papers.clinical_implications: Adds ALG8/glycosylation+chemical chaperones to the candidate list of mechanistic targets, alongside PYC-003 and Vertex VX-407 corrector strategies; clinically remote.
papers.what_happened: IUBMB Life narrative synthesis frames ALG8/glycosylation defects as a metabolic checkpoint in ADPKD with chemical chaperone implications.
papers.why_it_matters: Mechanistic rationale aligning with chaperone/corrector therapeutic strategies for ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Review article with mechanistic extrapolation; cancer-metabolism analogies are speculative; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation has been weak.

papers.title: Improving Risk Prediction in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
papers.abstract: (KI Reports editorial / commentary on improving ADPKD risk prediction; abstract not available via API.)
papers.novelty_assessment: Editorial commentary on KI Reports TKV+KFRE validation paper; useful framing but not new evidence.
key_findings: Editorial only
papers.clinical_implications: Reading-list companion to the TKV+KFRE validation paper.
papers.what_happened: KI Reports editorial on improving ADPKD risk prediction, accompanying the TKV+KFRE validation paper.
papers.why_it_matters: Frames the practical question of how clinicians should use TKV/KFRE/eGFR together for risk stratification.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Editorial only; no original data; abstract not retrievable.

papers.title: Validation of Combining Total Kidney Volume and Kidney Failure Risk Equation in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract: Retrospective observational study of adults with ADPKD with ≥1 CT/MRI-derived TKV between Jan 2015 and Jan 2023. In the eGFR<60 subgroup, an adjusted model combining age, sex, tolvaptan, KFRE, and Mayo Imaging Class achieved best performance (AIC 631, ΔC-statistic 0.47/0.28/0.27 at 1/3/5y) for the composite of KRT initiation or 40% eGFR decline; combinations of MIC+KFRE and KFRE alone closely followed. Conclusion: KFRE adds to MIC for risk prediction in ADPKD with eGFR<60.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds KFRE on top of Mayo Imaging Class for ADPKD risk prediction in eGFR<60; useful but observational and limited to advanced disease subgroup.
key_findings: Retrospective ADPKD cohort with CT/MRI TKV (2015-2023)
In eGFR<60 group, adding KFRE to Mayo Imaging Class improved risk prediction (ΔC up to 0.47 at 1y)
Composite outcome was KRT initiation or 40% eGFR decline
papers.clinical_implications: Supports using MIC + KFRE together for risk prediction in ADPKD eGFR<60; complements Ravichandran et al. JASN model in earlier disease.
papers.what_happened: KI Reports observational study validates that adding KFRE to Mayo Imaging Class improves risk prediction (KRT initiation or 40% eGFR decline) in ADPKD patients with eGFR<60.
papers.why_it_matters: KFRE is widely available; layering it on top of Mayo Imaging Class for advanced ADPKD adds practical risk-stratification value at minimal cost.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center retrospective; primary analysis confined to eGFR<60 subgroup; not new this week (March 2026 publication, surfaced now).

papers.title: Miniaturization of CRISPRa plasmids for efficient delivery into renal epithelial cells and Pkd1 transactivation.
papers.abstract: Type IIS-restriction-enzyme one-pot method shrinks CRISPRa plasmids from 9-11 kb to ~6 kb, raising nucleofection efficiency in Pkd1RC/- cells from 16% to 54% and in primary Pkd1RC/Cond;Pkhd1Cre+ cells from 10% to 31%. The mini-CRISPRa vector with Pkd1-targeting sgRNAs upregulated endogenous Pkd1 4.1-fold (p<0.001) in Pkd1RC/- cells and 2.9-fold (p<0.001) in primary cells versus non-targeting controls.
papers.novelty_assessment: New delivery-engineering approach to overcome size-related uptake barriers for CRISPRa-based PKD1 transactivation; relevant to the broader corrector / dosage-restoration strategy alongside PYC-003 and VX-407.
key_findings: Miniaturization of CRISPRa plasmid (~6 kb) substantially raises transfection efficiency in mouse PKD1 cell models
Mini-CRISPRa with Pkd1-targeting sgRNAs upregulated endogenous Pkd1 ~4-fold in Pkd1RC/- cells
~3-fold endogenous Pkd1 upregulation also achieved in primary Pkd1RC/Cond;Pkhd1Cre+ epithelial cells
papers.clinical_implications: Methods advance only; no in vivo data and no clinical readout. Expands tooling for laboratories pursuing PKD1 dosage restoration.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated; academic group (KU Med Center)

papers.what_happened: Mol Biol Reports paper describes a one-pot method to miniaturize CRISPRa plasmids and shows improved nucleofection efficiency plus endogenous Pkd1 upregulation in Pkd1-mutant mouse kidney cells.
papers.why_it_matters: Plasmid size has been a delivery bottleneck for CRISPRa-based PKD1 dosage restoration; smaller vectors transfect primary cells more efficiently, supporting downstream preclinical work.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In-vitro mouse kidney cells only; no in vivo cyst readout, no human cells, no comparison with viral or LNP delivery, and ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation track record.

papers.title: Pathophysiological significance of cholesterol in ciliopathies.
papers.abstract: Narrative review proposes ciliary cholesterol insufficiency as a unifying pathological mechanism in ciliopathies, including ADPKD. Notes that the polycystin complex localizes to ciliary membranes in a cholesterol-dependent manner and that PC2 has specific cholesterol-binding sites disrupted by pathogenic mutations. Discusses Smith-Lemli-Opitz, Zellweger, and broader ciliopathy contexts and speculates about cholesterol-targeted therapeutic opportunities.
papers.novelty_assessment: Niche narrative review reframing ciliopathies through cholesterol biology; ADPKD content is a small subsection.
key_findings: PC2 contains cholesterol-binding sites that ADPKD-pathogenic mutations may disrupt
Ciliary cholesterol enrichment is required for normal GPCR/ion-channel function in cilia
papers.clinical_implications: No actionable clinical implication; speculative therapeutic angle.
papers.what_happened: Fujita Medical Journal narrative review summarizes evidence linking ciliary cholesterol biology to ciliopathies, including ADPKD via PC2 cholesterol-binding sites.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds mechanistic context for cholesterol-PC2 interactions and ciliary lipid biology relevant to ADPKD pathogenesis.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review without original data; regional journal; speculative therapeutic implications.

papers.title: A patient with aortic dilation and polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Brief Kidney International clinical/teaching item describing an ADPKD patient with concurrent aortic dilation. Full abstract not provided in PubMed.

key_findings: Single-patient ADPKD case with aortic dilation reported as a brief KI clinical item
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces awareness of vascular phenotype in ADPKD; not practice-changing.
papers.what_happened: Kidney International published a brief clinical item describing an ADPKD patient with aortic dilation.
papers.why_it_matters: Reinforces awareness of vascular involvement in ADPKD; aligns with ongoing KDIGO 2025 vascular/ICA discussion.
papers.what_limits_confidence: n=1 teaching item, no abstract content available in PubMed, no controlled comparison.

papers.title: TLR2 Activation Enhances Inflammatory Signaling and Accelerates Cyst Growth and Renal Fibrosis in Polycystic Kidney Disease Mice
papers.abstract: Pkd1 deletion increased TLR2 and MyD88 mRNA in renal epithelial cells. In Pkd1RC/RC mice, the synthetic TLR2 agonist Pam3CSK4 amplified pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses, NF-κB activation in cyst-lining epithelial cells, mTOR signaling, and c-Myc/Wnt protein upregulation, accelerating cyst expansion and fibrosis. Endogenous TLR2 ligands decorin and biglycan were elevated in human PKD kidneys.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds TLR2-driven innate immunity to the inflammation/fibrosis target list in ADPKD; agonist-driven mouse experiment with limited human relevance.
key_findings: Pkd1 deletion upregulates TLR2/MyD88 in renal epithelial cells
TLR2 agonist Pam3CSK4 accelerates cyst growth and fibrosis in Pkd1RC/RC mice
Endogenous TLR2 ligands decorin and biglycan are elevated in human PKD kidneys
papers.clinical_implications: Hypothesis-generating only; suggests TLR2/innate immunity may be a target in ADPKD but no antagonist study or clinical translation.
papers.what_happened: IJMS preclinical study reports that TLR2 agonist accelerates cyst growth and renal fibrosis in Pkd1RC/RC mice, with elevated endogenous TLR2 ligands in human PKD tissue.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds TLR2/innate-immunity to the ADPKD inflammation-fibrosis pathway map and suggests a potential therapeutic axis.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse model only, agonist-driven (no TLR2-antagonist intervention shown), human data limited to descriptive ligand measurements; ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: miR-25-3p promotes proliferation and inhibits autophagy of renal cells in polycystic kidney mice by regulating ATG14-Beclin 1.
papers.abstract: Retraction notice for Ren Fail 2020 Nov;42(1):333-342 (PMID 32340512), which had reported that miR-25-3p promotes renal cell proliferation and inhibits autophagy via ATG14-Beclin 1 in a polycystic kidney mouse model.
papers.novelty_assessment: Retraction notice; not new science.
key_findings: Original 2020 paper retracted by Renal Failure
papers.clinical_implications: None — retraction notice removes a hypothesis-generating preclinical PKD paper from the literature.
papers.what_happened: Renal Failure published a retraction notice on 6 May 2026 for a 2020 paper claiming miR-25-3p promotes cyst-related renal cell proliferation and inhibits autophagy.
papers.why_it_matters: Removes a previously hypothesis-generating miRNA mechanism paper from the PKD literature.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retraction notice provides no new data; underlying ADPKD relevance of the original paper was modest (mouse cystic model with broad mechanism claims).

papers.title: Endocannabinoid System-Related Inflammation and Progression of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract: Case-control study (60 ADPKD adults, 45 healthy volunteers) measuring plasma anandamide (AEA), 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), TNF-α and IL-6 from a single venous draw. ADPKD patients had significantly lower AEA and 2-AG (p<0.001) and significantly higher IL-6 (p<0.001); TNF-α was nominally higher but not significant. Inflammatory markers correlated with endocannabinoid concentrations and renal function indices. Authors conclude the endocannabinoid system may modulate inflammation in ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: First clinical observational dataset on plasma endocannabinoids in ADPKD; complements concurrent preclinical Betkar/Tam Mol Med work on CB1R in ADPKD models.
key_findings: ADPKD patients (n=60) had significantly lower plasma AEA and 2-AG than healthy controls (n=45)
IL-6 was significantly higher in ADPKD vs controls (p<0.001); TNF-α difference was not significant
Endocannabinoid concentrations correlated with renal function indices in cross-section
papers.clinical_implications: None — cross-sectional associations only; no intervention, no longitudinal progression data.
papers.what_happened: A Polish single-center case-control study (60 ADPKD vs 45 controls) reports lower plasma AEA and 2-AG and higher IL-6 in ADPKD, with cross-sectional correlations to renal function.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds clinical evidence to the emerging hypothesis that endocannabinoid signaling and inflammation are linked in ADPKD, complementing recent preclinical CB1R work.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional, single-center, modest n; no longitudinal eGFR/TKV outcomes; plasma rather than tissue measurements; cannot establish direction of causation.

papers.title: Progressive endocannabinoid system dysregulation in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Translational study analyzing public human ADPKD kidney transcriptomic data and complementary mouse-model and cell experiments to characterize the endocannabinoid system (ECS), particularly CB1R, in ADPKD progression. Authors report progressive ECS dysregulation tracking with disease severity, with implications for CB1R as a candidate metabolic-inflammatory target.
papers.novelty_assessment: Provides preclinical scaffolding for the broader hypothesis that endocannabinoid signaling drives ADPKD progression; adds to a small but growing literature.
key_findings: ECS-related gene expression is progressively dysregulated across ADPKD severity in human transcriptomic data
CB1R signaling is implicated in inflammatory and metabolic features of ADPKD models
papers.clinical_implications: None — preclinical/translational hypothesis; CB1R inhibitors not in ADPKD clinical development.
papers.what_happened: Mol Med translational paper combining transcriptomic and model evidence reports progressive endocannabinoid system dysregulation in ADPKD with CB1R implicated in disease-related inflammatory/metabolic pathways.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides mechanistic scaffolding aligned with a recent clinical case-control study (Simankowicz IJMS 2026) finding altered plasma endocannabinoids in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mostly bioinformatic and preclinical readouts; no human interventional data; ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation history.

papers.title: P615: Solving the unsolved: HiFi long-read sequencing reveals hidden structural variants in ADPKD
papers.abstract: Conference abstract (NKF/ACMG context) describing application of PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing to ADPKD patients with previously unresolved diagnoses, reporting recovery of hidden structural variants in PKD1/PKD2. No abstract text available in indexed metadata.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds to a Yale group's published work on long-read sequencing for ADPKD diagnostic optimization; complements pm_41653026 (NGS optimization) and recent Reproductive Medicine and Biology long-read CAH/ADPKD work.
key_findings: HiFi long-read sequencing recovers ADPKD-causing structural variants missed by short-read NGS in unresolved cases (per abstract framing)
papers.clinical_implications: Could improve genetic diagnosis yield in ADPKD families with negative short-read NGS; methods/yield unspecified in abstract.
papers.what_happened: Conference abstract from the Somlo/Besse Yale group reporting that PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing recovers hidden structural variants in PKD1/PKD2 in previously unsolved ADPKD cases.
papers.why_it_matters: If validated, could meaningfully improve molecular diagnosis yield in genetically unsolved ADPKD families.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Conference abstract only — no n, no methods, no diagnostic-yield statistics, no peer-reviewed report.

papers.title: LB-22 Metastatic Cystic Papillary Renal Cell Carcinoma Mimicking Polycystic Disease
papers.abstract: NKF SCM 2026 late-breaking case abstract describing metastatic cystic papillary renal cell carcinoma initially mimicking polycystic kidney disease on imaging. No data available.
