key_findings: Cystic papillary RCC can mimic polycystic disease imaging; diagnostic pitfall
papers.clinical_implications: Reminder for nephrologists/radiologists that cystic RCC can mimic PKD on imaging; case-level evidence only.
papers.what_happened: NKF SCM 2026 late-breaking case abstract on metastatic cystic papillary RCC initially mimicking polycystic disease.
papers.why_it_matters: Underlines a known diagnostic pitfall when imaging shows atypical or unilateral cystic patterns.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient case abstract with no full methods.

papers.title: G-529 Concurrent Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis and Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Complex Diagnostic Challenge
papers.abstract: NKF SCM 2026 case abstract on a patient with concurrent hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis and polycystic kidney disease, framed as a diagnostic challenge.
papers.novelty_assessment: Conference case abstract; minimal scientific novelty.
key_findings: Concurrent hATTR and PKD increases diagnostic complexity (case)
papers.clinical_implications: Anecdotal teaching point; not actionable beyond awareness.
papers.what_happened: NKF SCM 2026 case abstract on concurrent hereditary ATTR amyloidosis and polycystic kidney disease.
papers.why_it_matters: Highlights diagnostic complexity when systemic amyloidosis coexists with cystic kidney disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient case abstract with no methods or follow-up.

papers.title: G-524 Synergistic Pathogenicity in Adult Polycystic Kidney Disease: An Index Case Report of Two Concurrent Mutations
papers.abstract: NKF SCM 2026 case abstract reporting an adult PKD index case carrying two concurrent pathogenic variants and proposing synergistic pathogenicity. No data table.
papers.novelty_assessment: Conference case abstract; consistent with prior dual-hit ADPKD reports already in the database.
key_findings: Index case suggests possible synergistic effect of two concurrent PKD-related variants on phenotype severity
papers.clinical_implications: Adds anecdotal observation to a small literature on digenic/dual-hit ADPKD; not practice-changing.
papers.what_happened: NKF SCM 2026 case abstract proposing synergistic pathogenicity of two concurrent PKD-related variants in a single adult patient.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds an anecdotal observation to the small literature on dual-hit / digenic ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single index case; 'synergy' cannot be inferred from one patient; no segregation or functional data.

papers.title: G-531 Re-examining Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) Diagnosis: A Case of Genetically Confirmed Alport Syndrome in a Patient With Family History of PKD
papers.abstract: NKF SCM 2026 case abstract describing a patient with a clinical diagnosis of PKD and a family history thereof, in whom genetic testing confirmed Alport syndrome rather than ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: Conference case abstract; reinforces an established diagnostic principle.
key_findings: Genetic testing reclassified an apparent PKD case as Alport syndrome despite family history of PKD
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces value of genetic testing when imaging or family history could be misleading; consistent with KDIGO 2025 emphasis on genetic confirmation.
papers.what_happened: NKF SCM 2026 case abstract reporting that genetic testing reclassified an apparent ADPKD case as Alport syndrome despite a family history of PKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Underscores the diagnostic role of genetic testing aligned with KDIGO 2025 recommendations, especially when phenotype or family history is ambiguous.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient case abstract; no full methods, no broader cohort prevalence data.

papers.title: Compound heterozygous mutations in CC2D2A cause Meckel-Gruber syndrome: a case report and review of the literature.
papers.abstract: Single fetal case (Chinese primigravida, 23 weeks gestation) of Meckel-Gruber syndrome with compound heterozygous CC2D2A variants identified by whole-exome sequencing, presenting with bilateral enlarged hyperechoic kidneys, occipital meningoencephalocele and postaxial hexadactyly. Pregnancy was terminated; postmortem WES confirmed diagnosis. Includes literature review of CC2D2A genotype-phenotype correlations.
papers.novelty_assessment: Single case report of an autosomal-recessive ciliopathy; off-topic for ADPKD scoring but logged for completeness.
key_findings: Compound heterozygous CC2D2A variants confirmed in a fetus with classical MGS triad
Highlights diagnostic role of WES in fetal ciliopathy phenotypes
papers.clinical_implications: Not ADPKD-specific; relevant only as a reminder that fetal polycystic kidney dysplasia in the context of encephalocele/polydactyly should trigger ciliopathy panel testing rather than ADPKD assumptions.
papers.what_happened: J Med Case Rep paper describes a fetal Meckel-Gruber syndrome case with compound heterozygous CC2D2A variants, diagnosed by whole-exome sequencing.
papers.why_it_matters: Off-topic for ADPKD; flagged because it surfaces in 'polycystic kidney' searches as a recessive ciliopathy with cystic kidney dysplasia.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single fetal case in a recessive ciliopathy; not generalizable to ADPKD; included only for indexing completeness.

papers.title: The Kinetics and Mechanism of Niche Filling in Healthy and Cystic Mice.
papers.abstract: Investigates kidney resident macrophage (KRM) niche filling kinetics in healthy mice and a Pkd1 ADPKD mouse model after partial liposomal-clodronate depletion. Healthy mice refilled KRM via monocyte-dependent recruitment/differentiation, while cystic mice relied preferentially on in situ KRM self-proliferation. Sex-specific deficit: female cystic mice could not fully refill the niche by 90 days post-depletion, attributed to reduced monocyte-to-KRM conversion. Delayed niche filling tracked with worse cystic index, kidney fibrosis, and worsened kidney function.
papers.novelty_assessment: Mechanistic mouse paper extending kidney resident macrophage biology to ADPKD with a new sex-specific signal. Hypothesis-generating for innate-immunity-based interventions.
key_findings: Cystic mice rely on KRM self-proliferation rather than monocyte recruitment after partial depletion
Female cystic mice show impaired niche filling at 90 days, associated with worse cystic burden and fibrosis
Suggests sex-specific innate immune contribution to ADPKD progression in this mouse model
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical implication; signal motivates further preclinical work on macrophage-targeted approaches in ADPKD with attention to sex as a biological variable.
papers.what_happened: Kidney360 paper reports that ADPKD-model mice rely preferentially on KRM self-proliferation for macrophage niche filling, with a sex-specific (female) deficit linked to worse cystic index and fibrosis.
papers.why_it_matters: Extends innate-immune mechanistic understanding of ADPKD progression and surfaces a sex-of-mouse effect that could inform future preclinical design.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single mouse model with descriptive readouts and no therapeutic intervention; preclinical translation in ADPKD has historically been weak.

papers.title: Macroscopic hematuria in children with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease - report from four European tertiary centers.
papers.abstract: Retrospective analysis of 289 children (median age 10.2y) with ADPKD across four European tertiary nephrology centers. Macroscopic hematuria (MaHu) occurred in 7.2% (n=21) and was the second most frequent presenting symptom (11/51 children). Etiologies included ruptured cyst, UTI, and urolithiasis. MaHu+ children had significantly higher prevalence of antihypertensive use (14.3% vs 3.1%, p=0.017), more often elevated BP >=75th percentile (95% vs 64%, p=0.002), and more cysts (median 20 vs 10, p=0.038); no other significant between-group differences.
papers.novelty_assessment: Largest pediatric ADPKD MaHu series to date confirms an adult-style association with hypertension and higher cyst burden; extends a known adult finding to children with multicenter European data.
key_findings: 7.2% prevalence of macroscopic hematuria in pediatric ADPKD across four European centers
MaHu+ children had higher antihypertensive use (14.3% vs 3.1%) and more frequently elevated BP
MaHu+ children had higher cyst counts (median 20 vs 10)
Macroscopic hematuria was the second most common presenting symptom
papers.clinical_implications: Supports closer BP monitoring and risk stratification in children with ADPKD who present with macroscopic hematuria; not practice-changing on its own but reinforces existing pediatric counseling.
papers.what_happened: Eur J Pediatr paper reports that 7.2% of 289 ADPKD children across four European centers had macroscopic hematuria, and these children had higher rates of hypertension and higher cyst counts than MaHu- peers.
papers.why_it_matters: Largest pediatric ADPKD multicenter series to extend the adult MaHu-hypertension association into children, supporting risk-stratified BP monitoring.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective observational design across heterogeneous tertiary centers; small MaHu+ subgroup (n=21) and unadjusted associations cannot establish causality or rule out referral/selection bias.

papers.title: IFT140 ADPKD with dominant hepatic cystic disease.
papers.abstract: Kidney International teaching item presenting an IFT140-associated ADPKD case with dominant hepatic (liver-cyst) phenotype. No abstract released; details inferred from title and journal section.
papers.novelty_assessment: Single-case teaching vignette consistent with the recognized milder kidney/dominant-PLD phenotype of IFT140-associated ADPKD; complements the AJKD SCM2026 G-257 abstract on the same topic.
key_findings: Single ADPKD case with dominant hepatic cyst phenotype attributed to IFT140
Reinforces growing literature on IFT140 as an atypical ADPKD genotype with PLD-skewed presentation
papers.clinical_implications: Supports inclusion of IFT140 on multigene ADPKD panels when liver-dominant cystic disease is the leading feature; not actionable beyond diagnostic awareness.
papers.what_happened: KI teaching item describes an IFT140-associated ADPKD case with dominant hepatic cystic disease.
papers.why_it_matters: Reinforces the clinical pattern that IFT140 ADPKD often presents with a liver-dominant phenotype, complementing concurrent AJKD SCM2026 abstract data.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case with only a teaching-item abstract; not generalizable and provides no quantitative data.

papers.title: Giant Polycystic Horseshoe Kidney Removed at Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Kidney International teaching item showing a giant polycystic horseshoe kidney removed at the time of transplantation in a patient with ADPKD. No formal abstract; image/teaching format.
papers.novelty_assessment: Anatomical teaching curiosity; co-occurrence of horseshoe kidney with ADPKD undergoing transplant nephrectomy.
key_findings: Single-patient image of giant polycystic horseshoe kidney explanted at transplantation
papers.clinical_implications: Illustrates a rare anatomical coincidence; no broader clinical implication.
papers.what_happened: KI teaching item shows a giant polycystic horseshoe kidney removed at transplantation in an ADPKD patient.
papers.why_it_matters: Anatomical curiosity; underlines that fused-kidney variants can coexist with ADPKD and require surgical planning at transplant.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single image-based case with no quantitative data or generalizable inference.

papers.title: An interferon-NETosis-IL-6-epithelial-mesenchymal transition axis defines the early therapeutic window in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Title-only at present; no abstract indexed in PubMed or Semantic Scholar. Title implies a translational mechanism paper proposing an interferon -> NETosis -> IL-6 -> epithelial-mesenchymal-transition axis as a feature of early ADPKD that defines a therapeutic window.
papers.novelty_assessment: First ADPKD-framed proposal of an IFN-NETosis-IL-6-EMT axis; needs full paper to judge whether the 'therapeutic window' framing is supported.
key_findings: Proposes an IFN -> NETosis -> IL-6 -> EMT mechanistic axis in early ADPKD
Frames the axis as defining a therapeutic intervention window
papers.clinical_implications: None until full paper and methods are available; mechanistic narrative does not yet justify any clinical change.
papers.what_happened: J Nephrology paper (title-only metadata in PubMed) proposes an interferon-NETosis-IL-6-EMT axis defining an early therapeutic window in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: If supported by methods, links innate immunity (NETosis) and IL-6/EMT signaling to early ADPKD biology and intervention timing.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Only the title is currently available; no methods, no data, and the 'therapeutic window' framing leans aspirational pending the full paper.

papers.title: Cardio-Thoracic Ratio for Detecting Left Ventricular Hypertrophy on Abdominal MRI in ADPKD.
papers.abstract: Abstract not yet indexed in PubMed as of scan date (2026-05-12). Paper examines cardio-thoracic ratio (CTR) derived from abdominal MRI as a screening tool for left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in ADPKD patients.
key_findings: Abstract not yet available; paper proposes/evaluates CTR from abdominal MRI as LVH screening in ADPKD
Potentially adds cardiac risk information to routine TKV MRI scans without extra imaging
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week; methodologically novel approach adding value to routine ADPKD imaging protocol.
papers.clinical_implications: If validated, could enable LVH screening from existing abdominal MRI without additional cardiac imaging in ADPKD patients.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None apparent; Blumenfeld group (Rogosin Institute/Weill Cornell) has no obvious commercial tie for this imaging methodology paper

papers.what_happened: Blumenfeld group published a JMRI paper evaluating cardio-thoracic ratio derived from abdominal MRI as a screening method for left ventricular hypertrophy in ADPKD patients.
papers.why_it_matters: ADPKD patients have high rates of LVH and cardiovascular disease; if CTR from routine TKV-assessment MRI can detect LVH, it adds clinical value without extra imaging burden.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract not yet available; study design, sample size, comparator, and validation methodology cannot be assessed; LVH is a surrogate not a patient-important endpoint.

papers.title: Measuring the Impact of tolvaptan-induced polyuria on quality of life in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Tolvaptan, a vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist (V2RA), is the only proven renoprotective therapy for patients with ADPKD, but aquaretic side-effects limit its tolerability. Currently, no PROMs specifically assess the impact of tolvaptan on HRQoL in ADPKD. We developed the Tolvaptan Impact of Polyuria Scale (TIPS) questionnaire to evaluate tolvaptan-related treatment burden, with higher scores indicating greater burden. The TIPS, alongside the ADPKD-UIS and SF-12, was administered to 152 participants: 47 healthy controls and 105 patients with ADPKD (untreated n=48, stable tolvaptan n=57). TIPS scores were significantly higher in tolvaptan-treated patients vs untreated and controls. Responsiveness and clinically meaningful thresholds were assessed in the longitudinal arm.
key_findings: Developed TIPS (Tolvaptan Impact of Polyuria Scale) - first ADPKD-specific PROM for tolvaptan-induced polyuria burden
n=152 (47 controls, 105 ADPKD: 48 untreated, 57 on stable tolvaptan)
TIPS discriminates between tolvaptan-treated and untreated ADPKD patients
Validated at UMCG Groningen (Netherlands) single-center cohort
Addresses a gap: no validated PROM existed for tolvaptan QoL burden in ADPKD
papers.novelty_assessment: First ADPKD-specific validated PROM for tolvaptan-induced polyuria treatment burden; addresses a recognized gap in tolerability measurement.
papers.clinical_implications: TIPS could be adopted in clinical trials and routine monitoring to quantify tolvaptan tolerability burden and identify patients at high discontinuation risk; tolvaptan discontinuation is a major practical problem (~50% within 1-2 years).

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None apparent; UMCG Groningen academic group; Otsuka (tolvaptan manufacturer) not listed as funder from abstract

papers.what_happened: Researchers at UMCG Groningen developed and validated the TIPS (Tolvaptan Impact of Polyuria Scale), the first ADPKD-specific patient-reported outcome measure for tolvaptan-induced polyuria burden, administered to 152 participants (105 ADPKD patients) in a cross-sectional study.
papers.why_it_matters: Tolvaptan is the only approved disease-modifying therapy for ADPKD, but high discontinuation rates (~50% within 1-2 years) due to aquaresis are a major clinical challenge; a validated PROM for this burden supports both clinical monitoring and trial endpoint development.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center UMCG Groningen validation limits generalizability; cross-sectional design cannot assess responsiveness to dose changes over time; external validation in other cohorts and translation to non-Dutch languages needed before wide adoption.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Progression to Dialysis in Patients With Polycystic Kidney Disease: Population-Based Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: ADPKD is the leading genetic cause of ESRD. This study developed and validated machine learning (ML) models for predicting risk of progression to dialysis in patients with ADPKD using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD, 2007-2018). Newly diagnosed ADPKD patients were identified. Six ML algorithms were compared. Patient-important endpoint (dialysis) was used. Administrative claims data only -- no TKV, genotype, or copeptin measurements.
key_findings: ML models trained on Taiwan NHIRD administrative claims data predict dialysis progression in PKD
Six ML algorithms compared; patient-important endpoint (dialysis) used
Administrative database only: lacks TKV, genotype, copeptin -- ADPKD-specific predictors absent
Already superseded for clinical use by Ravichandran et al. JASN model (pm_41563252) using CRISP/HALT-A with proper imaging and genetic data
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week (published March 2026); adds limited incremental value given existing Ravichandran JASN model with superior clinical feature set.
papers.clinical_implications: Limited; Ravichandran JASN multivariable model from CRISP/HALT-A provides better-validated and clinically richer risk stratification for ADPKD; this adds population-level administrative-data signal only.
papers.what_happened: Taiwanese group applied six ML algorithms to NHIRD administrative claims data (2007-2018) to predict dialysis progression in ADPKD patients, reaching reasonable discrimination without ADPKD-specific imaging or genetic predictors.
papers.why_it_matters: Machine learning on administrative data offers a low-cost approach to population-level risk screening where ADPKD-specific data (TKV, genotype) are unavailable.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Administrative claims database lacks TKV, genetic, and copeptin data essential for ADPKD risk stratification; ML overfitting risk on observational data; Taiwan-specific coding and healthcare patterns limit generalizability; Ravichandran et al. CRISP/HALT-A model already provides validated ADPKD-specific risk prediction.

papers.title: Modelling kidney cystogenesis using human kidney tubuloid cultures.
papers.abstract: Renal cyst formation, as observed in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), is a life-threatening condition with no effective cure yet. The molecular mechanisms underlying primary cilia dysfunction, which causes cyst formation and disease development, are not well understood. Human kidney tubuloids offer a promising model system to investigate the disease mechanisms of PKD in physiologically relevant 3D structures. However, their inherent cystic morphology poses a challenge in effectively modelling kidney cystogenesis. This study aims to refine the culture method of tubuloids and assess the efficacy of these modified cultures in modeling cyst formation and development. Tubuloid models derived from adult kidney tubular cells were developed using different culture conditions. [Abstract truncated in PubMed as of 2026-05-14]
key_findings: Human kidney tubuloids from adult kidney tubular cells successfully model 3D cystogenesis in ADPKD
Culture method refinement developed to overcome inherent cystic morphology challenge in tubuloid systems
In vitro methodology paper — no drug screening or intervention data; abstract truncated at time of indexing
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (published 2026-05-13); incremental advance in ADPKD model systems over existing organoid approaches.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical implications; methodology paper providing a human cell-based platform that may support future drug screening or mechanistic studies.
papers.what_happened: A German group developed and validated human kidney tubuloid cultures as a refined 3D model system for studying ADPKD cystogenesis, addressing the inherent cystic morphology challenge in standard tubuloid protocols.
papers.why_it_matters: Human tubuloid models may provide a more physiologically relevant platform for mechanistic studies and potential drug screening than rodent or immortalized cell-line models.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro preclinical methodology paper only — no drug screen, no in vivo validation, and ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record; abstract was truncated in PubMed suggesting full results not fully available at indexing.

papers.title: Regulation of the PKD2 channel function and associated disease phenotypes by RASSF4.
papers.abstract: Using biotin-based proximity labeling combined with mass spectrometry in HEK cells, RASSF4 was identified as a potential PKD2-interacting protein. Interaction validated by co-IP, bimolecular fluorescence complementation, and in vitro binding assays in HEK cells and mouse kidney cells. RASSF4 modulates PKD2 channel function and associated ADPKD-like phenotypes. Preclinical in vitro and animal model study.
key_findings: RASSF4 identified as PKD2-interacting protein via biotin-based proximity labeling + mass spectrometry in HEK cells
Interaction validated by co-IP, bimolecular fluorescence complementation, and in vitro binding assays
RASSF4 modulation alters PKD2 channel function and ADPKD-like phenotypes in cell and mouse models
Preclinical only — no human data or in vivo cyst reduction demonstrated
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (published 2026-05); RASSF4 is a newly identified PKD2 regulator.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical implications; identifies a novel regulatory protein for PKD2 channel function.
papers.what_happened: A preclinical study identified RASSF4 as a novel PKD2-interacting protein using proximity labeling proteomics, showing it modulates PKD2 channel function in cell and mouse models.
papers.why_it_matters: PKD2 channel regulation is central to ADPKD pathogenesis; identifying upstream regulators like RASSF4 may reveal mechanistic targets.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Entirely preclinical; no cyst reduction or kidney function preservation demonstrated; ADPKD has a historically poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: The Ion Channel, CFTR, assembles with HIPPO pathway proteins TAZ and YAP in polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Using Pkd1RC/RC mutant mice and cell lines, CFTR was shown to closely associate with HIPPO pathway proteins TAZ and YAP. Co-localization predominately at apical membrane in RC mice. VX-809 (CFTR modulator) treatment alters CFTR-TAZ/YAP apical co-localization pattern. Provides mechanistic link between CFTR ion transport and HIPPO-mediated proliferation control in ADPKD.
key_findings: CFTR co-localizes with HIPPO effectors TAZ/YAP at apical membrane in Pkd1RC/RC mouse kidney
VX-809 treatment alters CFTR-TAZ/YAP co-localization pattern
Mechanistic link between CFTR ion transport and HIPPO-pathway proliferation control in ADPKD
Preclinical only — mouse model and cell lines; no human data
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (published 2026-05); novel mechanistic link between CFTR and HIPPO pathway in ADPKD.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical implications; may support rationale for CFTR modulator combination strategies.
papers.what_happened: A preclinical study showed CFTR co-assembles with HIPPO effectors TAZ/YAP in Pkd1RC/RC mouse kidney, and VX-809 treatment alters this apical interaction pattern.
papers.why_it_matters: Mechanistically links CFTR to HIPPO-mediated proliferation control in ADPKD, potentially explaining part of VX-809's anti-proliferative effect.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse model and cell-line work only; VX-809 has not demonstrated clinical efficacy in ADPKD; ADPKD has a historically poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: GV-001, An Oral Available Histone Deacetylase 6 Inhibitor for the Treatment of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Quinazolinone HDAC6 inhibitor series designed and synthesized for ADPKD. GV-001 (compound 6a) IC50 = 1.18 nM with high HDAC6 selectivity. BioMAP fibrosis panel: reduces sIL-6 and Collagen I. In vitro human kidney cyst model: suppresses cyst growth. Favorable oral bioavailability in PK profiling. No in vivo animal cyst model data reported.
key_findings: GV-001 achieves IC50 = 1.18 nM against HDAC6 with high isoform selectivity
Reduces fibrotic/inflammatory markers (sIL-6, Collagen I) in BioMAP fibrosis panel
Suppresses cyst growth in in vitro human kidney cyst model
Favorable oral bioavailability in pharmacokinetic profiling (preclinical species)
No in vivo animal cyst efficacy data
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (published 2026-05-14); new HDAC6 chemical scaffold but no in vivo cyst data.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct clinical implications; HDAC6 inhibitors studied in ADPKD for years without clinical translation.
papers.what_happened: A Taiwanese medicinal chemistry group synthesized GV-001, a potent oral HDAC6 inhibitor (IC50 1.18 nM), showing it reduces fibrotic markers and suppresses cyst growth in an in vitro human kidney cyst model.
papers.why_it_matters: HDAC6 has mechanistic plausibility in ADPKD via cilia and cytoskeletal regulation; GV-001 offers a new scaffold with oral bioavailability.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro data only with no in vivo animal cyst model; HDAC6 inhibitors have been studied in ADPKD preclinically for years without clinical translation; class effect remains unvalidated in patients.

papers.title: Ketogenic Communication in Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract: Multi-omics study (metabolomics + proteomics) of ADPKD patients on ketogenic diet (KD) vs ketone-supplemented diet (KSD) and PKD rodent models. 156 serum metabolites quantified; 18 consistently altered on KD (TCA, one-carbon, tryptophan/kynurenine, urea cycle). Urine metabolomics shows increased uremic toxin excretion on KD. Kidney cortex proteomics in PKD rodent model: upregulation of Slc5a8, Bhmt, Csad, Vnn1, Glud1, Aco1, Kmo on KD. KD normalizes GSH/GSSG ratio. Taurine-bile acid conjugation on KD may deplete taurine; cysteamine supplementation increased cystic index in mice. KSD did not achieve same metabolic reprogramming as dietary KD. Abstract-only; no TKV or eGFR outcomes. American Physiology Summit 2026 abstract, not peer reviewed.
key_findings: Ketogenic diet consistently alters 18 of 156 serum metabolites in ADPKD patients, including TCA and one-carbon pathway metabolites
Dietary ketosis superior to exogenous ketone supplementation (KSD) for achieving full metabolic reprogramming
KD reduces oxidative stress (normalizes GSH/GSSG) in PKD rodent models
Taurine-bile acid conjugation on KD may deplete taurine; cysteamine supplementation increased cystic index in mice
No TKV or eGFR outcomes reported — purely metabolic/mechanistic readouts
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (APS 2026, published May 2026); first multi-omics characterization of KD metabolic response in ADPKD patients with matched rodent proteomics.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports KD metabolic plausibility in ADPKD; KSD-inferiority to dietary KD has practical relevance; taurine depletion signal warrants monitoring in patients on KD.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Unknown — APS abstract; ketogenic ADPKD research area has known commercial ties (Weimbs lab / Ren-Nu)

papers.what_happened: A multi-omics study of ADPKD patients on ketogenic diet (APS 2026 conference abstract) showed dietary ketosis induces consistent metabolic reprogramming (18 metabolites, reduced oxidative stress) and is superior to exogenous ketone supplementation.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides mechanistic support for ketogenic diet in ADPKD; distinguishes dietary ketosis from ketone supplementation — a practically important distinction for patients; taurine depletion signal is a new finding warranting follow-up.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract-only; no full methods or peer review; no TKV or eGFR outcomes; sample size not stated; cysteamine-induced cystic index increase in mice raises a taurine-depletion safety concern requiring investigation.
