papers.title: A comprehensive review of extrarenal manifestations of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
papers.abstract: Narrative review of extrarenal manifestations in ADPKD including liver cysts, intracranial aneurysms, cardiac valvular disease, hernias, and other systemic features.
key_findings: Narrative review of extrarenal ADPKD manifestations — no new original data
Stale — November 2025, is_new_this_week=false
papers.novelty_assessment: Stale — November 2025 narrative review; backfill. Low incremental value given KDIGO 2025 guideline.
papers.clinical_implications: Background context only.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review summarized extrarenal manifestations of ADPKD including liver cysts, intracranial aneurysms, and cardiovascular complications.
papers.why_it_matters: Extrarenal manifestations affect QoL and management in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no new data; KDIGO 2025 guideline already provides evidence-based guidance on extrarenal manifestations; stale by ~6 months.

papers.title: Pregnancy and Kidney Disease Progression in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract: Secondary analysis of HALT-PKD data (n=455 women). No association of 1-2 or 3+ prior pregnancies with eGFR slope, DTKV, or composite kidney failure. In-study pregnancy (n=13, propensity-matched 1:4) also null (eGFR slope Beta:-0.14 [-2.72,2.44]). Conclusion: pregnancy was not associated with ADPKD progression.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: HALT-PKD NIH-funded; no pharmaceutical sponsorship apparent

papers.what_happened: A secondary analysis of HALT-PKD trial data (n=455 women) found no association between pregnancy history or in-study pregnancies (n=13, propensity-matched) and eGFR slope, TKV change, or composite kidney failure outcomes in women with early- or late-stage ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Pregnancy's effect on ADPKD progression has been clinically uncertain; this null result from the best-characterized ADPKD cohort is informative for counseling reproductive-age women.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The in-study pregnancy comparison is n=13 (wide confidence intervals), follow-up was 2.5-4 years (short for a slowly-progressive disease), women were older (median age 45) than those most likely to become pregnant, and pregnancy was self-reported.

papers.title: Small-Molecule Degradation of the MicroRNA-21 Precursor Rescues Pathogenic Pathways in Cellular Models of Fibrosis
papers.abstract: TGP-21-RiboTAC degrades pre-miR-21 in polycystic kidney cell lines, derepresses PDCD4 and PPARalpha, and inhibits proliferation. In vitro only; no in vivo cyst model tested.
papers.what_happened: A RiboTAC small molecule (TGP-21-RiboTAC) degraded the miR-21 precursor in polycystic kidney cell lines and derepressed PDCD4 and PPARalpha in vitro.
papers.why_it_matters: miR-21 is overexpressed in ADPKD cystic tissue; targeted degradation of its precursor is a mechanistically novel approach to RNA-based therapy in PKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: All data are from cell lines only; no in vivo cyst model was tested, and ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record for RNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Cystic burden meets blood pressure: cardiac remodelling in paediatric autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Single-centre cross-sectional study n=116 children (<18 years) with ADPKD. Hypertension 12% (n=14), 8 masked hypertension. High BP (n=30, 26%) associated with higher cyst burden (56% vs 34%, p=0.036), LVH (16.6% vs 4.6%, p=0.034), higher relative LV wall thickness (0.34 vs 0.29, p<0.001) vs normotensives.
papers.what_happened: A single-centre cross-sectional study of 116 children with ADPKD found elevated BP associated with higher cyst burden and LV hypertrophy, with 12% meeting hypertension criteria including 8 with masked hypertension.
papers.why_it_matters: Pediatric ADPKD cardiac consequences of hypertension are poorly characterised; this adds cross-sectional evidence linking cyst burden to early LV remodelling.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-centre cross-sectional design cannot establish causation or progression trajectory; BP comparisons involve small subgroups (n=30) with no longitudinal kidney function data.

papers.title: Intraoperative Iliac Artery Dissection and Postoperative Cerebral Infarction in a Kidney Transplant Recipient With an RNF213 p.R4810K Variant: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Case report: 61-year-old ADPKD patient with RNF213 p.R4810K variant suffered intraoperative iliac artery dissection and cerebral infarction during kidney transplantation. ADPKD is only the renal etiology; focus is on RNF213 vascular complication.
papers.what_happened: Case report of an ADPKD transplant recipient with RNF213 variant who suffered intraoperative vascular dissection and cerebral infarction.
papers.why_it_matters: Highlights potential need for pre-transplant vascular risk screening in ADPKD patients with moyamoya-associated genetic variants.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report; ADPKD is incidental to the RNF213 finding; no generalizable ADPKD management implications.

papers.title: Dietary Taurine Supplementation and its Effects on Cystogenesis in an ARPKD Rat Model
papers.abstract: PCK rats (ARPKD model) have high taurine in cyst fluid (~6 mM) and elevated urinary taurine. Testing: taurine supplementation exacerbates vs beta-alanine depletion reduces cystic burden. No results disclosed. ARPKD not ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: APS 2026 abstract reporting high taurine in ARPKD (PCK rat) cyst fluid and testing whether dietary taurine supplementation vs beta-alanine-mediated depletion affects cystic burden.
papers.why_it_matters: Connects to taurine depletion signal observed in ADPKD patients on ketogenic diets (W20); raises whether taurine flux is mechanistically important in cystogenesis.
papers.what_limits_confidence: ARPKD model not ADPKD; abstract-only with no results; ARPKD-to-ADPKD translation is uncertain.

papers.title: Vasopressin Drives Increased Excitability in Isolated Renal Sensory Neurons from Polycystic Kidney Disease Mice
papers.abstract: Vasopressin drives increased excitability in isolated renal sensory neurons from PKD mice. Vasopressin pathway dual role: drives cyst formation via V2R and may drive renal pain. APS 2026 abstract.
papers.what_happened: APS 2026 abstract showing vasopressin increases excitability of isolated renal sensory neurons in PKD mice, suggesting a mechanism for pain.
papers.why_it_matters: Renal pain is a major burden in ADPKD; a vasopressin-pain link may have implications given V2R antagonism is already standard therapy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical mouse model, abstract-only data, PKD model not ADPKD-specific.

papers.title: Increased Renal Sensory Neuron Excitability Independent of Renal Cysticity in a Mouse Model of Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract: Renal sensory neuron excitability is increased in PKD models and contributes to renal cystic progression. Increased excitability shown to occur independently of cysticity. APS 2026 abstract.
papers.what_happened: APS 2026 abstract showing renal sensory neuron excitability is elevated in a PKD mouse model independently of cyst severity.
papers.why_it_matters: Complements companion vasopressin abstract; suggests renal pain neural program may be independent of structural cyst burden in PKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical mouse model, abstract-only, no patient data.

papers.title: Association of anemia with long-term renal prognosis in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Retrospective n=553 Japanese ADPKD patients. Hemoglobin levels and kidney outcomes (50% eGFR decline or RRT). Survival analyses. Possible overlap with pm_42053857 (same institution, n=552, Clin Exp Nephrol Apr 2026) - may represent duplicate or companion analysis.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective Japanese single-centre analysis of 553 ADPKD patients finding anemia (Hb levels) associated with long-term kidney outcomes.
papers.why_it_matters: Anemia in ADPKD is understudied; Hb level could serve as a simple prognostic marker if finding is validated.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective single-centre; possible partial overlap with companion paper pm_42053857 from same authors and similar n — results may duplicate rather than independently replicate.

papers.title: Post-COVID-19 Outcomes of Patients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Multicenter Study
papers.abstract: Multicenter retrospective study examining post-COVID-19 outcomes in ADPKD patients.
papers.what_happened: Multicenter retrospective study of post-COVID-19 outcomes in ADPKD patients.
papers.why_it_matters: ADPKD patients with reduced eGFR or on tolvaptan may have distinct COVID-19 vulnerability and recovery patterns.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective multicenter design; COVID-19 impact on ADPKD-specific progression is confounded by the pandemic's variable clinical course.

papers.title: Vascular transcriptional and metabolic changes precede progressive intrarenal microvascular rarefaction in ADPKD
papers.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Renal Physiology
papers.abstract: Transcriptional and metabolic analysis showing vascular changes precede intrarenal microvascular rarefaction in ADPKD models.
papers.what_happened: Translational study in ADPKD models showing vascular transcriptional and metabolic changes precede progressive intrarenal microvascular rarefaction.
papers.why_it_matters: Microvascular rarefaction may be an early and potentially targetable contributor to ADPKD progression independent of cyst burden.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical study; clinical relevance of intrarenal MV rarefaction trajectory in ADPKD has not been established in humans.

papers.title: Urinary interleukin-37 as a suggested protective biomarker of renal prognosis in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Cross-sectional study evaluating urinary IL-37 expression in ADPKD patients as a potential anti-inflammatory protective biomarker of renal prognosis.
papers.what_happened: Cross-sectional study found urinary IL-37 expression in ADPKD patients; authors suggest it may be a protective biomarker.
papers.why_it_matters: Novel inflammatory marker that may reflect anti-inflammatory activity; could stratify patients if validated longitudinally.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional design cannot establish prognostic utility; 'suggested protective biomarker' in the title overstates single cross-sectional data; claim_calibration 6/10 — rewrite conservative: this study identifies an association that requires prospective longitudinal validation before any prognostic inference is warranted.

papers.title: Ultrasound-assisted diagnosis and ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation of renal cell carcinoma in ADPKD
papers.abstract: Case report: RCC diagnosis and contrast-enhanced ultrasound-guided RFA in an ADPKD patient with severely distorted renal anatomy limiting conventional CT/MRI.
papers.what_happened: Case report of contrast-enhanced ultrasound-guided RFA for RCC in an ADPKD patient where conventional imaging was limited by distorted anatomy.
papers.why_it_matters: RCC detection in ADPKD is challenging; CEUS-guided RFA offers a potential minimally invasive approach in poor surgical candidates.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case; no comparative data on outcomes vs surgery in ADPKD.

papers.title: Coincidence of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and Alport syndrome: a case report and literature review
papers.abstract: Case report and literature review of concurrent ADPKD and Alport syndrome in one patient. Highlights difficulty of genetic diagnosis when two hereditary kidney diseases co-occur.
papers.what_happened: Case report of co-occurring ADPKD and Alport syndrome in one patient, with literature review.
papers.why_it_matters: Reinforces KDIGO 2025 guidance on comprehensive genetic testing; co-occurring hereditary diseases can confound phenotype attribution.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case; rare co-occurrence not generalizable.

papers.title: WCN26-476 SCO-792, an enteropeptidase inhibitor, attenuated renal and hepatic cystogenesis
papers.abstract: WCN26 abstract. SCO-792, an enteropeptidase inhibitor, reported to attenuate renal and hepatic cystogenesis. Abstract-only; stale item.
papers.what_happened: WCN26 abstract reporting SCO-792 (enteropeptidase inhibitor) reduced renal and hepatic cyst formation in a preclinical model.
papers.why_it_matters: Enteropeptidase inhibition is a novel mechanism; SCO-792 may address both renal and hepatic ADPKD manifestations.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract-only, stale (April 2026), no full methods or results; preclinical translation record is poor.

papers.title: WCN26-7417 Tamibarotene, an agonist of the retinoic acid receptor, in ADPKD
papers.abstract: WCN26 abstract on tamibarotene (RAR agonist) in ADPKD. Companion to NCT06289998 (ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING). No full results available.
papers.what_happened: WCN26 abstract on tamibarotene (RAR agonist) in ADPKD, companion to NCT06289998 trial.
papers.why_it_matters: Tamibarotene is an active clinical program; any WCN26 presentation may signal early trial data.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract-only, stale April 2026, no results data available.

papers.title: WCN26-6644 Selective PPARalpha Modulator Inhibits Cyst Enlargement in ADPKD
papers.abstract: WCN26 abstract. Selective PPARalpha modulator reported to inhibit cyst enlargement in ADPKD model. Mechanistically related to miR-21/PPARalpha pathway.
papers.what_happened: WCN26 abstract reporting a selective PPARalpha modulator inhibits cyst enlargement in a preclinical ADPKD model.
papers.why_it_matters: PPARalpha modulation intersects with fatty acid oxidation and metabolic reprogramming in cystic epithelia; mechanistically distinct from current clinical candidates.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract-only, stale, no full results; preclinical translation record is poor.

papers.title: ADPKD, pregnancy and preimplantation selection: clinical and bioethical considerations.
papers.abstract: Review examining preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) for ADPKD in the Italian legal context, permitted since 2015 for monogenic late-onset conditions. Discusses health risks of assisted reproductive technologies, embryo selection ethics, psychosocial implications, access equity, and shared decision-making framework for nephrology, obstetrics, and genetics multidisciplinary teams.
papers.what_happened: An Italian group published a narrative review examining the clinical and bioethical considerations of preimplantation genetic diagnosis for ADPKD, where Italian law has permitted PGD for monogenic late-onset disorders since 2015.
papers.why_it_matters: As genetic testing becomes standard in ADPKD management and KDIGO 2025 emphasizes genetic diagnosis, preimplantation genetic testing counseling is increasingly relevant for reproductive decision-making.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no primary data; the bioethical and legal framework is specific to Italy and may not generalize to other regulatory contexts.

papers.title: Future needs for clinical trials in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Perspective/review in Nature Reviews Nephrology discussing future methodological needs for clinical trials in ADPKD. No abstract available in PubMed.
papers.what_happened: Nature Reviews Nephrology published a perspective on future methodological needs for clinical trials in ADPKD (published March 24, 2026 — stale, not new this week).
papers.why_it_matters: NRN perspective pieces on trial methodology are influential for trialists, regulators, and funders shaping the ADPKD pipeline.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Stale item (>14 days); expert opinion, no primary data; no abstract available for detailed assessment.

papers.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology
papers.abstract: ACR Appropriateness Criteria for ADPKD imaging: ultrasound is first-line (detects cysts ≥2-3 mm, high diagnostic accuracy); MRI is alternative and preferred for TKV measurement; CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast is preferred for complications (hemorrhage, rupture, infection). TKV quantified by MRI is recommended as imaging biomarker for disease progression and treatment response assessment.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: ACR consensus process; possible imaging industry ties but not directly stated

papers.what_happened: The American College of Radiology published updated Appropriateness Criteria for ADPKD imaging, recommending US as first-line diagnostic, MRI as preferred for TKV measurement, and CT for complications (published March 12, 2026 — stale).
papers.why_it_matters: ACR criteria are widely used by radiologists and nephrologists; codification of MRI as the preferred TKV tool aligns with KDIGO 2025 and supports imaging biomarker acceptance.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Stale item (>14 days); consensus document, not primary research data; may lag emerging evidence on automated TKV tools.

papers.title: 2025 KDIGO Executive Summary: Diagnosis and Management of Pediatric Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Executive summary of the 2025 KDIGO guidelines specifically addressing pediatric ADPKD diagnosis and management. Builds on earlier frameworks including the 2019 international consensus statement for children and young people. Addresses screening, monitoring, early-onset hypertension, and treatment protocols for pediatric patients.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: KDIGO process; individual panelist conflicts listed in full guideline

papers.what_happened: Kidney & Blood Pressure Research published the KDIGO 2025 executive summary specifically focused on pediatric ADPKD diagnosis and management (stale, published early 2026).
papers.why_it_matters: Companion to the adult KDIGO 2025 guideline; provides evidence-based guidance for the management of ADPKD in children and adolescents, where screening and early hypertension management differ substantially from adults.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Stale item (>14 days); executive summary format may omit nuance present in the full guideline; evidence base for pediatric ADPKD is weaker than for adults.

papers.title: Cyst-type epithelial heterogeneity shapes therapeutic responsiveness in ADPKD
papers.abstract: bioRxiv preprint. No abstract indexed. Title suggests characterization of cyst-type epithelial heterogeneity and its relationship to therapeutic response in ADPKD — potentially relevant to why different cyst types respond differently to treatment.
papers.what_happened: A bioRxiv preprint (posted May 12, 2026) was indexed suggesting that cyst-type epithelial heterogeneity may shape therapeutic responsiveness in ADPKD; no abstract is available for assessment.
papers.why_it_matters: If validated, cyst-type heterogeneity could explain variable treatment responses and inform patient stratification for targeted therapies.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint with no abstract or methods available; cannot assess study design, endpoints, or claims; pre-peer-review.

papers.title: Paradoxical Hyponatremia on High-Dose Tolvaptan in ADPKD
papers.abstract: KIR item (likely WCN26 supplement or short report) describing paradoxical hyponatremia observed with high-dose tolvaptan in ADPKD. No abstract available.
papers.what_happened: A KIR item (likely WCN26 supplement) describes paradoxical hyponatremia in an ADPKD patient on high-dose tolvaptan (stale April 2026 — no abstract available).
papers.why_it_matters: Hyponatremia is counterintuitive given tolvaptan's aquaretic mechanism; awareness of this rare complication may inform monitoring.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Stale; no abstract or full text available; likely case report or single observation; cannot assess frequency or mechanism.

papers.title: Combined treatment with metformin and cinacalcet significantly reduces cyst growth of human 3D cells derived from ADPKD cyst-lining epithelia and restores the altered bioenergetic profile
papers.abstract: APS 2026 conference abstract. Combined metformin (200 µM) + cinacalcet (1 nM, 3 days) significantly reduced forskolin-induced cyst growth in human 3D ADPKD cyst-lining epithelial cells vs. either drug alone. Synergistic suppression of S6 ribosomal protein phosphorylation (mTORC1 marker). Dual treatment fully restored the bioenergetic profile including mitochondrial ATP production and oxidative phosphorylation — improvements beyond single-drug effects. No in vivo data reported.
papers.what_happened: An APS 2026 conference abstract reported that combined metformin + cinacalcet had synergistic effects in reducing cyst growth and restoring the bioenergetic profile in human 3D ADPKD cyst-lining epithelial cells in vitro.
papers.why_it_matters: Both drugs are clinically available; the combination approach targeting AMPK (metformin) and CaSR (cinacalcet) simultaneously addresses two ADPKD-relevant pathways, providing a rationale for a combination trial.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro only (3D cell model, no in vivo cyst readout); abstract-only, no peer-reviewed full paper; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation record is poor; headline overstates clinical implication.

papers.title: Greater netrin-1 in male ADPKD mice drives enhanced cyst growth compared to females
papers.abstract: APS 2026 abstract. Male Pkd1RC/RC mice had significantly greater renal netrin-1 levels than females (sex interaction p<0.0001), with associated higher cyst growth, BUN, and cell proliferation. Netrin-1 neutralizing antibody (10 mg/kg/48h, 4 weeks) reduced cyst growth, cell proliferation, and improved kidney function in both sexes (n=4-5/group); effects were more pronounced in males (sex*treatment interaction p<0.002). Suggests netrin-1 upregulation mediates the sex-specific difference in ADPKD progression observed clinically.
papers.what_happened: An APS 2026 abstract showed that netrin-1 is significantly higher in male vs. female Pkd1RC/RC mice, and that a netrin-1 neutralizing antibody reduced cyst growth more in males than females, proposing netrin-1 as a mechanistic basis for sex differences in ADPKD progression.
papers.why_it_matters: Males with ADPKD clinically progress faster than females; identifying a druggable molecular mediator (netrin-1) of this sex difference is a novel mechanistic insight worth following.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse model only (n=4-5/group), abstract-only, 4-week follow-up; sex-specific differences in mice may not translate to humans with the same magnitude; netrin-1 neutralization has no established clinical development path in ADPKD.

papers.title: Lithium carbonate attenuates renal expansion but exacerbates cyst morphometry in Pkd1 RC/RC mice
papers.abstract: APS 2026 abstract. Lithium carbonate (0.2% Li2CO3 diet, 8 weeks) was tested as a cheaper tolvaptan alternative via cAMP inhibition in male and female Pkd1RC/RC mice. Results: Li2CO3 reduced kidney volume on ultrasound in both sexes and total kidney mass in males (p=0.0178), but worsened cystic index (proportion of renal compartment occupied by cystic space) in males (p=0.0262) and reduced tubular min-FD in males (p=0.0001). Tissue injury, fibrosis, cyst quantity, and cross-sectional cyst area were not improved. Conclusion: Li2CO3 offers no protective benefit; in males it worsens cystic profile despite reducing total kidney mass.
papers.what_happened: An APS 2026 abstract tested lithium carbonate as a cheaper cAMP-inhibiting tolvaptan alternative in Pkd1RC/RC mice and found it offered no protective benefit; in males, it worsened the cystic index despite reducing total kidney mass.
papers.why_it_matters: Lithium's known AVP-cAMP inhibitory properties have prompted interest as an affordable tolvaptan surrogate; this preclinical result does not support that hypothesis and raises safety concerns about dissociation between kidney volume and cystic architecture.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse model only (abstract-only, 8 weeks); small n per sex group; cystic index worsening in males with apparent kidney mass reduction reveals dissociation that requires mechanistic explanation; not directly applicable to humans.

papers.title: Association of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with cardiovascular disease and mortality in patients with treated kidney failure
papers.abstract: A retrospective review of ANZDATA Registry patients with kidney failure commencing KRT between 1963 and 2020 (n=63,875, 2,466 ADPKD). ADPKD was independently associated with lower mortality on dialysis (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.67-0.75), similar post-transplant mortality (aHR 0.96), and slightly improved graft survival (aHR 0.87). Causes of death were similar including cardiovascular disease (27.5% vs 27.6%).

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None apparent (Australian academic group, ANZDATA registry)

papers.what_happened: An ANZDATA registry analysis of 63,875 KRT patients found ADPKD (n=2,466) was independently associated with lower dialysis mortality (aHR 0.71) but similar post-transplant mortality and graft survival compared to other kidney failure etiologies over 1963-2020.
papers.why_it_matters: Large registry data confirm ADPKD-specific KRT prognosis useful for clinical counseling; notably, the cardiovascular death proportion was similar to non-ADPKD patients despite ADPKD being a vascular disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective observational design spanning 57 years with major era heterogeneity; survival benefit likely explained by fewer comorbidities in ADPKD patients rather than disease-specific factors, and residual confounding cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Effectiveness and mechanistic effects of green mamba peptide MQ232 in an orthologous mouse model of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Tolvaptan is the only approved ADPKD treatment. MQ232 (green mamba V2R inverse agonist peptide) equally attenuated PKD vs tolvaptan in orthologous Pkd1 mouse model. Higher MQ232 doses produced greater cAMP/AQP2 reductions without proportional disease improvement, implicating non-cAMP V2R pathways (Src/ERK/CRAF/Akt/RPS6/Stat3).
papers.what_happened: Wang et al. tested MQ232, a green mamba-derived V2R inverse agonist peptide, in an orthologous Pkd1 mouse model and found it attenuated cystic kidney disease as effectively as tolvaptan, but with non-cAMP-dependent signaling contributing to disease attenuation.
papers.why_it_matters: Demonstrates V2R inverse agonist anti-PKD activity can be mechanistically separated from cAMP/aquaretic effects, potentially informing next-generation V2R-targeting compounds.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical orthologous mouse data only; ADPKD has a consistently poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record; no inference about human tolerability or efficacy is warranted.

papers.title: Identification of drug repurposing candidates for the treatment of polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Thermal proteome profiling identified birinapant, bardoxolone methyl, and salicylic acid as drug repurposing candidates for ADPKD. Shared mechanism: disruption of ADP/ATP translocases (SLC25A4/5/6) via reduced ATP production. Salicylic acid additionally inhibited PTK2/FAK (PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway).
papers.what_happened: Meyer et al. applied thermal proteome profiling to identify birinapant, bardoxolone methyl, and salicylic acid as drug repurposing candidates for ADPKD, with a shared mitochondrial ATP production mechanism and additional PTK2/FAK activity for salicylic acid.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides mechanistic basis for repurposing existing drugs against ADPKD targets; bardoxolone methyl connection echoes PHOENIX Phase 2 trial, though that trial's eGFR signal was likely hemodynamic.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro thermal proteome profiling discovery screen; requires in vivo cystic kidney validation; bardoxolone's prior ADPKD Phase 2 human data were inconclusive for disease modification.

papers.title: The effect of tolvaptan on renal progression and systemic inflammation in ADPKD.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective two-center cohort, n=80 ADPKD (40 tolvaptan vs 40 controls). Evaluated tolvaptan effect on inflammatory markers and renal progression. Inflammation plays a crucial role in ADPKD progression; study investigated potential anti-inflammatory effects of tolvaptan beyond V2R antagonism.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective two-center Turkish cohort (n=80) compared inflammatory markers and renal progression between tolvaptan-treated and control ADPKD patients, exploring whether tolvaptan has anti-inflammatory effects.
papers.why_it_matters: Tolvaptan's potential anti-inflammatory mechanisms could explain part of its benefit and might inform combination strategies.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective, n=80, no randomization; inflammatory marker surrogates; selection bias between treated and untreated patients is likely.

papers.title: Dapagliflozin use in tolvaptan-treated patients with ADPKD: exploring renal outcomes in a retrospective study.
papers.abstract_snippet: Observational study evaluating efficacy of dapagliflozin added to existing tolvaptan in ADPKD. Primary outcome: chronic eGFR slope via multivariable linear mixed-effect model; within-group analysis comparing eGFR slope before vs after adding dapagliflozin to tolvaptan.
papers.what_happened: Nakajima et al. retrospectively evaluated eGFR slope in ADPKD patients when dapagliflozin was added to existing tolvaptan, using within-patient before/after comparison and linear mixed-effect modeling.
papers.why_it_matters: The tolvaptan+SGLT2i combination is a highly relevant clinical question given both are used in ADPKD, providing early observational data pending RCTs like STOP-PKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Before/after design without concurrent controls cannot isolate dapagliflozin effect from natural trajectory or regression to the mean; Japanese single-center data.

papers.title: Real-world evidence for using urine osmolality as a practical tool in tolvaptan dose optimization in patients with ADPKD.
papers.abstract_snippet: Prospective single-center study, n=24 ADPKD patients on tolvaptan 7-50 months. Morning urine and 24-hour urine osmolality evaluated as biomarkers for individualized tolvaptan dosing. Dosing titrated based on tolerability and achievement of urine osmolality targets to minimize discontinuations and adverse events.
papers.what_happened: Marn Pernat et al. prospectively tracked 24 ADPKD patients with urine osmolality-guided tolvaptan dose titration over 7-50 months, exploring osmolality as a practical biomarker for individualizing tolvaptan dosing.
papers.why_it_matters: Tolvaptan discontinuation rates are high; a validated osmolality-guided dosing algorithm could improve retention, though this study is too small for definitive recommendations.
papers.what_limits_confidence: n=24, single center, no randomized comparison; urine osmolality targets lack standardization across centers.

papers.title: Translational readthrough therapy for ADPKD induces polycystin1 expression and partially rescues functional deficits in PKD1 mutant cells.
papers.abstract_snippet: In approximately 30% of ADPKD patients, the heritable mutation is a PKD1 nonsense variant. Translational readthrough therapy induced PC1 expression and partially rescued functional deficits in PKD1 nonsense-mutant cells in vitro. Approach targets the nonsense-mutation subset specifically.
papers.what_happened: Torban et al. demonstrated in vitro that translational readthrough therapy induces polycystin-1 expression and partially rescues functional deficits in PKD1 nonsense-mutant cells, providing proof-of-concept for a subset-specific approach targeting the ~30% of ADPKD patients with PKD1 nonsense mutations.
papers.why_it_matters: Mutation-class-specific therapy parallels the cystic fibrosis model (CFTR modulators); if in vivo data follow, this could represent a disease-modifying approach for a definable PKD1 subgroup.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro only; applies only to ~30% PKD1 patients with nonsense mutations; no in vivo cystic data; translational readthrough efficiency and off-target codon suppression in humans are unknown.

papers.title: Machine learning for predicting CKD stages in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a nationwide cohort study in Japan.
papers.abstract_snippet: Machine learning applied to nationwide Japanese ADPKD cohort to build CKD stage progression prediction models. ML captures nonlinear variable interactions beyond traditional regression, enabling personalized CKD progression prediction in ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: Shimada et al. applied machine learning to a nationwide Japanese ADPKD cohort to build a CKD stage progression prediction model, demonstrating feasibility of ML-based personalized risk stratification.
papers.why_it_matters: Complements existing validated risk models (Ravichandran JASN 2026, Mayo Imaging Classes) for the Japanese clinical context.
papers.what_limits_confidence: ML models require external validation; CKD stage is a cruder endpoint than eGFR slope or kidney failure; the Ravichandran multivariable model offers better-validated guidance for most settings.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator inhibitor GLPG2737 for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: phase 2a MANGROVE study.
papers.abstract_snippet: MANGROVE (NCT04578548): phase 2a RCT, n=66, GLPG2737 150mg vs placebo, 52 weeks. htTKV change: GLPG2737 +8.2% vs placebo +9.2% (difference -0.91%, p=0.61). eGFR change difference -2.31 mL/min/1.73m2 (p=0.17). Well tolerated. Study terminated early due to lack of efficacy.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Galapagos-funded (GLPG = Galapagos compound); academic investigators including Gansevoort (UMCG)

papers.what_happened: A phase 2a randomized double-blind trial (MANGROVE, n=66) showed GLPG2737 (CFTR inhibitor, 150 mg/day) did not reduce htTKV growth or slow eGFR decline vs placebo over 52 weeks in rapidly progressive ADPKD; the study was terminated early for lack of efficacy.
papers.why_it_matters: CFTR inhibition had substantial preclinical support; this negative RCT removes GLPG2737 from the ADPKD pipeline and challenges the CFTR-inhibition therapeutic hypothesis in humans.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Phase 2a exploratory design (underpowered for definitive conclusions), surrogate endpoints only (htTKV, eGFR), single dose tested — higher doses or other CFTR-targeting approaches remain untested.

papers.title: Nationwide epidemiological survey of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in Japan in 2022.
papers.abstract_snippet: Nationwide survey estimating ADPKD prevalence in Japan 2022: ~53,518 total patients (42.8 per 100,000; 1 in 2,335). Non-KRT patients estimated 40,901 (95% CI 29,543-52,259). Higher disease burden than previously recognized. Response rate 32.9%.
papers.what_happened: A nationwide survey estimated the total ADPKD-relevant population in Japan in 2022 at approximately 53,518 (42.8 per 100,000 population), higher than prior estimates.
papers.why_it_matters: Updated epidemiological data contextualizes ADPKD treatment uptake, guideline impact, and healthcare planning in Japan, where tolvaptan was first approved.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Survey design with a 32.9% response rate and registry KRT data that may include non-ADPKD polycystic kidney patients; wide confidence intervals (95% CI 29,543-52,259) on the non-KRT estimate.

papers.title: Semaglutide reduces kidney disease severity and improves vascular endothelial function in mice with polycystic kidney disease in a diet-dependent manner
papers.abstract_snippet: APS 2026 abstract. Semaglutide (0.4 mg/kg/day SC, 5 months) reduced htTKV growth in HFD-fed Pkd1RC/RC mice (+1.5% vs +14.9%, p=0.02) but not ConD mice. Endothelial function restored in ConD mice only. Weight loss appears to mediate kidney benefit on HFD. Antioxidant experiments implicate oxidative stress in vascular protection. Abstract-only, conference proceedings.
papers.what_happened: An APS 2026 conference abstract reported that semaglutide reduced htTKV growth in high-fat diet–fed Pkd1RC/RC mice (+1.5% vs +14.9%, p=0.02) but had no kidney volume effect in normal-fat diet mice, suggesting the anti-cystic benefit tracks adiposity reduction rather than direct GLP-1 RA action.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides preclinical context for the ongoing tirzepatide Phase 2 RCT (NCT06582875) and raises the hypothesis that GLP-1 RA kidney benefits in ADPKD may require an obese/high-fat phenotype.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract-only APS conference presentation, mouse model only, diet-dependent effect suggests weight loss may be the primary mediator rather than GLP-1 RA–specific mechanisms, and ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: Urinary biomarkers of tubular injury and inflammation in ADPKD patients under tolvaptan therapy.
papers.abstract_snippet: Single-center cross-sectional study of 80 adult ADPKD patients on tolvaptan evaluating urinary biomarkers (BMG, MCP-1, KIM-1, NGAL) and their association with disease severity markers including eGFR slope, Mayo Imaging Classification, and htTKV.
papers.novelty_assessment: New biomarker study in tolvaptan-treated patients; adds to monitoring literature but no control arm
key_findings: Urinary BMG, MCP-1, KIM-1, NGAL assessed in 80 ADPKD patients on tolvaptan
Biomarkers associated with Mayo class and eGFR slope
Cross-sectional design; all patients already on tolvaptan
papers.clinical_implications: Exploratory only; biomarkers may reflect tolvaptan's aquaretic tubular effects rather than disease modification; not actionable without prospective validation
papers.what_happened: A single-center cross-sectional study of 80 ADPKD patients on tolvaptan found urinary biomarkers (BMG, MCP-1, KIM-1, NGAL) to be associated with markers of disease severity including Mayo Imaging Classification and eGFR slope.
papers.why_it_matters: If validated prospectively, urinary tubular injury and inflammation markers could provide additional monitoring tools for tolvaptan-treated patients beyond eGFR and TKV.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; no untreated comparator (all patients on tolvaptan, so biomarker elevations may partly reflect aquaretic tubular effects of the drug rather than disease progression); single Romanian center; n=80 is modest for biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Native nephrectomy in relation to kidney transplantation in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease patients; a narrative review of the literature.
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review examining timing of native nephrectomy (pre-transplant, post-transplant, or simultaneous) in ADPKD patients requiring kidney transplantation. Reviews evidence on unilateral vs bilateral nephrectomy and outcomes, based on papers published in the last 10 years.
papers.novelty_assessment: Synthesizes recent nephrectomy-transplant literature; no new primary data; complements pm_42012776 (Helal Birjandi retrospective n=124) already in DB
key_findings: Narrative review of 10-year literature on native nephrectomy timing in ADPKD transplant recipients
Addresses pre-transplant, simultaneous, and post-transplant timing options
Addresses unilateral vs bilateral nephrectomy debate
papers.clinical_implications: Background synthesis for transplant teams; does not add new primary evidence to resolve the timing debate

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None apparent; UK academic surgery group

papers.what_happened: A narrative review from a UK urology group synthesized 10 years of literature on the timing and approach of native nephrectomy (pre-, peri-, or post-transplant; unilateral vs bilateral) in ADPKD patients requiring kidney transplantation.
papers.why_it_matters: Timing of native nephrectomy in ADPKD transplant candidates remains debated; a current synthesis is useful for transplant program planning even though it does not resolve the debate with new data.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review only — no systematic search, no meta-analysis, no new primary data; conclusions are limited by the quality of the underlying heterogeneous literature.

papers.title: The Role of Mitochondria in Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review synthesizing evidence on mitochondrial dysfunction in PKD: metabolic reprogramming, oxidative stress, redox homeostasis, and inflammation as mitochondria-mediated disease drivers. Covers both ADPKD and ARPKD aspects.
papers.novelty_assessment: Narrative review synthesizing mitochondrial mechanisms; connects to the ketogenic/metabolic reprogramming angle but no new primary data
key_findings: Reviews mitochondrial dysfunction as a driver of PKD pathogenesis
Covers metabolic reprogramming, oxidative stress, and redox imbalance in cyst epithelia
Contextualizes mitochondria-targeted therapies as research direction
papers.clinical_implications: Background reading; supports the metabolic reprogramming research theme but no clinical inference warranted from a review
papers.what_happened: A narrative review in IJMS (May 26, 2026) synthesized current evidence on mitochondrial dysfunction as a pathogenic driver in PKD, covering metabolic reprogramming, oxidative stress, and redox dysregulation in cyst-lining epithelia.
papers.why_it_matters: Mitochondria-focused synthesis is relevant to the growing metabolic reprogramming theme in ADPKD research (connected to ketogenic diet, BHB, and mTOR/AMPK pathway work), providing a mechanistic framework for this line of investigation.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no new primary data and no systematic search; covers both ADPKD and ARPKD without always distinguishing them; translation of mitochondria-targeted insights to clinical ADPKD interventions remains speculative.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of tolvaptan in rapidly progressing autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a single-center, prospective, single-arm study
papers.abstract_snippet: Single-center prospective single-arm study in Chinese patients with rapidly progressing ADPKD evaluating tolvaptan efficacy and safety on kidney volume and kidney function. Chinese patient cohort addressing regulatory and efficacy gap in Asian populations.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds to Chinese tolvaptan real-world data (see also pm_41774609 retrospective n=83); single-arm, stale
key_findings: Prospective single-arm study of tolvaptan in Chinese rapidly progressing ADPKD
Evaluates kidney volume and function outcomes
Data from a population with limited prior tolvaptan evidence
papers.clinical_implications: Exploratory; single-arm study without comparator cannot establish efficacy; adds to real-world safety data in Chinese patients
papers.what_happened: A prospective single-arm study evaluated tolvaptan efficacy and safety on kidney volume and function in Chinese patients with rapidly progressing ADPKD at a single center.
papers.why_it_matters: Tolvaptan data from Chinese populations are limited due to historical regulatory gaps; this adds to real-world tolerability and response data for this group.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-arm study with no comparator group prevents efficacy conclusions; prospective design without randomization; single Chinese center limits generalizability; publication in Translational Andrology and Urology (an unusual venue for ADPKD) warrants scrutiny; indexed >14 days after publication (stale event).

papers.title: Ivermectin ameliorates cyst progression in polycystic kidney disease rats and renal cell-derived cysts via suppression of chloride secretion
papers.abstract_snippet: Preclinical study: daily subcutaneous ivermectin (0.5 mg/kg for 12 weeks) in PKD rats reduced kidney-to-body weight ratio and improved renal function vs controls. Ivermectin as FXR agonist; inhibits chloride secretion, extending pm_41758537 FXR/TMEM16A story.
papers.novelty_assessment: Extends FXR/TMEM16A story (pm_41758537 in DB); ivermectin as FXR agonist is novel angle but PKD subtype unclear and no date
key_findings: Ivermectin (0.5 mg/kg SC, 12 weeks) reduced kidney/body weight ratio in PKD rats
Proposed mechanism: FXR agonism suppressing chloride secretion via TMEM16A inhibition
In vitro confirmation in renal cell-derived cysts
papers.clinical_implications: Preclinical only; PKD rat model subtype (ADPKD vs ARPKD) not confirmed; prior ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation record is poor; ivermectin has significant systemic toxicity at higher doses; no human relevance established
papers.what_happened: A preclinical study in PKD rats found that daily subcutaneous ivermectin (0.5 mg/kg for 12 weeks) reduced the kidney-to-body weight ratio and improved renal function, proposing FXR agonism and downstream TMEM16A chloride secretion inhibition as the mechanism.
papers.why_it_matters: Ivermectin's FXR agonism provides an additional experimental hook for the FXR/TMEM16A cyst fluid secretion pathway (extending pm_41758537); drug repurposing angle is of theoretical interest.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical rat model only with unclear PKD subtype (ADPKD vs ARPKD not confirmed); no date of publication; Pharmaceutical Sciences Asia is an obscure venue; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation is historically poor; ivermectin's systemic toxicity profile at anti-cyst doses is not addressed.

papers.title: HIF-Regulated Pannexin-1 Channel Drives Luminal ATP Accumulation in Kidney Cysts
papers.abstract_snippet: HIF-1alpha upregulates Pannexin-1 (ATP-release channel) in cyst-lining epithelial cells; Pannexin-1 localizes apically in human and murine ADPKD cyst tissue. Apical ATP release is elevated in PKD1-deficient cells on HIF-1alpha induction and attenuated by Probenecid and BB-FCF. HIF-dependent cyst growth in vitro inhibited by Probenecid (cell-permeable) basally and BB-FCF (cell-impermeable) luminally.
papers.novelty_assessment: First demonstration that HIF-1alpha-regulated Pannexin-1 mediates directional ATP release into ADPKD cyst lumen; Probenecid (FDA-approved, used for gout) attenuates this in vitro.
key_findings: Pannexin-1 is localized at the apical membrane of cysts in human and murine ADPKD kidney tissue
HIF-1alpha induces Pannexin-1 expression in kidney tubular cells
Pharmacological HIF-1alpha induction elevates apical ATP release in PKD1-deficient cyst-forming cells
Two Pannexin-1 inhibitors (Probenecid, BB-FCF) attenuate elevated ATP release
HIF-dependent cyst growth in vitro is inhibited by Probenecid (basolateral) and BB-FCF (luminal)
papers.clinical_implications: Purely preclinical. Probenecid is clinically available but this is a mechanism paper only; no in vivo cyst size outcome or ADPKD animal model progression data. ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation record is poor. Pannexin-1/purinergic signaling is a hypothesis-generating target.
papers.what_happened: A preclinical study identified HIF-1alpha-regulated Pannexin-1 channels as the mechanism for ATP accumulation in ADPKD cyst fluid, with Pannexin-1 confirmed at the apical membrane of human and murine ADPKD cysts, and two inhibitors (Probenecid, BB-FCF) attenuating elevated ATP release in PKD1-deficient cells.
papers.why_it_matters: HIF-1alpha/Pannexin-1/ATP purinergic signaling is a mechanistically coherent pathway for cyst fluid secretion, and Probenecid (an FDA-approved gout drug) served as one of the inhibitors tested.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In vitro mechanistic study only, no in vivo cyst growth outcome in an ADPKD animal model; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation is historically poor; these findings need validation in vivo before any translational inference.

papers.title: CRISPR activation of endogenous PKD1 increases polycystin-1 levels and suppresses cellular features of ADPKD
papers.abstract_snippet: bioRxiv preprint. CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) targeting endogenous PKD1 reported to increase polycystin-1 levels and suppress cellular features of ADPKD in a cell model. Abstract not available in SS record.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds a new preprint to the growing CRISPRa/PKD1-upregulation literature (related to pm_42068455 mini-CRISPRa); supports the wild-type allele upregulation strategy being pursued by VX-407 and RNA-based approaches.
key_findings: CRISPRa targeting of endogenous PKD1 reported to increase polycystin-1 levels in cell model
Cellular features of ADPKD reported as suppressed
papers.clinical_implications: Preclinical preprint only; no abstract or methods available in this record. Supports the hypothesis that upregulating the wild-type PKD1 allele can suppress cystogenesis, a concept being clinically pursued via small-molecule correctors (VX-407 NCT07161037) and RNA-based approaches (PYC-003 NCT06714006). ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation record is poor.
papers.what_happened: A bioRxiv preprint reports that CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) of the endogenous PKD1 allele increases polycystin-1 levels and suppresses cellular features of ADPKD in a cell model.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds independent preprint-level evidence for the CRISPRa/PKD1-upregulation strategy, complementing the mini-CRISPRa work (pm_42068455) and the VX-407 small-molecule corrector now in Phase 2a (NCT07161037).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint with no abstract or methods available in this record; preclinical cell model only; no in vivo data; preprints are not peer-reviewed; ADPKD preclinical-to-clinical translation record is historically poor.

papers.title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy to Assess the Intrarenal Microvasculature in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Prospective n=17 young (<40y) early-stage ADPKD (eGFR>90) vs n=17 age/sex-matched controls. Super-resolution ULM reliably quantified intrarenal microvasculature; ICC 0.96. Microvascular parameters (vessel density, tortuosity) differed between ADPKD and controls despite preserved eGFR. Cortical vessel density correlated with eGFR; tortuosity indices inversely correlated. JASN June 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: First published study applying ULM super-resolution ultrasound to ADPKD microvasculature assessment; promising non-invasive biomarker of preclinical parenchymal damage.
key_findings: ULM safely and reproducibly assessed intrarenal microvasculature in early-stage ADPKD (n=17 vs 17 controls)
Microvascular parameters (vessel density, tortuosity) differed between ADPKD and controls despite preserved eGFR>90
Cortical vessel density correlated directly with eGFR; tortuosity inversely correlated
High reproducibility: ICC 0.96, day-to-day CoV 1.8-10.7%
papers.clinical_implications: Proof-of-concept for ULM as a non-invasive biomarker of microvascular remodeling in early ADPKD; small sample (n=17), cross-sectional only, no longitudinal validation; requires larger prospective studies before clinical adoption.
papers.what_happened: Super-resolution ultrasound localization microscopy reliably quantified intrarenal microvascular parameters (vessel density, tortuosity) in early-stage ADPKD patients (eGFR>90, n=17) and age-matched controls, finding microvascular differences despite preserved kidney function.
papers.why_it_matters: Microvascular rarefaction in early ADPKD may be a detectable biomarker of parenchymal damage before eGFR declines; ULM is non-invasive and avoids biopsy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cross-sectional single-centre study with n=17 only; no longitudinal follow-up to validate ULM parameters as progression markers; clinical utility unproven beyond proof-of-concept.

papers.title: Association of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease With Incident Aortic Dissection or Aneurysm
papers.abstract_snippet: Observational cohort n=2,568,283 (Japanese nationwide DeSC database 2014-2023), 1,102 ADPKD by ICD-10. HR 1.76 (95%CI 1.13-2.73) for incident aortic dissection or aneurysm combined; HR 2.53 (1.13-5.66) specifically for dissection; HR 1.56 (0.94-2.60) for aneurysm (CI crosses 1). Association stronger in BMI>=25. AJKD June 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Large-scale Japanese database study providing population-level HR estimates for aortic disease in ADPKD; the dissection signal (HR 2.53) is notable, though aortic aneurysm alone does not reach significance.
key_findings: 2.57M-person Japanese nationwide cohort; 1,102 ADPKD by ICD-10 code
ADPKD associated with HR 1.76 (95%CI 1.13-2.73) for combined aortic dissection or aneurysm
Stronger signal for aortic dissection: HR 2.53 (1.13-5.66)
Aortic aneurysm alone: HR 1.56 (0.94-2.60, CI crosses 1, not independently significant)
Association stronger in BMI≥25 subgroup
papers.clinical_implications: Supports awareness of aortic disease risk in ADPKD patients, particularly for dissection; however, ICD-10 code ADPKD identification may be inaccurate, and the AA signal alone does not reach significance. Does not change surveillance guidelines without replication in Western cohorts.
papers.what_happened: A large Japanese nationwide administrative database study (2.57M individuals, n=1,102 ADPKD by ICD-10) found ADPKD associated with 76% higher risk of incident aortic dissection or aneurysm (HR 1.76), with a stronger signal for aortic dissection (HR 2.53) than aneurysm (HR 1.56, non-significant alone).
papers.why_it_matters: Provides the largest epidemiological estimate to date for aortic disease risk in ADPKD, potentially informing clinical surveillance practices and multidisciplinary management.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective design, ICD-10 code ADPKD identification without genetic or imaging confirmation, ADPKD n=1,102 is small relative to the total cohort, no data on PKD genotype, aortic aneurysm HR alone does not reach significance, Japanese population may not generalise to other populations.

papers.title: Kidney Volume and Molecular Processes are Dynamic in ADPKD
papers.abstract_snippet: Kidney volume changes by Mayo class and age were determined in a large well-characterized ADPKD cohort with long follow-up. Rate of kidney volume growth differs between classes and age stages, with the predominant biological processes varying dynamically across disease progression. KI Reports June 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Deepens understanding of cyst growth rate heterogeneity across Mayo classes; limited novelty relative to existing TKV literature.
key_findings: Rate of kidney volume growth differs between Mayo Imaging Classes and age stages
Predominant biological processes vary dynamically across ADPKD progression
papers.clinical_implications: Adds nuance to Mayo Imaging Classification interpretation; does not change current clinical practice. Context for interpreting TKV trajectories in clinical trials.
papers.what_happened: A large well-characterized ADPKD cohort study characterised the dynamic relationship between kidney volume growth rates and molecular processes across Mayo Imaging Classes and age stages.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides granular data on progression heterogeneity across disease stages, potentially relevant for clinical trial endpoint selection and stratification.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract describes a descriptive study; molecular process data likely from biomarker/transcriptomic correlates without experimental validation; KI Reports June print issue but online since February 2026.

papers.title: Molecular genetic diagnosis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease - A systematic review
papers.abstract_snippet: PRISMA systematic review. 23,718 records screened; 20 studies met inclusion criteria (>=30 clinically diagnosed ADPKD, patient-level diagnostic data). Jan 2015-Aug 2025. Reviewed testing methods, diagnostic yield, and identified genes across methods (WES, panel, Sanger, long-read).
papers.novelty_assessment: Systematic synthesis of genetic diagnostic yield across ADPKD testing methods; useful reference but likely confirms existing knowledge.
key_findings: Systematic review of 20 studies with patient-level genetic diagnostic data (Jan 2015-Aug 2025)
Reviewed testing methods, diagnostic yield, and gene identification across WES, panel, and other approaches
papers.clinical_implications: Useful synthesis for diagnostic labs choosing sequencing strategy; does not introduce new data. Context for interpreting diagnostic yield claims.
papers.what_happened: A PRISMA systematic review of 20 studies assessed molecular genetic diagnostic methods and yield in clinically diagnosed ADPKD, covering publications from 2015 to August 2025.
papers.why_it_matters: Synthesises comparative diagnostic yield across sequencing methods (NGS panel, WES, long-read) relevant for diagnostic labs and genetic counselling practices.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Published in Global Medical Genetics, a journal without established ADPKD editorial track record; full methods and yield data not available in abstract; likely confirms rather than challenges existing literature.

papers.title: Toward Physiologically Relevant Organoid Models of Polycystic Kidney Disease through Microenvironment Reconstruction
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Perspective/review on reconstructing the PKD tissue microenvironment (cyst-lining epithelial, stromal, and immune cells + systemic factors) in organoid models. Argues this is essential to elucidate PKD pathogenesis mechanisms and develop effective therapeutics. JASN June 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Perspective piece advocating for more complex organoid models; adds context to the existing ADPKD organoid field (related to pm_41946363 and other organoid papers in DB).
key_findings: Argues for reconstructing the full PKD tissue microenvironment (epithelial, stromal, immune, systemic) in organoids
Current organoid models lack physiological complexity that may be critical for therapeutic target validation
papers.clinical_implications: Review perspective only; no new data. Sets research agenda for next-generation ADPKD organoid models. Low clinical decision usefulness.
papers.what_happened: A JASN perspective argued that existing PKD organoid models lack the microenvironmental complexity (epithelial-stromal-immune interactions, systemic factors) needed for physiologically relevant therapeutic target validation.
papers.why_it_matters: Frames the current limitations of ADPKD preclinical organoid models and sets an agenda for more complex systems that may better predict clinical translation.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Perspective/review with no new experimental data; published online January 2026 — available for months before JASN June print.

papers.title: Unrecognized Biases and Validation Gaps in TraceOrg for Automated Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Volumetry
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Letter to JASN raising concerns about unrecognized biases and validation gaps in TraceOrg, the automated TKV web tool (pm_41186985 in DB). No abstract available. JASN June 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Letter raising methodological concerns about TraceOrg; companion to pm_41186985 (TraceOrg paper) in DB; adds nuance to automated TKV measurement reliability.
key_findings: Letter raising concerns about unrecognized biases and validation gaps in TraceOrg automated TKV tool
papers.clinical_implications: Relevant for labs using or considering TraceOrg for clinical TKV measurement; raises caution about uncritical adoption.
papers.what_happened: A JASN letter raised concerns about unrecognized biases and validation gaps in TraceOrg, the automated TKV measurement web tool validated in pm_41186985.
papers.why_it_matters: TraceOrg is being promoted as a clinical-grade automated TKV tool; methodological concerns are relevant to users and clinical trial endpoints relying on automated volumetry.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Letter format only with no abstract available; specific biases and gaps not quantifiable from this record.

papers.title: Author's Reply: Unrecognized Biases and Validation Gaps in TraceOrg for Automated Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Volumetry
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Author reply to pm_41563366 letter on TraceOrg biases. No abstract available. JASN June 2026 print issue.

key_findings: Author reply to letter challenging TraceOrg automated TKV tool (pm_41563366)

papers.what_happened: Author reply to the letter challenging TraceOrg automated TKV measurement tool (pm_41563366).
papers.why_it_matters: Completes the TraceOrg debate; see pm_41563366 for the substantive concern.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Reply letter format; no abstract; no new data.

papers.title: Generation of a human-induced pluripotent stem cell line (NUMNi003-A) from a patient with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease harboring a PKD1 gene variant
papers.abstract_snippet: iPSC generation from ADPKD patient with PKD1 variant. Cells expressed stem cell markers and could differentiate into all three germ layers. Intended for studying PKD1 variant mechanisms. Research resource paper; no disease modeling data in this publication.
papers.novelty_assessment: Standard iPSC resource generation paper; adds to the pool of ADPKD iPSC lines but contains no disease modeling data.
key_findings: iPSC line NUMNi003-A generated from ADPKD patient with PKD1 variant
Cells expressed stem cell markers and could differentiate into 3 germ layers
papers.clinical_implications: Research resource only; no disease modeling or therapeutic data in this publication.
papers.what_happened: Researchers generated an iPSC line (NUMNi003-A) from an ADPKD patient with a PKD1 variant; the cells were characterised for stem cell markers and pluripotency.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to available ADPKD iPSC resources for studying PKD1 variant-specific mechanisms and potential drug screening.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Resource/characterisation paper only; no disease phenotype or cystogenesis data reported in this publication.

papers.title: Deciphering the Cell-Specific Specificity of the α-Klotho-Cellular Inhibitor of Apoptosis Protein 1 Axis in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Letter commenting on cell-type specificity of the α-Klotho/cIAP1 axis study (pm_41563399 in DB). No abstract. JASN June 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Letter addressing cell-specificity of α-Klotho/cIAP1 axis (companion to pm_41563399 in DB).
key_findings: Letter on cell-type specificity of the alpha-Klotho/cIAP1 axis in ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: No clinical implications; addresses mechanistic interpretation of pm_41563399.
papers.what_happened: A letter commented on the cell-type specificity of the alpha-Klotho/cIAP1 axis finding from pm_41563399 (alpha-Klotho TNF-cIAP1 Pkd1 mouse study, JASN May 2026).
papers.why_it_matters: Companion to pm_41563399; contributes nuance to mechanistic interpretation of the alpha-Klotho/cIAP1 pathway in ADPKD.

papers.title: Authors' Reply: Deciphering the Cell-Specific Specificity of the α-Klotho-Cellular Inhibitor of Apoptosis Protein 1 Axis in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Author reply to pm_41615725 letter on alpha-Klotho/cIAP1 axis cell specificity. No abstract. JASN June 2026 print issue.

key_findings: Authors' reply to letter on alpha-Klotho/cIAP1 axis (pm_41615725, companion to pm_41563399)
