papers.title: Health-related quality of life in people with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a systematic review.
papers.abstract_snippet: Systematic review (Medline, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Web of Science + Google Scholar) of HRQoL in ADPKD by CKD stage and KRT modality. Studies Jan 2014 - Oct 2024. Generic, kidney-specific, and ADPKD-specific PROMs; scores adjusted to population norms.
papers.novelty_assessment: First systematic review synthesizing HRQoL data across all CKD stages and KRT modalities in ADPKD; standardizes comparison using population norms.
key_findings: Systematic synthesis of HRQoL evidence in ADPKD by disease stage and KRT modality
Uses five databases including ADPKD-specific PROMs
Population-norm-adjusted comparisons across CKD stages
papers.clinical_implications: Provides evidence base for patient counseling about disease-stage-specific QoL expectations; may inform PRO selection in future ADPKD trials.
papers.what_happened: Gittus et al. published a systematic review synthesizing HRQoL data across all CKD stages and KRT modalities in ADPKD, using five databases and population-norm-adjusted PROM scores.
papers.why_it_matters: HRQoL data stratified by disease stage and treatment modality are scarce in ADPKD; this synthesis informs patient counseling and PRO selection in future trials.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Quality of the review depends on the methodological heterogeneity of included primary studies; PROMs differ across studies, limiting cross-study comparisons.

papers.title: Arterial stiffness and choroidal vascularity index in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with preserved kidney function.
papers.abstract_snippet: Single-center, cross-sectional study; n=41 ADPKD patients with eGFR>60 and n=40 age/sex-matched controls. Arterial stiffness assessed by cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI). Choroidal vascularity index (CVI) measured by spectral-domain OCT. Correlation analyses of vascular and ocular parameters.
papers.novelty_assessment: Novel combination of systemic arterial stiffness (CAVI) and choroidal vascularity index (OCT) in ADPKD with preserved kidney function; extends vascular phenotyping beyond renal endpoints.
key_findings: ADPKD patients with preserved kidney function (eGFR>60) show differences in arterial stiffness and choroidal vascularity compared to controls
Single-center cross-sectional study, n=41 ADPKD vs n=40 controls
Correlation between systemic and ocular vascular parameters explored
papers.clinical_implications: No immediate clinical implications; may inform future biomarker studies of early vascular involvement in ADPKD. Hypothesis-generating.
papers.what_happened: Mert et al. compared arterial stiffness (CAVI) and choroidal vascularity index (OCT) in 41 ADPKD patients with preserved kidney function versus 40 matched controls in a single-center cross-sectional study.
papers.why_it_matters: Early vascular involvement in ADPKD before overt kidney function decline is clinically relevant; this adds an ocular microvascular dimension to the vascular phenotype.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small sample (n=81 total), single-center, cross-sectional design, and surrogate endpoints only — no longitudinal follow-up, no clinical outcomes, no TKV data.

papers.title: Serum and urine prognostic biomarkers for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract_snippet: SR/MA of 58 studies; 33 urinary and 29 serum/blood prognostic biomarkers in ADPKD evaluated. Most frequently studied: urine osmolality, copeptin, proteinuria, MCP-1, uric acid. Most studied outcomes: eGFR and TKV. GRADE approach used. Cochrane/Embase/PubMed search to April 2025; longitudinal studies >=10 participants >=1 year follow-up included.
papers.novelty_assessment: Most comprehensive SR/MA of ADPKD prognostic biomarkers to date; GRADE-rated evidence for 62 biomarkers across 58 studies; provides a synthesis reference for trial design and patient stratification.
key_findings: 58 studies included; 33 urinary and 29 serum/blood biomarkers evaluated
Most studied biomarkers: urine osmolality, copeptin, proteinuria, MCP-1, uric acid
Most studied outcomes: eGFR and TKV (both surrogates)
GRADE approach applied to rate certainty of evidence
PubMed, Embase, Cochrane search up to April 2025
papers.clinical_implications: Synthesis resource for biomarker selection in clinical trials and patient management. Does not introduce novel biomarkers; consolidates and grades existing evidence. Most studied biomarkers (copeptin, osmolality) are already incorporated into KDIGO 2025 guidance.
papers.what_happened: Khawandi et al. published a GRADE-rated systematic review and meta-analysis in BMC Nephrology synthesizing prognostic biomarker evidence from 58 ADPKD studies, covering 33 urinary and 29 serum biomarkers.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides the most comprehensive GRADE-rated evidence synthesis of ADPKD prognostic biomarkers to date, potentially guiding clinical trial design and patient stratification.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The synthesis quality is bounded by the observational and heterogeneous nature of the underlying studies, and all identified biomarkers remain surrogates rather than patient-important endpoints.

papers.title: RENAL DENERVATION IN PATIENTS WITH AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE: FIRST RESULTS FROM THE RANDOMIZED RDN-ADPKD STUDY
papers.abstract_snippet: ESH 2026 Congress abstract (J Hypertension supplement). First results from the randomized RDN-ADPKD study (NCT05460169). Renal denervation for hypertension in ADPKD patients. No abstract text available — title only.
papers.novelty_assessment: First conference disclosure of results from the randomized phase of NCT05460169 (RDN-ADPKD study); no data available from abstract-only indexing.
key_findings: ESH 2026 abstract: 'First results from the randomized RDN-ADPKD study'
No abstract text or data available — title-only disclosure
papers.clinical_implications: Cannot assess until full data are available. Renal denervation for BP management in ADPKD is a distinct mechanistic question from disease progression.
papers.what_happened: Schmieder et al. (Erlangen group, NCT05460169 investigators) presented 'first results' from the randomized RDN-ADPKD study at ESH 2026 as a J Hypertension supplement abstract.
papers.why_it_matters: NCT05460169 is the primary randomized trial of renal denervation for hypertension in ADPKD; any results disclosure is a tracked milestone for hypertension management in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract text or data are available; this is a title-only discovery from SS indexing — results cannot be evaluated without the full abstract or publication.

papers.title: Nature and Nurture? The Case of Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
papers.abstract_snippet: CJASN editorial/perspective; no abstract available.
papers.novelty_assessment: CJASN editorial with no abstract available; likely commenting on genetics-environment interplay in PKD.
key_findings: No abstract available; editorial/perspective piece
papers.clinical_implications: Cannot assess without full text.
papers.what_happened: Cobiellas Carballo and Heung published a CJASN editorial on genetics/environment interactions in polycystic kidney disease.
papers.why_it_matters: CJASN editorial format suggests commentary on a related study; editorial opinion is not independently practice-changing.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract available; editorial opinion without primary data.

papers.title: Successful use of dupilumab in a patient with atopic dermatitis and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a case report.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report of dupilumab (anti-IL-4/IL-13) for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in a patient with ADPKD. No adverse renal effects observed.
papers.novelty_assessment: Minimal ADPKD-specific scientific relevance; reports dupilumab use in a comorbid patient without ADPKD-specific outcome.
key_findings: Dupilumab appears safe in a single ADPKD patient with atopic dermatitis; no adverse renal effects
papers.clinical_implications: No ADPKD-specific clinical implications; single case report in a non-ADPKD-focused journal.
papers.what_happened: A case report in Dermatology Reports describes successful dupilumab use in a patient with comorbid atopic dermatitis and ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides minimal safety signal for dupilumab in an ADPKD patient; no disease-specific findings.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report with no ADPKD-specific outcome measures; no renal-specific endpoints or follow-up.

papers.title: Methodological limitations in assessing ADPKD-scoliosis association: a critical appraisal.
papers.abstract_snippet: Critical appraisal letter discussing methodological limitations in prior work assessing ADPKD-scoliosis association. No abstract available.
papers.novelty_assessment: Methodological critique letter; minimal direct scientific contribution to ADPKD management or treatment.
key_findings: Critical appraisal of methodological limitations; no primary data
papers.clinical_implications: No clinical implications for ADPKD disease management or treatment.
papers.what_happened: A letter published in Int Urol Nephrol critically appraises methodological limitations in prior work on the ADPKD-scoliosis association.
papers.why_it_matters: Not material to ADPKD disease management or treatment pipeline.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract; letter format without primary data.

papers.title: Canadian Society of Nephrology Commentary on the 2025 Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes Clinical Practice Guidelines for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Canadian Journal of Kidney Health and Disease
papers.abstract_snippet: Canadian Society of Nephrology commentary providing a national perspective on the KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline. A committee of adult/pediatric nephrologists, a genetic counselor, and a patient partner (with an Indigenous perspective) surveyed key practice points and commented with Canadian nuance on multidisciplinary care, challenges with genetic testing, and use of CKD therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors in ADPKD. Relied on KDIGO evidence summaries; did not replicate or update systematic reviews.
papers.novelty_assessment: Regional (Canadian) adaptation/commentary on the existing KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline; no new evidence generated. Follows the same pattern as prior KDOQI US (pm_41864657) and CARI AU/NZ (pm_42011799) commentaries already tracked.
key_findings: Provides Canadian-specific practice nuance on the KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline
Emphasizes multidisciplinary care, genetic-testing access challenges, and SGLT2 inhibitor use in ADPKD
Built on KDIGO evidence summaries via expert survey/consensus; systematic reviews not updated
papers.clinical_implications: Supports guideline implementation for Canadian practitioners; limited direct relevance outside Canada and adds no new disease-specific evidence.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Multiple panel members report speaker/advisory fees from Otsuka, Bayer, GSK, Amgen, AstraZeneca, Novartis, Lupin and others; consensus commentary, no new trial data.

papers.what_happened: The Canadian Society of Nephrology published a commentary giving a Canadian perspective on the KDIGO 2025 ADPKD clinical practice guideline.
papers.why_it_matters: It helps Canadian clinicians apply the global KDIGO 2025 ADPKD recommendations to local practice (genetic testing access, SGLT2 inhibitor use, multidisciplinary care).
papers.what_limits_confidence: It is an expert consensus commentary that did not update the underlying systematic reviews and adds no new evidence; relevance is region-specific and many authors disclose industry ties.

papers.title: Collecting Duct-Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles Deliver Pkd2 mRNA to Restore Polycystin-2 and Attenuate ADPKD
papers.abstract_snippet: Preprint: collecting duct-targeted lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) deliver Pkd2 mRNA to restore polycystin-2 expression and attenuate cyst expansion in a preclinical ADPKD model, addressing the renal-epithelial delivery barrier for gene-replacement therapy. Preclinical only; PKD2-directed.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (preprint posted 2026-06-05). Novel modality: kidney-collecting-duct-targeted LNP delivery of Pkd2 mRNA for direct polycystin restoration. Preclinical proof-of-concept only.
key_findings: Collecting-duct-targeted LNPs delivered Pkd2 mRNA and restored polycystin-2 in a preclinical ADPKD model
Reported attenuation of cyst expansion (surrogate/mechanistic readout)
Aims to address the renal-epithelial delivery barrier that limits ADPKD gene therapy
papers.clinical_implications: No near-term clinical implication; preclinical proof-of-concept for direct gene/mRNA replacement targeting the PKD2 defect. ADPKD has a historically poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.
papers.what_happened: A bioRxiv preprint (June 5, 2026) reports collecting-duct-targeted lipid nanoparticles delivering Pkd2 mRNA to restore polycystin-2 and reduce cyst burden in a preclinical ADPKD model.
papers.why_it_matters: It is an early proof-of-concept for directly correcting the underlying polycystin deficiency via targeted mRNA delivery, addressing the renal-epithelial delivery barrier that has limited ADPKD gene therapy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Non-peer-reviewed preprint with preclinical-only data, PKD2-directed (covers a minority of ADPKD), no durability/safety data, and ADPKD's historically poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record; the title 'Attenuate ADPKD' overstates what an animal cyst-burden readout supports.

papers.title: Disruption of Polycystin-1 Cleavage Impairs Mitochondrial Bioenergetics and Calcium Uptake in a Substrate-Dependent Manner.
papers.journal: American Journal of Physiology. Renal Physiology
papers.abstract_snippet: In male Pkd1V/V mice (orthologous point variant at the polycystin-1 GPS cleavage site), isolated kidney mitochondria showed reduced oxygen consumption and calcium retention with NADH-generating substrates (but not succinate), decreased complex I/III/V subunits, and lower calcium-homeostasis proteins (VDAC1, MCU, MICU1/2, NCLX). Mitochondrial mass markers were preserved or increased; redox/4-HNE unchanged at the mitochondrial level. Authors conclude cleaved PC1 is important for maintaining mitochondrial mass, integrity, and function.
papers.novelty_assessment: Adds mechanistic detail linking impaired PC1 GPS cleavage to substrate-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction in an orthologous mouse model; reinforces the metabolic/mitochondrial thesis of ADPKD but is a single preclinical study (male mice only) with no therapeutic readout.
key_findings: Pkd1V/V kidney mitochondria show reduced oxygen consumption and calcium retention with NADH-linked (complex I) substrates but not with succinate
Decreased levels of complex I/III/V subunits and calcium-handling proteins (VDAC1, MCU, MICU1/2, NCLX)
Mitochondrial mass markers preserved/increased and mitochondrial redox markers unchanged, suggesting functional rather than mass defect
papers.clinical_implications: None directly; supports continued interest in mitochondrial/metabolic pathways as potential ADPKD targets but is preclinical and mechanistic only.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Academic FAPESP funding; none apparent commercial.

papers.what_happened: In an orthologous Pkd1V/V mouse model, disrupted polycystin-1 GPS cleavage was associated with substrate-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction (reduced complex I-linked respiration and calcium uptake) and lower complex I/III/V and calcium-handling proteins.
papers.why_it_matters: It strengthens the mechanistic case that mitochondrial/metabolic dysfunction is downstream of polycystin-1 loss, a pathway several investigational ADPKD therapies aim to target.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical single-model study in male mice only with mechanistic/biochemical endpoints and no therapeutic or in-vivo disease-progression readout; ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: Anti-Polyamine Therapy Restrains Kidney Cyst Growth in an Orthologous Mouse Model of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Pkd1RC/RC mice treated for five months with DFMO (difluoromethylornithine/eflornithine, an FDA-approved irreversible ODC1 inhibitor) in drinking water showed significantly reduced percent kidney weight/body weight, cystic index, and cyst number versus controls. Kidney RNA-seq showed correction of many PKD-perturbed genes/pathways and healthier inferred cellular architecture. Authors propose repurposing DFMO and implicate polyamines in epithelial and myeloid (M2-like macrophage) cell fate in PKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: First report (preprint) that the FDA-approved ODC1 inhibitor DFMO slows cyst growth in a slow-progression orthologous ADPKD mouse model, providing a repurposing rationale and mechanistic link to polyamine metabolism; preclinical and not yet peer-reviewed.
key_findings: 5-month oral DFMO reduced kidney weight/body weight, cystic index, and cyst number in Pkd1RC/RC mice vs control
RNA-seq showed normalization of many PKD-perturbed pathways and inferred healthier cellular composition
Implicates polyamine synthesis in driving epithelial proliferation and M2-like macrophage fate in PKD
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests DFMO/eflornithine as a repurposing candidate worth further preclinical and eventual clinical evaluation in ADPKD; no human data and ADPKD preclinical signals frequently fail to translate.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not disclosed in preprint metadata; Vitek MP affiliation may carry commercial interest (to verify).

papers.what_happened: A bioRxiv preprint reports that the FDA-approved ODC1 inhibitor DFMO (eflornithine), given orally for five months, reduced kidney cyst burden and corrected PKD-perturbed transcriptional pathways in an orthologous Pkd1RC/RC ADPKD mouse model.
papers.why_it_matters: It offers a drug-repurposing rationale targeting polyamine metabolism, an already-approved compound that could in principle be moved toward clinical testing if the signal holds.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical, not-yet-peer-reviewed preprint with surrogate cyst-burden endpoints in mice only; ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record and no human efficacy or safety data exist for this indication.

papers.title: Thyroid Hormones Exhibit Promising Prognostic and Therapeutic Potential in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Patient-derived renal epithelial cells were used to engineer 3D polycystic tubules to test anti-cystogenic effects of thyroid hormones (THs). Thyroxine (T4) inhibited cyst growth by modulating proliferative, metabolic and ferroptotic pathways via avb3 integrin binding. In PCK rats, T4 decreased kidney weight and significantly reduced macrocystic area (Vehicle 9.255+/-2.654 vs T4 1.945+/-0.850). Authors propose THs as prognostic and therapeutic agents.
papers.novelty_assessment: First report implicating thyroid hormone signaling in ADPKD cystogenesis and proposing thyroxine as a multi-pathway anti-cystogenic agent in patient-derived 3D tubules plus a PCK rat model; entirely preclinical.
key_findings: Thyroxine reduced cyst formation in patient-derived 3D polycystic tubules in vitro
T4 acted via avb3 integrin binding, modulating proliferative, metabolic and ferroptotic pathways
In PCK rats, T4 reduced kidney weight and macrocystic area versus vehicle
papers.clinical_implications: Raises a mechanistic hypothesis and possible biomarker/stratification angle, but giving exogenous thyroxine carries cardiovascular and metabolic risks; far from clinical applicability and the PCK rat is a PKHD1 (ARPKD-type) model, not an orthologous PKD1 ADPKD model.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None apparent in abstract; not fully disclosed in metadata.

papers.what_happened: A preclinical study reports that thyroxine (T4) suppresses cyst growth in patient-derived 3D polycystic tubules and reduces macrocystic area in PCK rats, acting via avb3 integrin and proliferative/metabolic/ferroptotic pathways.
papers.why_it_matters: It identifies thyroid hormone signaling as a previously unexplored pathogenic and potentially druggable pathway in polycystic kidney disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Entirely preclinical (in vitro plus a PCK rat model that is a PKHD1/ARPKD-type model rather than an orthologous ADPKD model), surrogate cyst-burden endpoints only, the 'promising therapeutic potential' framing overstates a hypothesis, and exogenous thyroxine carries real clinical risks.

papers.title: The AT2 receptor as a potential target for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease therapy?
papers.abstract_snippet: Editorial / expert opinion proposing the angiotensin II type 2 (AT2) receptor as a candidate therapeutic target in ADPKD. No primary data presented.
papers.novelty_assessment: Opinion piece framing the AT2 receptor as a potential ADPKD target; conceptual, no new experimental data.
key_findings: Proposes AT2-receptor agonism as a hypothesis worth exploring in ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: None actionable; agenda-setting commentary only.
papers.what_happened: An expert-opinion editorial proposes the angiotensin II type 2 (AT2) receptor as a potential therapeutic target in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: It flags a possible RAS-related target for future preclinical investigation.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Opinion piece with no primary data; purely hypothesis-level and not practice-relevant.

papers.title: Total kidney volume and frailty severity in ADPKD: A pilot observation.
papers.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association
papers.abstract_snippet: Pilot observational letter reporting an association between total kidney volume (TKV) and frailty severity in patients with ADPKD. No abstract/full methods available (Letter).
papers.novelty_assessment: Small pilot letter linking TKV to frailty in ADPKD; preliminary and underpowered.
key_findings: Reports a cross-sectional association between higher TKV and greater frailty severity in ADPKD (pilot)
papers.clinical_implications: Hypothesis-generating only; cannot establish that kidney enlargement drives frailty.
papers.what_happened: A pilot observational letter reports a cross-sectional association between total kidney volume and frailty severity in patients with ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: It raises the possibility that imaging severity tracks with systemic frailty, of potential prognostic interest.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Pilot letter with no published methods, likely small sample, and a cross-sectional design that cannot separate correlation from causation or confounding by age/kidney function.

papers.title: Exploring urinary allantoin and adenosine in pediatric autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: no clear association with disease severity.
papers.abstract_snippet: Observational case-control study: 34 genotyped PKD1-ADPKD children (<18y, preserved function) vs 31 healthy controls. Urinary allantoin, adenosine and allantoin/uric-acid ratio did NOT differ between groups. Inverse correlations of allantoin with TKV (r=-0.49) but no correlation with LIC score, and a strong negative correlation with age, limiting biomarker utility.
papers.novelty_assessment: Largely negative pediatric biomarker study finding urinary allantoin/adenosine do not discriminate early PKD1-ADPKD from controls; appropriately cautious.
key_findings: Urinary allantoin, adenosine and allantoin/uric-acid ratio did not differ between pediatric ADPKD and controls
Allantoin inversely correlated with TKV (r=-0.49, p=0.004) but not with LIC score
Allantoin correlated strongly negatively with age, confounding its use as a severity marker
papers.clinical_implications: Argues against urinary allantoin/adenosine as standalone early-progression biomarkers in pediatric ADPKD; mainly prunes a candidate.
papers.what_happened: A case-control study (34 PKD1-ADPKD children vs 31 controls) found urinary allantoin, adenosine and the allantoin/uric-acid ratio did not differ between groups and showed only an age-confounded inverse correlation with total kidney volume.
papers.why_it_matters: It tempers enthusiasm for these oxidative-stress metabolites as non-invasive early-progression biomarkers in pediatric ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small single-center cross-sectional cohort with preserved kidney function; the one TKV correlation is confounded by age and absent against the LIC imaging score, so the negative conclusion itself is preliminary.

papers.title: Biallelic PKD1 mutations causing neonatal death in an extremely preterm infant: a Korean case report of very early-onset ADPKD.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report of very early-onset ADPKD: extremely preterm Korean infant with biallelic (compound heterozygous) PKD1 variants (truncating p.Tyr3781Ter + hypomorphic p.Phe1292Leu in trans), lethal at day 2, with paternal somatic mosaicism explaining mild paternal phenotype. Supports PGT for the couple.
papers.novelty_assessment: First Korean report of neonatal-lethal biallelic PKD1 VEO-ADPKD with documented paternal mosaicism; illustrative for counseling but a single rare case.
key_findings: Compound heterozygous PKD1 variants (truncating + hypomorphic, in trans) caused neonatal-lethal ADPKD phenocopying ARPKD
Paternal somatic mosaicism explained the discordant mild paternal phenotype and unpredictable recurrence risk
Supports preimplantation genetic testing for affected families
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces gene-dosage and mosaicism considerations in counseling families with severe perinatal cystic disease; not generalizable to typical adult ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes neonatal-lethal very early-onset ADPKD from biallelic PKD1 variants in trans, with paternal somatic mosaicism explaining the father's mild disease.
papers.why_it_matters: It illustrates gene-dosage and mosaicism mechanisms relevant to genetic counseling and recurrence-risk estimation in severe perinatal cystic disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case of a rare, non-typical genotype that phenocopies ARPKD; not generalizable to common adult ADPKD and provides no therapeutic insight.

papers.title: P-STAT3-dependent SPP1 transcription in cholangiocytes drives hepatic stellate cells activation in congenital hepatic fibrosis.
papers.abstract_snippet: Single-cell RNA-seq of a congenital hepatic fibrosis (CHF) patient with PKHD1 mutations plus a Pkhd1 knockout mouse implicate a p-STAT3 -> SPP1 -> integrin a8b1 cholangiocyte-to-hepatic-stellate-cell axis driving liver fibrosis. CHF is part of the ARPKD/PKHD1 spectrum.
papers.novelty_assessment: Mechanistic ARPKD/PKHD1-spectrum liver-fibrosis study; tangential to ADPKD and scored low per ARPKD handling rule.
key_findings: scRNA-seq implicates an SPP1-integrin a8b1 cholangiocyte-stellate signaling axis in CHF
p-STAT3 drives SPP1 transcription in cholangiocytes
Validated in a Pkhd1 knockout mouse model
papers.clinical_implications: Relevant to ARPKD/PKHD1-related liver disease, not ADPKD; no near-term clinical applicability.
papers.what_happened: A single-cell and mouse study identifies a p-STAT3/SPP1/integrin signaling axis between cholangiocytes and hepatic stellate cells driving fibrosis in PKHD1-related congenital hepatic fibrosis.
papers.why_it_matters: It clarifies a potentially druggable fibrosis mechanism within the broader polycystic/hepatic-disease spectrum.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This concerns PKHD1/ARPKD-spectrum liver disease rather than ADPKD, is entirely preclinical, and its findings may not transfer to autosomal dominant disease (scored low per ARPKD handling rule).

papers.title: GLUT9b- and ABCG2-mediated collecting duct urate transport uncover a vasopressin-independent mechanism of renal water reabsorption.
papers.abstract_snippet: Identifies intracellular urate (via apical GLUT9b uptake and reduced ABCG2 efflux) as a vasopressin-independent regulator of AQP2 apical trafficking through PDE4/cAMP/AMPK. In vivo ABCG2 inhibition with probenecid increased apical AQP2 and markedly attenuated tolvaptan-induced polyuria in WT and Pkd1RC/RC ADPKD mice while preserving tolvaptan's ADPKD-modifying (cyst-attenuating) efficacy. In a Phase 2 trial of tolvaptan-treated ADPKD patients, probenecid reduced urine volume and nocturia frequency.
papers.novelty_assessment: First description of a vasopressin-independent urate-AMPK-AQP2 pathway and a translational proof-of-concept (mice + a Phase 2 human signal) that probenecid can reduce tolvaptan's aquaretic burden (polyuria/nocturia) while, in mice, preserving cyst-attenuating efficacy.
key_findings: Intracellular urate accumulation (apical GLUT9b uptake, reduced ABCG2 efflux) drives apical AQP2 accumulation via PDE4/reduced-cAMP/AMPK, independent of V2R signaling
Probenecid (ABCG2 inhibition) attenuated tolvaptan-induced polyuria in WT and Pkd1RC/RC ADPKD mice while preserving tolvaptan's cyst-attenuating efficacy (preclinical)
In a Phase 2 trial of tolvaptan-treated ADPKD patients, probenecid reduced urine volume and nocturia frequency
papers.clinical_implications: Aquaresis (polyuria, nocturia) is the principal tolerability/adherence barrier for tolvaptan; an add-on that blunts polyuria without sacrificing efficacy could meaningfully improve real-world tolvaptan use, but the efficacy-preservation evidence is preclinical and the Phase 2 human data lack reported n/effect size/design detail in the abstract.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not fully disclosed in abstract; probenecid is a generic agent (lower commercial-product bias). JCI full disclosures in main text.

papers.what_happened: A JCI translational study reports a vasopressin-independent urate-AMPK-AQP2 water-reabsorption pathway and shows that the ABCG2 inhibitor probenecid attenuates tolvaptan-induced polyuria in ADPKD mice (while preserving cyst-attenuating efficacy) and reduced urine volume/nocturia in a Phase 2 trial of tolvaptan-treated ADPKD patients.
papers.why_it_matters: It offers a mechanistically grounded strategy to reduce tolvaptan's aquaretic burden, the main reason patients discontinue an otherwise disease-modifying therapy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The 'preserved efficacy' claim is demonstrated only in mice (ADPKD has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record), and the supporting Phase 2 human data are described without reported sample size, effect magnitude, or trial design in the abstract.

papers.title: A pilot study of magnetic resonance fingerprinting and radiomics analysis in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: MRF-derived T1/T2 quantitative maps and radiomic features in 18 children/young adults with ADPKD (normal kidney function) vs 11 healthy volunteers. Mean T1/T2 in non-cystic parenchyma and whole kidney were significantly higher in ADPKD; combined radiomic features differentiated ADPKD from controls (AUC 0.79-0.99 non-cystic parenchyma; 0.92-0.96 whole kidney).
papers.novelty_assessment: First pilot applying MR fingerprinting-derived T1/T2 radiomics to ADPKD, suggesting non-cystic parenchymal tissue changes are detectable before functional decline.
key_findings: MRF T1/T2 relaxation times higher in ADPKD non-cystic parenchyma and whole kidney vs healthy volunteers
Radiomic feature combinations differentiated ADPKD from controls (AUC up to 0.99)
Signal present in young patients with still-normal kidney function
papers.clinical_implications: Hints at an early tissue-level imaging biomarker of parenchymal involvement, but this is a small cross-sectional pilot with no link to progression or outcomes.
papers.what_happened: A pilot study found that MR fingerprinting-derived T1/T2 radiomic features distinguished 18 young ADPKD patients with normal kidney function from 11 healthy volunteers, including in non-cystic parenchyma.
papers.why_it_matters: It suggests quantitative MRI may detect early parenchymal involvement before measurable functional loss, a potential early biomarker.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Very small cross-sectional sample (n=18 vs 11), classification-only AUC endpoints with high radiomics overfitting risk, and no association with disease progression or outcomes.

papers.title: Abdominal arterial calcification profile in kidney transplant candidates: a comparison between patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and those with other causes of kidney failure.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective cohort of 4088 adult kidney-transplant candidates at three Mayo Clinic sites (2005-2024). After 1:1 propensity matching (309 ADPKD vs 309 non-ADPKD CKD), abdominal arterial calcification (modified Agatston on non-contrast CT) was significantly lower in ADPKD (median 425.3, IQR 0.0-2033.5) than non-ADPKD (median 1256.8).
papers.novelty_assessment: Large propensity-matched comparison characterizing a distinct (lower) abdominal arterial calcification burden in ADPKD versus other causes of kidney failure among transplant candidates.
key_findings: ADPKD transplant candidates had significantly lower abdominal arterial calcification than matched non-ADPKD CKD candidates
Difference persisted after 1:1 propensity matching on major cardiovascular confounders
Supports the recognized comparatively favorable vascular profile of ADPKD
papers.clinical_implications: May refine cardiovascular risk stratification and transplant-timing considerations in ADPKD, but the endpoint is a calcification surrogate, not cardiovascular events.
papers.what_happened: A propensity-matched retrospective Mayo Clinic cohort found that ADPKD kidney-transplant candidates had significantly lower abdominal arterial calcification scores than matched non-ADPKD CKD candidates.
papers.why_it_matters: It quantifies the comparatively favorable vascular calcification profile of ADPKD, relevant to cardiovascular risk stratification and transplant timing.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective single-system design with residual confounding despite matching, and the outcome is a CT calcification surrogate rather than cardiovascular events.

papers.title: Liver Transplantation for Polycystic Liver Disease: A Retrospective Analysis From a University Center.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective single-center analysis (1994-2024): of 1188 liver transplants, 9 (0.75%) were for polycystic liver disease (PLD), mostly women (88.8%), mean age 47.3y, indicated mainly for compressive symptoms/QoL. Survival 66.6% at 30 days, 55.5% at 5 years; 3 required retransplantation for hepatic artery thrombosis.
papers.novelty_assessment: Small single-center 30-year case series of liver transplantation for polycystic liver disease, a condition frequently associated with ADPKD but here not ADPKD-specific.
key_findings: PLD accounted for 9/1188 (0.75%) liver transplants over 30 years
Main indication was compressive symptoms / quality-of-life impairment
5-year survival 55.5%; 3 of 9 required retransplantation for hepatic artery thrombosis
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces liver transplantation as a last-resort option for severely symptomatic polycystic liver disease, but provides little ADPKD-specific or generalizable guidance.
papers.what_happened: A single-center retrospective series reported outcomes of 9 liver transplants performed for polycystic liver disease over 30 years, mainly for compressive symptoms, with 55.5% 5-year survival.
papers.why_it_matters: Polycystic liver disease is a common extrarenal manifestation of ADPKD, and transplantation remains the only curative option for severe symptomatic hepatomegaly.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Tiny case series (n=9) spanning 30 years from one center, descriptive only, and not ADPKD-specific.

papers.title: A three-year randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of lanreotide in stage 2/3 autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 3-year trial (LIPS, NCT02127437) of monthly lanreotide 120 mg vs saline placebo in 144 adults with ADPKD and mGFR 30-89 mL/min/1.73m2. Primary endpoint (iohexol-measured GFR slope) not met: annualized between-arm difference -0.3 mL/min/1.73m2/yr (95% CI -3.4 to 2.8). A positive creatinine-eGFR signal (+1.2, 0.27-2.15) was not replicated by cystatin C-eGFR or urinary creatinine clearance. Hypoglycemia 11.1% (lanreotide) vs 1.4% (placebo).
papers.novelty_assessment: First full peer-reviewed publication of the LIPS Phase 3 randomized trial (NCT02127437), which completed primary data collection in July 2019 -- the publication, not the underlying scientific event, is what is new. Missed by the tracker during the 2026-06-18 to 2026-07-21 pipeline gap.
key_findings: Primary endpoint negative: no difference in measured (iohexol) GFR slope over 3 years, between-arm difference -0.3 mL/min/1.73m2/yr (95% CI -3.4 to 2.8)

A significant creatinine-based eGFR signal (+1.2 mL/min/1.73m2/yr) was NOT reproduced by cystatin C-eGFR or urinary creatinine clearance, which the authors attribute to a non-GFR effect on creatinine physiology
Kidney events and quality-of-life scores were similar between arms
New safety signal: hypoglycemia in 11.1% of lanreotide vs 1.4% of placebo participants; gastrointestinal adverse events more frequent with lanreotide
Enrollment stopped early at 144 of 180 planned participants due to slow recruitment, widening the confidence interval
papers.clinical_implications: Does not support somatostatin-analogue therapy for kidney-function protection in stage 2/3 ADPKD, and adds a hypoglycemia monitoring consideration if lanreotide is used for other indications such as polycystic liver disease.

claim_audit.study_design: interventional-RCT (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3 years, measured GFR primary endpoint)
claim_audit.endpoint_type: surrogate (measured GFR slope by iohexol clearance; secondary kidney events and QoL)
claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Academic investigator-initiated (Assistance Publique - Hopitaux de Paris); somatostatin analogue supplied context not stated in abstract.

papers.what_happened: A 3-year randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of monthly lanreotide in 144 adults with stage 2/3 ADPKD did not meet its primary endpoint of slowing iohexol-measured GFR decline, and reported a previously unflagged hypoglycemia signal (11.1% vs 1.4%).
papers.why_it_matters: This is among the strongest randomized evidence to date on somatostatin analogues in ADPKD, using measured rather than estimated GFR, and it weakens the case for using lanreotide to protect kidney function in this population.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Recruitment stopped early (144 of 180 planned), so the confidence interval (-3.4 to +2.8 mL/min/1.73m2/yr) cannot exclude a modest benefit or harm; the trial completed in 2019 and these data are only now published, and results apply only to adults with mGFR 30-89 mL/min/1.73m2.

papers.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Octreotide, Lanreotide, and Pasireotide in ADPKD and PLD: A Network Meta-analysis with Real-world Evidence from the FAERS Database.
papers.abstract_snippet: Network meta-analysis of the limited randomized literature on octreotide, lanreotide and pasireotide for TKV, TLV and eGFR in ADPKD/PLD, combined with a FAERS disproportionality/Cox analysis of biliary adverse events. Reports TKV reduction for octreotide and pasireotide at 6-12 months and for lanreotide beyond 2 years; cholelithiasis the most common biliary adverse event, with age and drug identified as independent predictors.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly published (2026-07-20) and directly relevant to interpreting the concurrently published negative lanreotide RCT (pm_42320793): volumetric reduction without demonstrated GFR benefit.
key_findings: Octreotide (MD -3.7, 95%CI -4.3 to -3.2) and pasireotide (-5.0, -8.2 to -1.8) associated with TKV reduction vs placebo at 6-12 months; lanreotide (-7.8, -10.2 to -5.4) at >2 years
Lanreotide showed inferior TLV growth-rate reduction vs octreotide over 2-3 years (10.0, 2.7 to 18.0)
Cholelithiasis was the most common biliary adverse event across all three agents; younger age and pasireotide associated with higher risk
Authors explicitly note pooled estimates come from 'limited available trials'
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces that somatostatin analogues reduce cyst volume surrogates while leaving kidney-function benefit unproven, and highlights cholelithiasis as the dominant biliary toxicity to counsel about.

claim_audit.study_design: meta-analysis (network meta-analysis of few trials) plus pharmacovigilance database analysis
claim_audit.endpoint_type: surrogate (TKV, TLV, eGFR) plus spontaneously-reported adverse events
claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None declared in abstract; no commercial sponsor stated.

papers.what_happened: A network meta-analysis of a small number of somatostatin-analogue trials reported differing time courses of TKV and TLV reduction across octreotide, lanreotide and pasireotide, paired with a FAERS analysis identifying cholelithiasis as the leading biliary adverse event.
papers.why_it_matters: It provides the first side-by-side comparison of the three somatostatin analogues on cyst-volume surrogates and biliary safety in ADPKD and polycystic liver disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The network is sparse and built on few small trials, all endpoints are volumetric or eGFR surrogates rather than patient-important outcomes, indirect comparisons are fragile, and FAERS spontaneous reports have no denominator and are subject to reporting bias -- so the Cox 'predictors of cholelithiasis' analysis should not be read as risk estimation.

papers.title: Association between nephrolithiasis and kidney disease progression in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract_snippet: Prospective HOPE-PKD cohort (Korea) of 410 ADPKD patients with baseline CT; CT-confirmed nephrolithiasis (cyst-wall calcification excluded) vs no stones. Median 5.18 years follow-up; 51 (12.4%) reached RRT. Adjusted HR 2.84 (95% CI 1.26-6.38) for RRT initiation and 1.83 (1.03-3.27) for the composite secondary outcome.
papers.novelty_assessment: First prospective, imaging-confirmed assessment of nephrolithiasis as a progression risk factor in ADPKD with a patient-important (RRT) endpoint; prior evidence was retrospective.
key_findings: Imaging-confirmed nephrolithiasis independently associated with RRT initiation (adjusted HR 2.84, 95% CI 1.26-6.38, P=.012)
Composite secondary outcome (>=50% eGFR decline, doubling of creatinine, or RRT) HR 1.83 (1.03-3.27, P=.041)
Associations appeared more pronounced in males, higher BMI, worse baseline kidney function, larger kidney volume, and PKD1 genotype
Cyst-wall calcifications were explicitly excluded using established CT criteria, reducing a common misclassification problem
papers.clinical_implications: Supports considering CT-detected kidney stones as an additional risk marker alongside Mayo imaging class and genotype, though it does not establish that treating stones alters kidney outcomes.

claim_audit.study_design: observational-prospective (prospective cohort with imaging-confirmed exposure and patient-important endpoint)
claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Y.K. Oh reports research grants from Korea Otsuka Pharmaceutical; other authors declare none.

papers.what_happened: In a prospective Korean cohort of 410 ADPKD patients followed a median 5.2 years, CT-confirmed nephrolithiasis was independently associated with a higher risk of starting renal replacement therapy (HR 2.84).
papers.why_it_matters: Kidney stones are common and potentially modifiable in ADPKD, so an independent association with kidney failure would add a practical element to risk stratification.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is observational, so stones may be a marker of more severe underlying disease rather than a cause; only 51 primary events drove a wide confidence interval (1.26-6.38), the secondary endpoint barely excluded the null (lower bound 1.03), exposure was assessed on a single baseline CT, and the cohort is single-country.

papers.title: Halting cyst progression in ADPKD using long-term ketogenic metabolic therapy and supplementation with exogenous ketones and alkaline citrate-a case series.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective case series of four self-referred individuals (ages 33-71) with truncating PKD1 variants who independently adopted carbohydrate restriction, intermittent fasting and a commercial ketone/citrate medical food (KetoCitra) for 6 months to ~4 years. Serial routine-care imaging re-analysed volumetrically showed stabilization or reduction of TKV relative to prior growth trends in all four. Two authors were employees of Santa Barbara Nutrients, Inc.; the senior author is a shareholder, holds a managerial position, and is an inventor on related patents.
papers.novelty_assessment: Commercially conflicted uncontrolled case series with a title that substantially overstates the evidence; scored down aggressively per the framework's rules on commercial and conflicted studies.
key_findings: Four self-selected cases with truncating PKD1 variants showed TKV stabilization or reduction relative to their own prior growth trends
One participant shifted from Mayo Class 1C to 1B; three showed downward trajectory shifts within existing classes
Interventions were heterogeneous in type, intensity and duration (6 months to ~4 years)
Two authors were employees of the company selling the medical food; the senior author is a shareholder, holds a managerial position, and is a named inventor on related patents
papers.clinical_implications: None. This design cannot support any clinical recommendation; it is at most a rationale for prospective controlled trials, several of which are already registered.

claim_audit.endpoint_type: surrogate (TKV, liver volume, Mayo imaging class)
claim_audit.comparator: baseline-only (each patient's own prior growth trend)
claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Substantial: two authors were employees of Santa Barbara Nutrients, Inc. (maker of KetoCitra); senior author is a shareholder with a managerial position and an inventor on related patents, and reports consulting/research funding from Chinook Therapeutics, Insmed and Kyowa Kirin.

papers.what_happened: Four self-referred ADPKD patients who adopted ketogenic metabolic therapy plus a commercial ketone/citrate medical food were retrospectively reported to show TKV stabilization or reduction compared with their own prior growth trends.
papers.why_it_matters: Dietary and metabolic interventions are of high interest to the ADPKD patient community, and this is longitudinal human volumetric imaging rather than animal data.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The title claim of 'halting cyst progression' is not supported by the design: n=4, self-selected, uncontrolled, retrospective, each patient serving as their own historical comparator, heterogeneous co-interventions, a surrogate endpoint, and direct financial conflicts including company employment, shareholding and patents on the product studied -- regression to the mean and selection of responders cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Real-World Outcomes of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Therapy in Nondiabetic Autosomal-Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Effects on Progression to Dialysis in a TrinetX Cohort".
papers.journal: Mayo Clinic Proceedings: Innovations, Quality & Outcomes
papers.abstract_snippet: Corrigendum to the March 2026 TriNetX propensity-matched analysis of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy and progression to dialysis in nondiabetic ADPKD (parent article pm_41853136, DOI 10.1016/j.mayocpiqo.2026.100709). The corrigendum text is not available in the PubMed record, so the nature and materiality of the correction could not be determined from indexing alone.
papers.novelty_assessment: Correction notice only; no new scientific event. Flagged as an action item for deep analysis to verify whether the parent study's conclusions changed.
key_findings: Correction notice issued against the TriNetX SGLT2i-in-nondiabetic-ADPKD observational study already tracked as pm_41853136
Specific content of the correction is not exposed in the PubMed record
Parent study conclusions should be treated as provisional pending review of the corrigendum full text
papers.clinical_implications: Flags the need to re-check the parent observational SGLT2i study before citing its dialysis-progression estimate; no independent clinical implication.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the correction notice.

papers.what_happened: A corrigendum was published against the March 2026 TriNetX observational study of SGLT2 inhibitors and progression to dialysis in nondiabetic ADPKD, which is already tracked in this database.
papers.why_it_matters: The parent study is one of the few human datasets on SGLT2 inhibitors specifically in nondiabetic ADPKD, so any correction to it affects how much weight that estimate should carry.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The correction text is not available through PubMed indexing, so it is currently unknown whether the correction is trivial (e.g., an author affiliation) or affects the effect estimates -- the parent paper should be re-examined during deep analysis before its results are cited further.

papers.title: Comparison of genetic profile and kidney outcomes between very early-onset and non-very-early-onset autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract_snippet: Systematic review and Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis of 19 studies (736 children: 335 VEO, 401 non-VEO). VEO-ADPKD showed higher odds of hypertension (OR 2.08, 95% CrI 1.00-2.70), proteinuria (1.58, 1.00-2.60), CKD (1.77, 1.00-2.66) and kidney failure (1.99, 1.00-2.69). Biallelic PKD1 mutations (38/158 vs 0/147) and perinatal death (34/320 vs 0/401) occurred exclusively in the VEO group.
papers.novelty_assessment: First meta-analytic quantification of the VEO-ADPKD versus non-VEO pediatric phenotype gap; underlying evidence base remains small retrospective series.
key_findings: VEO-ADPKD associated with higher odds of hypertension, proteinuria, CKD and kidney failure than non-VEO pediatric ADPKD
Biallelic PKD1 mutations found only in the VEO group (38/158 vs 0/147), supporting a dose-dependent severity model
Perinatal death occurred only in the VEO group (34/320 vs 0/401), reported descriptively due to complete separation
Evidence for maternal inheritance in VEO-ADPKD was weak (OR 1.31, BF10 1.6)
papers.clinical_implications: Supports early genetic evaluation in children presenting in utero or in the first 18 months, particularly to identify biallelic PKD1 cases whose course more closely resembles mild ARPKD.

claim_audit.study_design: review-systematic / meta-analysis (of observational pediatric case series)
claim_audit.endpoint_type: patient-important (kidney failure, perinatal death) plus surrogate

papers.what_happened: A meta-analysis of 19 studies covering 736 children found that very early-onset ADPKD carries higher odds of hypertension, proteinuria, CKD and kidney failure, with biallelic PKD1 mutations and perinatal death occurring exclusively in the VEO group.
papers.why_it_matters: It quantifies how distinct the very early-onset pediatric phenotype is and strengthens the case for genetic testing to separate biallelic PKD1 disease from typical ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Every pooled credible interval has a lower bound of exactly 1.00, meaning the null was only just excluded; the search covered MEDLINE only, the underlying studies are small retrospective case series prone to ascertainment and publication bias, and complete separation prevented formal estimation for the two most striking findings.

papers.title: Factors associated with loss of renal function in patients with polycystic kidney disease: a nationwide real-world data analysis.
papers.abstract_snippet: Japanese national intractable-disease registry analysis of 3562 ADPKD patients followed >3 years (2015-2021). Mean eGFR decline -3.17 mL/min/1.73m2/yr. Advanced CKD stage and proteinuria were the strongest correlates of >=30% eGFR decline (CKD G4 HR 7.23, 5.51-9.50; albuminuria A3 HR 2.02, 1.71-2.40).
papers.novelty_assessment: Large national confirmation of known prognostic factors (CKD stage, proteinuria); confirmatory rather than novel.
key_findings: Mean eGFR decline -3.17 (-3.25 to -3.09) mL/min/1.73m2/yr across 3562 registry patients
CKD stages G3a/G3b/G4 carried HRs of 1.89, 3.84 and 7.23 for >=30% eGFR decline
Proteinuria categories A2 and A3 carried HRs of 1.66 and 2.02
CART analysis identified younger patients at advanced CKD stages with proteinuria as the highest-risk group
papers.clinical_implications: Supports proteinuria monitoring and CKD-heatmap-style risk stratification in advanced ADPKD, but largely confirms established prognostic factors.
papers.what_happened: A Japanese national registry analysis of 3562 ADPKD patients found that advanced CKD stage and higher proteinuria were the strongest correlates of a >=30% eGFR decline over more than three years.
papers.why_it_matters: It quantifies progression risk in a large, unselected national ADPKD population rather than a trial-enriched cohort.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The findings largely confirm already-established prognostic factors, the design is a retrospective registry analysis without imaging or genotype adjustment, the endpoint is a surrogate, and registry inclusion required meeting Japanese intractable-disease criteria, limiting generalizability.

papers.title: The effect of tolvaptan on total kidney volume and inflammatory markers in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective single-centre study of 67 ADPKD patients (40 tolvaptan, 27 untreated) over 24 months. NLR, PLR and SII decreased in the tolvaptan group and increased in controls, with lower percentage TKV growth in treated patients. Tolvaptan-treated patients were younger with higher baseline TKV.
papers.novelty_assessment: Small retrospective association between tolvaptan use and blood-count inflammatory indices; confounded by indication.
key_findings: Inflammatory indices (NLR, PLR, SII) fell in tolvaptan users and rose in untreated patients over 24 months
Percentage TKV increase was lower in the tolvaptan group; significant time x treatment interactions reported
Treated patients were younger and had higher baseline TKV than controls -- classic confounding by indication
Authors conclude only that further prospective studies are needed
papers.clinical_implications: Does not change tolvaptan prescribing; at most suggests an anti-inflammatory correlate worth testing prospectively.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Authors declare no conflicts of interest.

papers.what_happened: A retrospective study of 67 ADPKD patients found that blood-count-derived inflammatory indices fell over 24 months in the 40 taking tolvaptan while rising in 27 untreated patients, alongside lower percentage TKV growth.
papers.why_it_matters: If tolvaptan has an anti-inflammatory component, that would add to the cAMP-centred mechanistic account of its effect.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Treated and untreated groups differed substantially at baseline (tolvaptan patients were younger with larger kidneys), so confounding by indication is severe; n=67 is small, the design is retrospective and non-randomized, and NLR/PLR/SII are crude, non-specific surrogates rather than validated inflammation endpoints.

papers.title: Association between polycystic kidney disease and valve disease: a nationwide population-based nested case-control study.
papers.abstract_snippet: Nationwide nested case-control study of 331,125 individuals (66,225 with valvular heart disease, 264,900 matched controls) using ICD-10-CM codes. PKD prevalence 0.37% in cases vs 0.21% in controls; adjusted OR 1.609 (95% CI 1.217-2.038).
papers.novelty_assessment: Population-scale quantification of an already well-recognized ADPKD-valve association; confirmatory.
key_findings: PKD associated with higher odds of valvular heart disease (aOR 1.609, 95% CI 1.217-2.038)
PKD prevalence 0.37% among valve-disease cases vs 0.21% among matched controls
Association consistent across demographic and clinical subgroups, with temporal and cumulative-exposure analyses reported as supportive
Both exposure and outcome defined solely by diagnostic codes
papers.clinical_implications: Consistent with long-recognized valvular involvement in ADPKD; does not by itself justify changing echocardiographic screening practice.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the available record.

papers.what_happened: A nationwide nested case-control study of 331,125 people found polycystic kidney disease was associated with roughly 1.6-fold higher odds of a valvular heart disease diagnosis.
papers.why_it_matters: Valvular disease is a recognized extrarenal ADPKD manifestation, and this puts a population-level estimate on the association.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Both PKD and valve disease were identified from diagnostic codes with no imaging or genetic confirmation, PKD patients undergo more cardiac imaging than controls so detection bias is likely, ADPKD and unspecified PKD were pooled, and the association is not new -- mitral valve prolapse in ADPKD is long established.

papers.title: Fracture risk assessment in early-stage autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study using FRAX, QFracture, and Garvan models.
papers.abstract_snippet: Cross-sectional study of adults with early-stage ADPKD and preserved kidney function; fracture risk calculable in 67 (QFracture), 46 (FRAX) and 23 (Garvan). Median 10-year major osteoporotic and hip fracture risks were consistently low, BMD was preserved, and age was the only independent predictor -- neither eGFR nor htTKV was associated with fracture risk.
papers.novelty_assessment: First evaluation of fracture-risk calculators in early ADPKD; a modest negative result on eGFR and htTKV as bone-risk markers.
key_findings: Median predicted 10-year fracture risks were low across all three calculators in early-stage ADPKD
NEGATIVE finding: neither eGFR nor height-adjusted TKV was associated with fracture risk in any model
Age was the only independent predictor of estimated fracture risk
QFracture was most practically applicable given its broader age range and CKD variables
papers.clinical_implications: Provides mild reassurance that early-stage ADPKD with preserved function is not accompanied by elevated calculated fracture risk, and does not support htTKV as a bone-risk marker.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the available record.

papers.what_happened: A cross-sectional study of adults with early-stage ADPKD found low calculated 10-year fracture risk across FRAX, QFracture and Garvan, with preserved bone mineral density and no association between fracture risk and either eGFR or height-adjusted total kidney volume.
papers.why_it_matters: Prior work suggested ADPKD might carry excess fracture risk relative to other CKD, and this is the first direct evaluation of fracture-risk calculators in the early-stage population.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small and unevenly powered (only 23 patients for the Garvan model), cross-sectional with no observed fracture outcomes -- only calculator-predicted risk -- and restricted to preserved kidney function, so it says nothing about advanced ADPKD.

papers.title: Kidney and Cardiovascular Outcomes by CKD stage and etiology of CKD: A Randomly Selected Nationwide Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study in Japan (Reach-J Study).
papers.abstract_snippet: Randomly sampled nationwide Japanese CKD G3b-G5 cohort (n=2249, 31 institutions, 5-year follow-up). PKD accounted for 5.8% of the cohort and had the highest KRT initiation rate at stages G4/G5, later surpassing diabetic kidney disease on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Higher proteinuria predicted worse renal outcomes across all etiologies.
papers.novelty_assessment: Places ADPKD's progression trajectory in comparative national context against other CKD etiologies.
key_findings: PKD comprised 5.8% of a randomly sampled national advanced-CKD cohort
PKD had the highest KRT initiation rate at CKD stages G4/G5, overtaking diabetic kidney disease later in follow-up
Diabetic kidney disease drove earlier KRT initiation but PKD surpassed it over time
Higher proteinuria predicted worse renal outcomes across all etiologies, while cardiovascular and mortality rates did not differ by proteinuria stage
papers.clinical_implications: Contextualizes ADPKD's distinctive trajectory in advanced CKD -- later but steeper progression to kidney replacement therapy than diabetic kidney disease.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the available record.

papers.what_happened: A randomly sampled nationwide Japanese cohort of 2249 advanced-CKD patients found that polycystic kidney disease, though only 5.8% of the cohort, had the highest rate of kidney replacement therapy initiation at stages G4/G5.
papers.why_it_matters: Random institutional sampling reduces referral bias, giving a relatively unbiased comparison of ADPKD's trajectory against other CKD causes at the same stage.
papers.what_limits_confidence: PKD represents only 130 or so patients, the analysis is descriptive with limited adjustment, subgroup comparisons by etiology and stage are numerous, and Japanese practice patterns for KRT initiation may not generalize.

papers.title: Diagnostic Performance of Routine Abdominal MRI for Detecting Left Ventricular Hypertrophy in ADPKD.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective study of 156 ADPKD patients (27 with echocardiographic LVH). Height-adjusted LV wall volume measured on routine T2-weighted abdominal MRI detected echo-defined LVH with AUC 0.82 (sensitivity 92%, specificity 64% at 60 mL/m), rising to 0.92 after adjustment for body surface area, age, sex and systolic BP.
papers.novelty_assessment: Proposes opportunistic cardiac assessment from routine ADPKD surveillance MRI; needs external validation.
key_findings: Height-adjusted LV wall volume from routine abdominal MRI detected echo-defined LVH with AUC 0.82 (0.74-0.90)
Sensitivity 92% but specificity only 64% at the 60 mL/m threshold
Performance was robust across sex, CKD stage, Mayo class and blood pressure subgroups
Adjusted AUC improved to 0.92 -- but this is a within-sample adjustment, not external validation
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests routine ADPKD surveillance MRI could opportunistically flag left ventricular hypertrophy, though echocardiography remains the reference standard and specificity is modest.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the available record.

papers.what_happened: In 156 ADPKD patients, height-adjusted left ventricular wall volume derived from routine abdominal MRI detected echocardiographically defined left ventricular hypertrophy with an AUC of 0.82.
papers.why_it_matters: ADPKD patients already undergo serial abdominal MRI for TKV, so extracting cardiac information at no extra cost would be practically attractive.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective single-cohort design with only 27 LVH cases, manual segmentation that may not be reproducible in routine workflow, specificity of just 64% at the proposed threshold, no external validation, and the improved AUC of 0.92 comes from in-sample covariate adjustment rather than independent testing.

papers.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Intracranial Aneurysm Screening: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract_snippet: Systematic review of 15 economic modelling studies from 8 countries (1996-2025) on screening for unruptured intracranial aneurysms. Nine evaluated high-risk populations including ADPKD. Model inputs varied widely (assumed UIA prevalence 0.5% to 19%; annual rupture rates varied), and study quality was assessed with a modified ECOBIAS checklist.
papers.novelty_assessment: Synthesizes the health-economic literature on ICA screening; documents heterogeneity rather than resolving ADPKD screening policy.
key_findings: 15 modelling studies across 8 countries reviewed; 9 covered high-risk populations including ADPKD
Assumed unruptured intracranial aneurysm prevalence varied enormously across models (0.5% to 19%)
Wide heterogeneity in model inputs, perspectives and rupture-rate assumptions limits pooled conclusions
No primary clinical data -- all included studies are health-economic models
papers.clinical_implications: Relevant to the ongoing debate about whether to screen ADPKD patients for intracranial aneurysms, but the review documents input heterogeneity rather than resolving the question.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the available record.

papers.what_happened: A systematic review of 15 health-economic modelling studies on intracranial aneurysm screening found wide variation in key input assumptions across the nine studies covering high-risk groups such as ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Intracranial aneurysm screening in ADPKD remains contested, and cost-effectiveness is a central argument on both sides.
papers.what_limits_confidence: These are models, not clinical studies -- conclusions are driven entirely by input assumptions that ranged from 0.5% to 19% for aneurysm prevalence, ADPKD-specific results are not separable from other high-risk groups in the summary, and no pooled estimate was produced.

papers.title: Clinical impact of genetic testing in inherited kidney diseases.
papers.abstract_snippet: Single tertiary-centre prospective enrolment of 256 patients (175 adults, 81 children) with suspected inherited kidney disease, 2020-2023, using targeted panels or exome sequencing with CNV and MUC1 analysis. Pathogenic variants found in 38.7%; PKD1, PKD2, COL4A5, COL4A4 and HNF1B accounted for 62.6% of solved cases. Diagnostic yield highest in cystic kidney disease (72.0%).
papers.novelty_assessment: Real-world diagnostic yield data supporting genetic testing in cystic kidney disease.
key_findings: Overall diagnostic yield 38.7%; highest in cystic kidney diseases at 72.0%
PKD1 and PKD2 were among the five genes accounting for 62.6% of all solved cases
Positive family history, extrarenal manifestations and hypertension predicted a genetic diagnosis
Kidney survival varied substantially across genetic subgroups
papers.clinical_implications: Supports genetic testing as high-yield in suspected cystic kidney disease and reinforces its role in prognosis, consistent with current KDIGO ADPKD guidance.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the available record.

papers.what_happened: A single-centre prospective cohort of 256 patients with suspected inherited kidney disease reported a 38.7% overall diagnostic yield from genetic testing, rising to 72.0% in cystic kidney disease, with PKD1 and PKD2 among the top contributing genes.
papers.why_it_matters: It quantifies the practical return on genetic testing in a real clinical service, which matters for the access and reimbursement arguments made in recent ADPKD guideline commentaries.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single tertiary centre with referral-enriched case mix, so the 72% cystic-disease yield will not generalize to unselected populations; ADPKD-specific outcomes are not separated from other cystic diseases, and the kidney-survival comparisons across genetic subgroups involve small subgroups.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Epidemiology of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease among patients incident on first kidney replacement therapy between 1990-2023, in a major hospital in the Northwest of Portugal.
papers.abstract_snippet: Review of 6791 kidney-replacement-therapy initiation reports at a Porto academic hospital (1990-2023) identifying 426 ADPKD patients, with genotype available for 168 (39.4%). Investigates a suspected regional excess of PKD2 disease, particularly the truncating variant PKD2 p.(Gln61*), against national registry prevalence figures.
papers.novelty_assessment: Regional genetic epidemiology documenting a probable PKD2 founder effect in northwest Portugal.
key_findings: 426 ADPKD patients identified among 6791 incident KRT reports over 33 years
Genotype data available for only 39.4% of identified ADPKD patients
Investigates a suspected regional founder effect for the truncating PKD2 p.(Gln61*) variant
Compares local against national Portuguese registry ADPKD prevalence among incident KRT patients
papers.clinical_implications: Illustrates how regional founder variants can shift the local PKD1/PKD2 ratio and hence expected age at kidney failure; limited relevance outside northwest Portugal.

key_findings: Gd-hProCA32.Collagen detected ~2.8-fold greater total renal cyst volume and 1.5-fold higher cyst count than gadobutrol in PCK rats/Pkd2-mutant mice (p<0.0001)
Signal correlated strongly with histological collagen (Sirius red) staining; gadobutrol showed no meaningful correlation
Agent revealed radial-striation microfibrosis patterns not visible with conventional MRI, in kidney and liver
All data are from rodent models only; no human data reported
papers.clinical_implications: None yet; this is a preclinical imaging-agent proof-of-concept, not a clinical monitoring tool.

claim_audit.endpoint_type: surrogate (imaging/histological fibrosis signal, not a patient outcome)
claim_audit.comparator: active (gadobutrol, standard clinical contrast agent) -- within animal models only
claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the abstract; academic preclinical imaging-agent study, possible undisclosed IP interest in the contrast agent.

papers.what_happened: A preprint reports a new collagen-targeted MRI contrast agent (Gd-hProCA32.Collagen) that detected significantly more renal/hepatic cyst volume and fibrosis-associated signal than the standard clinical agent gadobutrol in PCK rats and Pkd2-mutant mice, correlating with histological collagen staining.
papers.why_it_matters: If it eventually translates to humans, a fibrosis-specific imaging agent could enable earlier, non-invasive detection of a subclinical fibrotic phase of ADPKD that current TKV/eGFR-based monitoring cannot detect.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is an unreviewed preprint using only rodent models; no human data exist, the title's 'unmasking' framing overstates present translational readiness, and ADPKD preclinical imaging findings have a historically weak record of clinical translation.

papers.title: Combination siRNA delivery as a therapeutic strategy for ADPKD
papers.abstract_snippet: Preclinical preprint reporting collecting-duct-targeted peptide-amphiphile micelles co-delivering Tmem16a and Mcp-1 siRNA, reducing kidney enlargement, cyst burden, tubular injury, and macrophage infiltration in an inducible Pkd1-deficient mouse model, with target engagement shown in human ADPKD patient-derived cells in vitro.
papers.novelty_assessment: First disclosure of a dual-target (TMEM16A + MCP-1) siRNA nanoparticle strategy for ADPKD; joins the growing preclinical RNAi/gene-silencing cluster (CRISPRa, mRNA-LNP) already tracked.
key_findings: TMEM16A and MCP-1 are consistently upregulated in cyst-lining collecting-duct epithelia across mouse, pig, and human ADPKD models
Combined silencing of both targets in human ADPKD cells produced greater cyst-growth reduction than silencing either alone

Collecting-duct-targeted peptide-micelle siRNA co-delivery reduced kidney enlargement, cystic burden, tubular injury, and macrophage infiltration in Pkd1-deficient mice, exceeding non-targeted delivery at equivalent doses
Efficacy and target engagement also shown in ADPKD patient-derived collecting-duct cells in vitro
papers.clinical_implications: None yet; this is an early-stage preclinical nanomedicine/RNAi delivery platform, not a clinical therapy.

claim_audit.endpoint_type: surrogate (kidney weight, cyst burden, gene expression -- not patient outcomes)
claim_audit.comparator: active (non-targeted siRNA delivery, single-target silencing) -- within preclinical models
claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the abstract; academic preclinical nanomedicine study.

papers.what_happened: A preprint reports that collecting-duct-targeted peptide-micelle nanoparticles co-delivering TMEM16A and MCP-1 siRNA reduced kidney enlargement, cyst burden, tubular injury, and macrophage infiltration in an inducible Pkd1-deficient mouse model, with added efficacy over single-target or non-targeted delivery, and showed target engagement in ADPKD patient-derived cells in vitro.
papers.why_it_matters: It adds a new dual-target RNAi/nanoparticle delivery approach to the expanding gene-silencing pipeline for ADPKD (alongside CRISPRa and mRNA-LNP strategies already tracked), with a combination rationale not previously demonstrated in vivo.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is an unreviewed preprint with in vivo efficacy shown only in a short-term mouse model; there is no long-term safety, pharmacokinetic, or human in vivo data, and the abstract's framing as an 'effective therapeutic strategy' overstates what mouse-only data can support given ADPKD's historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: Pregnancy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Maternal and Fetal Considerations: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review of maternal and fetal risks and practical management considerations for pregnancy in individuals with ADPKD, synthesizing PubMed/MEDLINE literature and clinical practice guidelines.
papers.novelty_assessment: Narrative synthesis of an under-covered ADPKD subtopic (pregnancy management); no new primary data.
key_findings: Summarizes maternal risks (hypertension, preeclampsia, UTIs, potential accelerated CKD progression) and fetal risks in ADPKD pregnancies
Proposes practical management considerations for counseling and monitoring, drawing on existing guidelines rather than new evidence
papers.clinical_implications: May inform patient counseling discussions but does not itself establish new management thresholds; underlying evidence base for ADPKD-specific pregnancy risk remains sparse.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review summarizes maternal and fetal considerations for pregnancy in ADPKD and offers practical management guidance based on existing literature and guidelines.
papers.why_it_matters: Pregnancy counseling is a recurring practical concern for reproductive-age ADPKD patients and this consolidates scattered evidence into one reference.
papers.what_limits_confidence: As a narrative (non-systematic) review with no new primary data, it reflects existing evidence quality rather than adding new certainty about ADPKD-specific pregnancy risk.

papers.title: Metabolomics in renal cystic disease: links to mechanisms and identification of pathways for potential pre-diagnosis.
papers.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Renal Physiology
papers.abstract_snippet: Review synthesizing metabolomics studies of human PKD and renal cystic disease, with pathway enrichment analyses conducted separately for overall cystic kidney disease and ADPKD/Pkd1 vs non-Pkd1 subsets; highlights amino acid metabolism pathways (arginine biosynthesis; glycine/serine/threonine, the latter specific to ADPKD/Pkd1 models) and relative suppression of carbohydrate energy metabolism.
papers.novelty_assessment: Synthesizes existing metabolomics literature (mostly preclinical/mouse-model derived) rather than reporting a new primary dataset; identifies an ADPKD/Pkd1-specific pathway signature across pooled studies.
key_findings: Top-ranked pathways across pooled PKD metabolomics studies: arginine biosynthesis; alanine/aspartate/glutamate metabolism; glycine/serine/threonine metabolism; citrate cycle
Glycine/serine/threonine metabolism pathway enrichment was specific to ADPKD/Pkd1 mouse models, not seen in non-Pkd1 cystic disease
Overall pattern suggests amino-acid-metabolism activation with relative suppression of carbohydrate-based energy metabolism, i.e., a substrate-utilization shift rather than global energy failure
papers.clinical_implications: Proposes metabolomics as a potential earlier and less invasive diagnostic/mechanistic tool than imaging or genetic testing, but this is a hypothesis derived largely from mouse-model data pooled across heterogeneous studies, not a validated human biomarker panel.
papers.what_happened: A review pools published metabolomics studies of PKD and cystic kidney disease, identifying amino-acid-metabolism pathways enriched overall and a glycine/serine/threonine signature specific to ADPKD/Pkd1 models.
papers.why_it_matters: Offers candidate mechanistic/biomarker pathways for earlier, non-invasive detection of ADPKD, an area where imaging and genetic testing both have real limitations.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The pooled pathway signal is drawn predominantly from heterogeneous preclinical (largely mouse) metabolomics studies rather than a validated human biomarker cohort, and ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: Diagnosing Mendelian Kidney Disease: Hidden Niches in the (Kidney) Genome.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report of a family in which the index patient carries both ADPKD (PKD1, maternal line) and ADTKD (UMOD, paternal line); the pathogenic PKD1 variant (c.2180T>C, p.Leu727Pro) was missed by exome sequencing and only identified via long-range PCR amplification and whole-genome sequencing, illustrating a known technical blind spot for PKD1 (six highly homologous pseudogenes) in standard massively parallel sequencing.
papers.novelty_assessment: Case-level illustration of an already-recognized diagnostic-lab pitfall (PKD1 pseudogene interference with exome sequencing), not a new mechanism or population-level finding.
key_findings: Index patient has dual Mendelian kidney disease diagnoses: ADPKD from PKD1 (maternal) and ADTKD from UMOD (paternal)
The causal PKD1 missense variant was not detected by exome sequencing and required traditional long-range amplification plus whole-genome sequencing to resolve
Authors caution that broad, non-specialized use of massively parallel sequencing for PKD1 can produce false-negative or inconclusive results without dedicated methods
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces that a negative exome-sequencing result does not rule out ADPKD given known PKD1 pseudogene-related technical limitations; supports referral to labs with PKD1-specific long-range sequencing capability when clinical suspicion is high despite negative standard genetic testing.
papers.what_happened: A single-family case report shows a patient with both ADPKD (PKD1) and ADTKD (UMOD), where the causal PKD1 variant was missed by exome sequencing and only found via long-range PCR plus whole-genome sequencing.
papers.why_it_matters: Illustrates a well-known but easily forgotten diagnostic-lab limitation: standard exome sequencing can miss PKD1 pathogenic variants due to pseudogene homology, which is relevant to genetic testing labs and clinicians interpreting negative results.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a single case/family illustration of an already-established technical limitation, not new evidence about prevalence or generalizability of missed PKD1 diagnoses.
