papers.title: Prognostic Systematic Reviews: Challenges and Insights-An Example.
papers.abstract_snippet: Methods commentary reflecting on challenges encountered while conducting the authors' own systematic review and meta-analysis of prognostic biomarkers in ADPKD (the same review tracked in this database as pm_42237252), focusing on screening, data extraction, and analysis/interpretation difficulties caused by reporting heterogeneity.
papers.novelty_assessment: A methods/process reflection piece companion to an already-tracked ADPKD biomarker systematic review; contains no new ADPKD clinical or biomarker data.
key_findings: Authors describe methodological lessons from conducting an ADPKD prognostic-biomarker systematic review and meta-analysis (companion to pm_42237252)
Greatest challenges were data analysis/interpretation due to variable outcome reporting across studies, and screening/extraction burden from a large volume of non-primarily-prognostic studies
papers.clinical_implications: None directly; this is guidance for future systematic reviewers, not new ADPKD clinical evidence.
papers.what_happened: The authors of the ADPKD prognostic-biomarker systematic review (pm_42237252) published a separate methods commentary describing challenges encountered while conducting that review.
papers.why_it_matters: Useful for other systematic reviewers but carries no new ADPKD clinical or biomarker findings beyond what pm_42237252 already reported.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a process/methods reflection, not a data-bearing study; it cannot itself be evaluated for clinical evidence strength.

papers.title: Variants and variability - a cohort of Omani children sheds more light on autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Editorial commenting on a cohort study of Omani children with autosomal RECESSIVE polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD), highlighting genotype-phenotype variability.
papers.novelty_assessment: Editorial on an ARPKD (not ADPKD) cohort study; logged per project rule to track ARPKD items at low relevance since findings do not directly apply to ADPKD.
key_findings: Editorial accompanying an Omani pediatric ARPKD cohort study, discussing genotype-phenotype variability in PKHD1-related disease
papers.clinical_implications: None for ADPKD; ARPKD is a distinct, autosomal recessive disease driven by PKHD1, mechanistically and clinically separate from ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2).
papers.what_happened: An editorial discusses a cohort study of ARPKD (autosomal recessive, PKHD1-driven) in Omani children.
papers.why_it_matters: Not directly relevant to ADPKD; logged for tracker completeness given topical adjacency.
papers.what_limits_confidence: ARPKD is a genetically and clinically distinct disease from ADPKD; findings do not generalize to the ADPKD population this tracker monitors.

papers.title: Impacts of Metabolic and Mitochondrial Reprogramming on ADPKD Drug Targets and Repurposing
papers.abstract_snippet: Review of ADPKD-driven metabolic and mitochondrial reprogramming (impaired mitochondrial respiration, glucose/lipid/amino-acid metabolism) as a source of candidate drug targets (mTOR, PPAR family, CYP450) for repurposing FDA-approved drugs, positioned as potential complements or alternatives to tolvaptan.
papers.novelty_assessment: Narrative review (v2 revision of a Dec-2025 preprint) synthesizing existing metabolic/mitochondrial ADPKD literature for drug-repurposing rationale; no new experimental data.
key_findings: Frames ADPKD metabolic/mitochondrial reprogramming as altering both disease-driving pathways (mTOR, PPAR) and drug metabolism (CYP450), relevant to repurposing candidates
Positions repurposed metabolic-pathway drugs as potential tolvaptan complements or alternatives given tolvaptan's cost and hepatotoxicity risk
papers.clinical_implications: None directly actionable; this is a target-identification rationale for future preclinical/repurposing work, not new efficacy evidence.
papers.what_happened: A preprint (v2, originally posted Dec 2025) reviews ADPKD metabolic and mitochondrial reprogramming to propose candidate drug-repurposing targets as complements or alternatives to tolvaptan.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a mechanistic rationale that could guide future preclinical repurposing screens in a disease with only one approved disease-modifying drug.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is an unreviewed narrative-review preprint with no new experimental data or candidate-drug efficacy testing; ADPKD's preclinical-to-clinical translation record is historically weak.

papers.title: DESI-MS-Based Analysis of Drug Distribution in Human Renal Cystic Tissue Using the Chorioallantoic Membrane (CAM) as a 3D In Vivo Model
papers.abstract_snippet: Preclinical methods preprint using desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI) to visualize tissue penetration of benzbromarone (a TMEM16A inhibitor and candidate ADPKD therapeutic) in human renal cyst tissue grafted onto the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM), showing selective drug accumulation along the cyst epithelium where TMEM16A is located.
papers.novelty_assessment: First demonstration of DESI-MSI-based drug-distribution mapping in human ADPKD cyst tissue on a CAM ex vivo/in vivo hybrid platform; a pharmacology/methods advance, not an efficacy study.
key_findings: Benzbromarone, a TMEM16A inhibitor and candidate ADPKD drug, penetrates human renal cyst tissue cultured on the CAM model and selectively accumulates along the cyst epithelium

DESI-MSI combined with high-resolution mass spectrometry and multivariate analysis (UMAP, sparse multinomial classification) could distinguish CAM from cystic tissue and drug-treated from untreated regions
Demonstrates feasibility of the CAM/DESI-MSI platform for studying topical drug distribution in human renal cyst tissue
papers.clinical_implications: None yet; this establishes a tissue-distribution methodology, not therapeutic efficacy or safety data for benzbromarone in ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: A preprint demonstrates that DESI mass spectrometry imaging can visualize benzbromarone (a TMEM16A-inhibiting candidate ADPKD drug) distribution within human renal cyst tissue grown on a chorioallantoic membrane platform, showing selective accumulation at the cyst epithelium.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a new tissue-level tool to check whether candidate ADPKD drugs actually reach their target site in human cyst tissue, which could help de-risk future drug-development decisions.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a drug-distribution/methods demonstration only, with no efficacy, safety, or in vivo systemic pharmacokinetic data, and the CAM ex vivo model has unknown generalizability to human renal drug exposure.

papers.title: Real-world data assessment of the burden of ADPKD: prevalence, clinical profile, and health care costs in a Chilean public health network
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective health-records study (2021-2023) of 98 ADPKD patients in the Araucania-Sur Health Service network in Chile, characterizing demographics, comorbidities, medications, CKD-stage distribution, and annual per-patient healthcare costs (USD 1,477 to 13,075 across CKD stages 1-2 through 5); estimated ADPKD prevalence 1 in 7,784, well below expected epidemiological prevalence, suggesting significant underdiagnosis.
papers.novelty_assessment: First real-world burden-of-disease/cost description for ADPKD in a Chilean public health network; a regional epidemiology contribution rather than a treatment or mechanistic finding.
key_findings: 98 ADPKD patients identified in a 2021-2023 regional health-records review, estimated prevalence 1 in 7,784 (12.8/100,000) -- well below expected general-population ADPKD prevalence (~1/1,000), consistent with substantial underdiagnosis
ADPKD-CKD patients were on average 15 years younger than the general non-ADPKD CKD population
Annual healthcare costs rose sharply with CKD stage: USD 1,477 (stage 1-2) to USD 2,490 (stage 3), 3,785 (stage 4), and 13,075 (stage 5) per patient
Hypertension (56%) and dyslipidemia (32%) were the most common comorbidities; losartan, amlodipine and furosemide were the most-used antihypertensives
papers.clinical_implications: Supports the case for earlier ADPKD detection to reduce downstream cost burden in this health system, but is a single-region descriptive study with small n and preprint status.
papers.what_happened: A preprint describes a retrospective real-world assessment of 98 ADPKD patients in a Chilean public health network, reporting an apparent prevalence well below expected, a younger age at CKD onset than the general CKD population, and steeply rising per-patient costs with CKD stage.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides rare region-specific real-world burden-of-disease and cost data for ADPKD outside the usual US/European registries, and flags likely underdiagnosis.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-region retrospective health-records study with a small cohort (n=98), unreviewed preprint status, and possible ICD-10-coding-based ascertainment bias affecting the prevalence estimate.

papers.title: Gas in a Cyst: Emphysematous Infection in ADPKD Post-Transplant.
papers.abstract_snippet: Short image-based case report (no structured abstract available) describing emphysematous (gas-forming) infection of a native ADPKD cyst in a kidney transplant recipient.
papers.novelty_assessment: Single new case image/report, genuinely new this week but of very narrow scope.
key_findings: Case report of gas-forming (emphysematous) infection in a native ADPKD kidney cyst after transplantation.
No abstract or structured data available -- appears to be a short clinical-image feature.
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces that native cyst infection remains a recognized post-transplant complication in ADPKD, but a single case provides no basis for changing management.
papers.what_happened: A single-patient image-based case report describes an emphysematous (gas-forming) infection of a native ADPKD kidney cyst after transplantation.
papers.why_it_matters: Serves as a reminder to transplant nephrologists of an uncommon but serious native-cyst complication in ADPKD recipients.
papers.what_limits_confidence: N=1 case report with no abstract or methods; provides no generalizable data on incidence, risk factors, or management.

papers.title: Impact of race-based and race-free CKD-EPI equations on estimated glomerular filtration rate in a multicenter retrospective cohort of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Multicenter retrospective cohort of 597 ADPKD patients (515 self-identified Caucasian, 82 African-American) comparing 2009 vs 2021 race-free CKD-EPI equations; median baseline eGFR in Caucasian patients rose from 85.0 to 88.6 mL/min/1.73m2 under the race-free equation, with staging shifts that varied by ethnic group.
papers.novelty_assessment: First ADPKD-specific quantification of the race-free CKD-EPI equation's staging impact in a multi-ethnic cohort; genuinely new this week.
key_findings: 597 ADPKD patients (515 Caucasian, 82 African-American) had eGFR recalculated under 2009 vs 2021 (race-free) CKD-EPI equations.
Median baseline eGFR in Caucasian patients increased from 85.0 to 88.6 mL/min/1.73m2 under the race-free equation.
CKD stage reclassification differed by self-identified ethnic group, with implications for staging-dependent decisions (e.g., tolvaptan eligibility, trial enrollment).
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests that switching eGFR equations can shift a patient's CKD stage and could affect tolvaptan-eligibility or trial-enrollment thresholds that are staged by eGFR; not a treatment-efficacy finding.
papers.what_happened: A multicenter retrospective cohort of 597 ADPKD patients found that switching from the 2009 to the 2021 race-free CKD-EPI equation shifted estimated eGFR and CKD staging, with the effect differing by self-identified ethnic group.
papers.why_it_matters: eGFR-based staging drives tolvaptan-eligibility and trial-enrollment decisions in ADPKD, so a systematic shift from a formula change is operationally relevant even without any new biology.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a retrospective recalculation exercise (not a new physiological finding), the African-American subgroup is comparatively small (n=82), and it says nothing about kidney outcomes or treatment effect.

papers.title: Cefepime-Induced Delirium in a Patient With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Case Report.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report of a 63-year-old woman with ADPKD-related CKD who developed delirium after cefepime, started for a UTI associated with infected renal cysts; symptoms resolved within 24 hours of drug discontinuation (Naranjo score 6, 'probable').
papers.novelty_assessment: New case report this week, but the finding (cefepime neurotoxicity in CKD) is an already well-described drug-safety phenomenon; ADPKD is the incidental CKD etiology, not the subject of the finding.
key_findings: 63-year-old woman with ADPKD-related CKD and an infected renal cyst developed acute delirium 24-48h after starting cefepime for a UTI.
Symptoms resolved within 24 hours of cefepime discontinuation; Naranjo scale classified the association as 'probable' (score 6).
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces general nephrology practice of considering cefepime neurotoxicity and dose-adjusting/avoiding cefepime in patients with reduced kidney function, including ADPKD; not an ADPKD-specific mechanism.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes cefepime-induced delirium in a woman with ADPKD-related CKD being treated for a UTI arising from an infected renal cyst, resolving after drug discontinuation.
papers.why_it_matters: A minor reminder for clinicians to watch for cefepime neurotoxicity when treating cyst infections in ADPKD patients with reduced kidney function.
papers.what_limits_confidence: N=1 case report of a well-established general drug-safety phenomenon; ADPKD is incidental context, not the subject of new evidence.

papers.title: Genome and transcriptome sequencing reveal pathogenic activation of a pseudoexon in PKD1 via a de novo-common variant complex allele.
papers.abstract_snippet: Single-patient case report: a deep intronic de novo single-nucleotide substitution combined with an adjacent common benign SNV created a novel splice donor site activating a 114-bp pseudoexon in PKD1 intron 16, resolving a previously unsolved ADPKD diagnosis via paired genome + transcriptome sequencing.
papers.novelty_assessment: New case-level demonstration this week of a genuinely novel genetic mechanism (two independently-benign variants combining into a pathogenic dinucleotide allele) rather than a previously known pattern.
key_findings: A de novo intronic SNV plus an inherited common SNV in PKD1 intron 16 combined to form a dinucleotide variant that neither alone was predicted to be pathogenic.
The combined variant created a novel splice donor site; RNA-seq confirmed inclusion of a 114-bp pseudoexon with an in-frame premature stop codon.
Resolved a previously unsolved ADPKD diagnosis after years of inconclusive standard genetic testing, via paired genome + transcriptome sequencing.
papers.clinical_implications: Illustrates that genome+transcriptome sequencing can resolve ADPKD cases left unsolved by standard testing, and flags that adjacent 'benign' variants should not automatically be dismissed -- relevant to diagnostic labs handling clinically-suspected but genetically-unconfirmed ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: Paired genome and transcriptome sequencing in a single ADPKD family resolved a previously unsolved diagnosis by showing that a de novo intronic variant plus an adjacent inherited benign variant together activate a pathogenic pseudoexon in PKD1.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to the recognized set of PKD1 diagnostic blind spots (alongside pseudogene homology) that standard exome sequencing can miss, supporting escalation to genome+RNA sequencing in clinically clear but genetically unresolved ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a single-family case report describing a rare variant-combination mechanism; it does not establish how often this mechanism explains other unsolved ADPKD cases.

papers.title: Burden of Potential Kidney Failure in Apparently Asymptomatic Individuals
papers.abstract_snippet: Exome screen of 6,272 individuals evaluated for reasons unrelated to kidney disease found pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variants in 70 CKD-associated genes in 2.7% (168/6,272); PKD1/PKD2 variants accounted for 2.2% of the cohort (138 individuals), second only to COL4A3/4/5.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly surfaced preprint (posted 2026-06-16, first indexed in this scan's Europe PMC sweep); population-scale incidental-finding estimate for PKD1/PKD2 carriage is a fresh data point though the underlying exomes were collected earlier.
key_findings: Among 6,272 exomes obtained for non-kidney indications, 168 individuals (2.7%) carried a pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variant in one of 70 CKD-associated genes.
PKD1/PKD2 variants were found in 138 individuals (2.2% of the full cohort), the largest single-gene-family contributor after COL4A3/4/5 (0.5%).
Authors argue genetic predisposition to CKD, including ADPKD, is underestimated in asymptomatic populations.
papers.clinical_implications: Hypothesis-generating support for opportunistic genomic screening picking up unsuspected ADPKD-causing variants; does not by itself establish penetrance, phenotype severity, or a case for population screening.
papers.what_happened: An unreviewed preprint screening 6,272 exomes obtained for unrelated reasons found pathogenic/likely-pathogenic PKD1/PKD2 variants in 2.2% of individuals, without confirming a clinical ADPKD phenotype in carriers.
papers.why_it_matters: If replicated with phenotype confirmation, this would inform how common unrecognized ADPKD-causing genotypes are in the general population -- relevant to screening-policy discussions.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a preprint (not peer-reviewed) with no full methods available in the abstract, no phenotypic confirmation that variant carriers have or will develop ADPKD, and variant pathogenicity calls from exome pipelines carry a known false-positive rate.

papers.title: Functional characterization of the PMM2 p.Arg238His variant supports a modifier role in polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract_snippet: Targeted 63-gene PKD sequencing panel in 418 PKD patients identified 4 unrelated carriers of PMM2 c.713G>A (p.Arg238His); recombinant expression showed the variant has reduced thermal stability and altered kinetics consistent with partial N-glycosylation-pathway dysfunction, supporting a genetic-modifier role.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly surfaced preprint (posted 2026-06-08); first reported in vitro functional characterization of this specific PMM2 variant in a PKD context.
key_findings: A 63-gene NGS panel in 418 PKD patients identified 4 unrelated heterozygous carriers of PMM2 p.Arg238His.
Recombinant expression in E. coli showed the mutant protein has reduced thermal stability and altered Km/Vmax kinetics versus wild-type.
Authors propose PMM2 as a candidate genetic modifier contributing to phenotypic variability in PKD, not a primary disease gene.
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests extending diagnostic NGS panels to include glycosylation-pathway genes like PMM2 could eventually help explain variable ADPKD severity, but this is not yet actionable for patient counseling.
papers.what_happened: A preprint reports in vitro biochemical evidence that a rare PMM2 variant found in 4 of 418 PKD patients has destabilizing effects consistent with a mild N-glycosylation defect, proposed as a genetic modifier of PKD severity.
papers.why_it_matters: Genetic modifiers help explain why ADPKD severity varies so much between patients with the same PKD1/PKD2 genotype -- a long-standing open question in the field.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Unreviewed preprint; only 4 variant carriers identified from a general PKD cohort with unclear ADPKD-vs-other-PKD-subtype breakdown, and in vitro protein kinetics do not establish a clinical severity effect.

papers.title: Collecting Duct-Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles Deliver Pkd2 mRNA to Restore Polycystin-2 and Attenuate ADPKD
papers.abstract_snippet: Collecting-duct-targeted lipid nanoparticles delivering Pkd2 mRNA (CD-mPkd2) induced reversal of established cystic disease, restored renal architecture, and reduced fibrosis/inflammation in Pkd2-deficient mice with repeat dosing, without detectable off-target toxicity; a single dose also reduced cyst burden in a Pkd1-deficient background.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly surfaced preprint (posted 2026-06-05); first disclosure of collecting-duct-targeted mRNA replacement reversing established cystic disease in a Pkd2-deficient mouse model, joining the CRISPRa/mRNA-LNP gene-restoration cluster already tracked from prior scans.
key_findings: A collecting-duct-targeting-peptide lipid nanoparticle (CD LNP) delivered Pkd2 mRNA more efficiently to cyst-lining renal epithelia than non-targeted LNPs.
Repeated dosing in Pkd2-deficient mice reversed established cystic disease, restored renal architecture, and reduced fibrosis/inflammation, without detectable off-target toxicity.
A single dose also reduced cyst burden and improved renal function in a distinct (Pkd1-deficient) genetic background.
papers.clinical_implications: None yet -- this is a preclinical gene-replacement proof-of-concept in mice; no human dosing, safety, or durability data exist.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in abstract; mRNA/LNP delivery platform likely has associated IP interest

papers.what_happened: A preprint reports that collecting-duct-targeted lipid nanoparticles delivering Pkd2 mRNA reversed established cystic disease and restored renal architecture in Pkd2-deficient mice, with a single dose also reducing cyst burden in Pkd1-deficient mice.
papers.why_it_matters: Direct mRNA-based polycystin restoration, if it eventually translated to humans, would address the underlying genetic defect rather than downstream pathways -- a strategically important modality alongside the CRISPRa and RNA-silencing programs already in the pipeline tracker.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Unreviewed preprint reporting mouse-only data; ADPKD preclinical gene-therapy findings have a historically weak record of translating to human efficacy, and no durability, dosing-interval, or long-term safety data are presented.

papers.title: CRISPR activation of endogenous PKD1 increases polycystin-1 levels and suppresses cellular features of ADPKD
papers.abstract_snippet: CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) targeting the PKD1 promoter increased Pkd1/PKD1 mRNA and PC1 protein in mouse Pkd1-RC/- cells and primary human ADPKD patient-derived renal epithelial cells, reducing proliferation and in vitro cyst formation in 3D culture; effect was heterogeneous across human donor lines.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly surfaced preprint (posted 2026-05-25); demonstrates CRISPRa-driven reduction of in vitro cyst formation and validation in primary human ADPKD patient-derived cells, extending the CRISPRa-for-PKD1 concept already tracked via pm_42068455 (a plasmid-miniaturization methods paper from the same research area).
key_findings: CRISPRa targeting the PKD1 promoter increased PC1 protein and reduced proliferation and 3D in vitro cyst formation in a mouse Pkd1-RC/- collecting-duct cell model.
Pkd1 activation improved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced glycolytic dependency, and normalized cAMP/cMyc/pCreb/pErk/pYap1 signaling associated with cystogenesis.
CRISPRa successfully activated PKD1 in primary renal epithelial cells from human ADPKD donor kidneys, though the response was heterogeneous (significant upregulation in 2 of the tested lines).
papers.clinical_implications: None yet -- proof-of-concept only in cell culture; no in vivo cyst-burden or kidney-function data, and human-cell response variability suggests translational uncertainty.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in abstract; possible institutional IP interest in CRISPRa platform

papers.what_happened: A preprint shows CRISPR activation of the endogenous PKD1 promoter raises polycystin-1 levels and reduces in vitro cyst formation in mouse cells and primary human ADPKD patient-derived renal cells, though the human-cell response was inconsistent across donors.
papers.why_it_matters: CRISPRa-based upregulation of a patient's own PKD1 allele is a strategically distinct gene-therapy approach from mRNA replacement or RNA silencing, and this is an early but concrete step toward showing it works in human ADPKD cells.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Unreviewed preprint with in vitro-only data (no animal cyst-burden model in this abstract), heterogeneous response across human donor lines undercuts generalizability, and ADPKD preclinical gene-therapy work has a historically weak translation record.

papers.title: ParaDISM: Precise mapping of short reads to genes with highly homologous regions
papers.abstract_snippet: A new short-read alignment pipeline (ParaDISM) reduces misalignment-driven false variant calls in genes with highly homologous paralogs/pseudogenes; validated computationally and applied to 18 ADPKD short-read datasets (16 exomes, 2 gene panels), where it outperformed bowtie2/bwa-mem/minimap2 for PKD1 pseudogene-region variant calling.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly surfaced preprint (posted 2026-05-21); a diagnostics-tooling advance directly addressing the PKD1 pseudogene sequencing blind spot flagged in other recent case reports (e.g. pm_42497974).
key_findings: ParaDISM is an open-source pipeline that uses multiple sequence alignment of reference paralogs to disambiguate short-read placement in highly homologous regions.

Benchmarked on GIAB HG002 and on 18 real ADPKD short-read datasets (16 exomes, 2 panels), it reduced misalignment artifacts and false variant calls versus standard aligners (bowtie2, bwa-mem, minimap2).
Applied to the PKD1 locus, a gene with six highly homologous pseudogenes that are a known source of false-negative/false-positive genetic testing results.
papers.clinical_implications: Could improve diagnostic-lab accuracy for PKD1 variant calling from standard short-read sequencing if adopted, potentially reducing the false-negative rate that motivates long-range PCR/whole-genome workarounds; not yet clinically validated or deployed.
papers.what_happened: A preprint introduces ParaDISM, an open-source short-read alignment pipeline that reduces misalignment-driven false variant calls in highly homologous genes, and shows improved performance over standard aligners on 18 real ADPKD short-read datasets at the PKD1 locus.
papers.why_it_matters: Directly targets a recognized ADPKD diagnostic blind spot (PKD1 pseudogene homology causing missed or false variant calls in standard sequencing), which could improve genetic testing yield if validated and adopted by diagnostic labs.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Unreviewed preprint; the ADPKD validation cohort is small (18 datasets) and methodological superiority in read alignment has not yet been shown to change actual diagnostic yield in a clinical lab setting.

papers.title: Understanding Variation Between Kidney Centres in Implementation of Tolvaptan in the Management of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Multiple Case Study
papers.abstract_snippet: Qualitative multiple case study of 3 UK NHS kidney centres (12 clinician interviews, 23 clinic observations, 8 documents; Dec 2024-Sep 2025) analyzed via the CFIR implementation-science framework, finding that centralized, specialist-led tolvaptan pathways enabled more consistent, timely, guideline-concordant prescribing than distributed/hybrid pathways.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly surfaced preprint (posted 2026-05-21); a qualitative implementation-science study, not a new clinical or biological finding, but a fresh angle on a previously quantitatively-documented UK tolvaptan prescribing-variation problem.
key_findings: Qualitative case study of 3 NHS kidney centres selected for differing tolvaptan prescribing practices, using semi-structured interviews, clinic observations, and document analysis mapped to the CFIR framework.

Centralized, specialist-led pathways (Case 2) enabled earlier, more systematic tolvaptan initiation than a distributed pathway with less experienced staff (Case 1), which showed delays and variable eligibility application.
One centre (Case 3) reported occasional off-guideline tolvaptan use, contributing to higher relative prescribing volume.
papers.clinical_implications: Suggests centralized, specialist-led care pathways may reduce inequitable access to tolvaptan; an operations/service-design finding rather than evidence about tolvaptan's efficacy or safety.
papers.what_happened: A qualitative implementation-science study of 3 UK kidney centres found that centralized, specialist-led tolvaptan care pathways were associated with more consistent and timely guideline-concordant prescribing than distributed pathways.
papers.why_it_matters: Complements prior quantitative UK real-world tolvaptan data (e.g. Marshall propensity-weighted cohort, McFarlane C-MAJOR registry) by identifying an organizational mechanism -- care-pathway centralization -- that may explain some prescribing variation and access inequity.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Unreviewed preprint with only 3 case-study centres and a qualitative design; findings on 'what works' for implementation are context-specific and not generalizable to other health systems without further testing.

papers.title: PKD1 upstream open reading frames affect Polycystin-1 expression and polycystic kidney disease phenotypes.
papers.abstract_snippet: Two humanized PKD1 5'UTR mouse models with uORF start-codon edits ('delta-uORF') show 2-4-fold increased PC1 protein expression and prevention of kidney cysts in Dnajb11 and Pkd1-missense backgrounds; steric antisense oligonucleotides blocking PKD1 uORF1 also substantially increase PC1 expression in vitro.
papers.novelty_assessment: First disclosure of PKD1 uORFs as a translational brake on PC1 dosage and of uORF-blocking ASOs as a candidate strategy to raise PC1 expression; genuinely new mechanism and therapeutic angle this week.
key_findings: PKD1 5'UTR contains conserved, actively-translated upstream open reading frames (uORFs) that suppress downstream PC1 translation.
Removing uORF start codons ('delta-uORF') in humanized mouse models increased PC1 protein 2-4-fold and prevented kidney cyst formation in both Dnajb11 and Pkd1-missense mouse models.
Steric antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) blocking PKD1 uORF1 substantially increased PC1 expression in vitro, suggesting a druggable route to raise PC1 dosage without gene replacement.
papers.clinical_implications: Proposes a mechanistically distinct therapeutic strategy for ADPKD/ADPLD caused by reduced PC1 dosage (raising expression from the remaining functional allele via uORF blockade), but this is mouse-model and in-vitro-only work; no human PC1 dosage, safety, or delivery data exist yet.
papers.what_happened: A JCI paper identified translation-suppressing upstream open reading frames in the PKD1 5'UTR and showed that removing them, or blocking them with antisense oligonucleotides, raises Polycystin-1 protein expression and prevents cysts in mouse models.
papers.why_it_matters: Offers a mechanistically new way to increase PC1 dosage from the remaining functional allele, which is a long-standing therapeutic goal for ADPKD caused by PKD1 haploinsufficiency.
papers.what_limits_confidence: All efficacy data are from mouse models and in-vitro ASO experiments; ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record, and no human dosing, delivery, or safety data exist yet.

papers.title: Comparison of eGFR based on Serum Cystatin C or Creatinine in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective Mayo Clinic cohort of 697 ADPKD patients comparing race-free CKD-EPI creatinine, cystatin C, and creatinine-cystatin C equations against height-adjusted TKV and, in a 50-patient subset, iothalamate-measured GFR; the combined creatinine-cystatin C equation was least biased and most precise versus mGFR.
papers.novelty_assessment: Full-paper follow-up to a Mayo Clinic AJKD SCM2026 abstract (G-528) tracked in a prior scan; now presents complete methodology and an mGFR-validated subset, genuinely new disclosure this week.
key_findings: In 697 ADPKD patients, htTKV correlated moderately with eGFR from all three race-free CKD-EPI equations (r -0.53 to -0.54 overall), with stronger correlation in higher Mayo Imaging Classification (MIC) risk subclasses.

In a 50-patient subset with iothalamate-measured GFR, the combined creatinine-cystatin C equation was the least biased (mean bias -0.86 mL/min/1.73m2) and most precise (P30 84%) compared to either single-marker equation.
All three eGFR equations performed similarly in their association with htTKV, so equation choice does not materially change TKV-based risk stratification.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports using the combined creatinine-cystatin C CKD-EPI equation when a more accurate eGFR is needed in ADPKD research or borderline staging decisions, but this is a retrospective single-center analysis and does not address treatment or outcomes.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective Mayo Clinic study of 697 ADPKD patients compared three race-free CKD-EPI eGFR equations against height-adjusted TKV and, in a 50-patient subset, against measured GFR, finding the combined creatinine-cystatin C equation was the most accurate.
papers.why_it_matters: TKV and eGFR both drive ADPKD risk stratification and trial eligibility, so knowing which eGFR formula best approximates measured GFR helps standardize research and borderline clinical staging.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center retrospective design, and the mGFR-validated comparison subset is small (n=50); the study says nothing about treatment effect or long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Modulation of Cyst Growth in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Cell Physiology
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review synthesizing cAMP/Ca2+/purinergic signaling, disturbed cell turnover, metabolic reprogramming, and HIF-1alpha as interconnected drivers of ADPKD cyst growth, and surveying corresponding therapeutic strategies under investigation.
papers.novelty_assessment: New synthesis review published this week; does not report new primary data, so scientific novelty is low despite publication novelty being high.
key_findings: Proposes that ADPKD cyst growth arises from a self-reinforcing network of cAMP/Ca2+/purinergic signaling, disturbed cell turnover (proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy, ferroptosis), and metabolic reprogramming, integrated by HIF-1alpha.
Surveys candidate therapeutic strategies spanning polycystin-restoration, cAMP/purinergic modulation, chloride-secretion inhibition, metabolic targeting, and HIF-1alpha pathway intervention.
Argues that no single-node therapy is likely sufficient and that multi-nodal combination approaches will likely be required.
papers.clinical_implications: A conceptual synthesis for research prioritization, not a clinical finding; does not itself provide evidence for any specific intervention.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review synthesized current mechanistic understanding of ADPKD cyst growth signaling and metabolism and surveyed corresponding candidate therapeutic strategies.
papers.why_it_matters: Offers researchers a consolidated framework for how converging signaling and metabolic pathways drive cyst growth, useful for prioritizing mechanistic research.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a narrative review with no new primary data or systematic methodology, so it carries no independent evidentiary weight.

papers.title: Plasma Amino Acid Signatures Associated with Disease Progression and Hypertension in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Targeted Metabolomics and Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract_snippet: Targeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics of 38 plasma amino acids in 203 ADPKD patients stratified by disease progression (rapid vs. slow) and hypertension status, with SVM models predicting outcomes from amino acid profiles; valine, glutamic acid, homocitrulline and methylhistidines elevated in rapid progression and hypertension.
papers.novelty_assessment: New exploratory biomarker/ML study published this week; extends the growing metabolomics-in-ADPKD literature but is single-cohort and not externally validated.
key_findings: Targeted metabolomic profiling of 38 plasma amino acids in 203 ADPKD patients stratified by rapid vs. slow disease progression and by hypertension status.
Valine, glutamic acid, homocitrulline, and methylhistidines were elevated in both rapid-progression and hypertensive groups; isoleucine and citrulline were elevated only in rapid progressors.
Support Vector Machine models combining clinical and amino-acid data were developed to predict progression/hypertension status.
papers.clinical_implications: Exploratory biomarker signal for research prioritization only; amino acid panels are not validated or actionable for clinical risk-stratification of ADPKD progression today.
papers.what_happened: A targeted metabolomics study of 203 ADPKD patients identified plasma amino acid signatures associated with rapid disease progression and hypertension, and built SVM models to predict these groups.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds a candidate non-genetic biomarker panel for ADPKD progression risk, a space still dominated by TKV and eGFR-slope measures.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center, cross-sectional/retrospective design with no external validation cohort; predictive-model performance from small feature sets is prone to overfitting, and 'progression' groups are not defined against a hard clinical endpoint in the abstract.

papers.title: From cystogenesis to carcinogenesis in ADPKD: risk modeling and a multistep precision surveillance.
papers.abstract_snippet: Letter/perspective proposing a risk-modeling and multistep precision-surveillance framework for renal cell carcinoma risk in ADPKD; no primary data reported.
papers.novelty_assessment: New opinion/letter this week proposing a conceptual surveillance framework; not a new scientific event or dataset.
key_findings: Proposes conceptual links between ADPKD cystogenesis pathways and renal cell carcinoma risk.
Advocates for a multistep, risk-stratified precision surveillance approach for RCC in ADPKD patients.
No primary data, cohort, or validation of the proposed model is presented (PubMed record has no abstract; classified as a Letter).
papers.clinical_implications: A conceptual proposal only; does not itself provide evidence to change RCC surveillance practice in ADPKD.
papers.what_happened: A letter/perspective proposed a conceptual risk-modeling and multistep precision-surveillance framework for renal cell carcinoma risk in ADPKD patients.
papers.why_it_matters: RCC surveillance strategy in ADPKD is not well standardized, so a proposed framework could seed future validation studies.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is an opinion/letter with no primary data, cohort, or validation reported (no abstract indexed in PubMed); it is a proposal, not evidence.

papers.title: GANAB-related Polycystic Kidney Disease Mimicking the Cutaneous Findings of Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report of a 59-year-old woman with GANAB-related ADPKD presenting with cafe-au-lait macules and axillary freckling mimicking neurofibromatosis type 1; NF1/SPRED1 testing was negative and genome sequencing found a pathogenic GANAB variant (c.181C>T, p.Arg61*).
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly published case report this week describing a diagnostic pitfall in a rare ADPKD genotype.
key_findings: A 59-year-old woman with GANAB-related ADPKD had cafe-au-lait macules and axillary freckling, cutaneous findings not previously reported as a feature of GANAB-related disease and classically associated with NF1.
Targeted NF1 and SPRED1 gene testing was negative; genome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic GANAB germline variant.
Authors caution the observation is based on a single individual.
papers.clinical_implications: A diagnostic-pitfall alert for clinicians evaluating cafe-au-lait macules, relevant mainly to the rare GANAB subtype of ADPKD/ADPLD, not typical PKD1/PKD2 disease.
papers.what_happened: A case report described a woman with GANAB-related ADPKD who had cafe-au-lait macules and axillary freckling mimicking neurofibromatosis type 1, resolved by genome sequencing to a pathogenic GANAB variant.
papers.why_it_matters: Highlights a possible diagnostic pitfall where a rare ADPKD-gene skin phenotype could be mistaken for NF1.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report in the rare GANAB genotype; authors themselves caution generalizability, and it does not apply to typical PKD1/PKD2 ADPKD.

papers.title: Compression of the Porta Hepatis in a Patient With Hepatic Cysts Secondary to Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Case Report.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report of a 67-year-old woman with ADPKD and large hepatic cysts causing porta hepatis compression and biliary strictures requiring stenting, without other accompanying liver disease.
papers.novelty_assessment: Single new case report this week; illustrates a rare but recognized complication of ADPKD-associated polycystic liver disease.
key_findings: A 67-year-old woman with ADPKD developed porta hepatis compression and biliary strictures from large hepatic cysts, requiring biliary stenting.
No other accompanying liver disease was present; presentation attributed to mass effect from polycystic liver involvement.
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces that symptomatic hepatic cyst mass effect, though uncommon, should remain on the differential for biliary obstruction in ADPKD patients with significant liver cyst burden.
papers.what_happened: A single case report described porta hepatis compression and biliary strictures from hepatic cysts in an ADPKD patient, managed with biliary stenting.
papers.why_it_matters: A reminder that polycystic liver disease can rarely cause mechanical biliary complications.
papers.what_limits_confidence: n=1 case report; provides no generalizable evidence about incidence, risk factors, or management effectiveness.

papers.title: Letter to the Editor: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is not a risk factor for scoliosis.
papers.abstract_snippet: Letter to the editor disputing a prior claim that ADPKD is a risk factor for scoliosis; epub Dec 2025, now assigned to the August 2026 print issue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: epub'd December 2025; only now receiving August 2026 issue pagination.
key_findings: A letter argues against a prior claim that ADPKD is a risk factor for scoliosis.
papers.clinical_implications: Minimal; a correspondence item, not new primary data.
papers.what_happened: A letter to the editor argues ADPKD is not a risk factor for scoliosis, countering a prior published claim.
papers.why_it_matters: Minor correspondence relevant to clinicians managing musculoskeletal comorbidities in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Correspondence item with no primary data or methods; epub'd 8 months ago and only now issue-paginated, not a new scientific event.

papers.title: Horseshoe kidney and polycystic horseshoe kidney: a forensic autopsy-based study in Portugal.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective forensic autopsy series (n=31,325) in Portugal (2017-2022) estimating prevalence of horseshoe kidney and the rare comorbid finding of polycystic horseshoe kidney.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: epub'd January 2026, only now issue-paginated to August 2026.
key_findings: Large forensic autopsy series (n=31,325) in Portugal used to estimate prevalence of horseshoe kidney and the rare comorbid entity polycystic horseshoe kidney.
papers.clinical_implications: Descriptive prevalence data only; does not inform ADPKD management or typical-genotype patients.
papers.what_happened: A Portuguese forensic autopsy series of 31,325 cases estimated the prevalence of horseshoe kidney and the rare comorbid finding of polycystic horseshoe kidney.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides population-level anatomic prevalence data relevant to radiologists and forensic pathologists.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Polycystic horseshoe kidney is an exceedingly rare anatomic variant; findings are not generalizable to typical ADPKD anatomy or progression.

papers.title: Polycystin-2 (PC2): structural insights and its role in disease pathogenesis.
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review of PC2 structure, localization (ER, plasma membrane, cilium), and regulatory mechanisms across renal and extra-renal disease.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: epub'd February 2026.
key_findings: Narrative synthesis of PC2 structural features and disease-relevant regulatory mechanisms; no new primary data.
papers.clinical_implications: Background synthesis only; no direct clinical actionability.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review summarized PC2 structural biology and its role across renal and extra-renal disease.
papers.why_it_matters: Consolidates mechanistic background useful for researchers studying polycystin channel biology.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no new primary data or systematic methodology; stale, epub'd 6 months ago.

papers.title: A HaloTag Knock-In Resource for In Vivo and In Vitro Analysis of Endogenous Polycystin-2 Localization, Turnover, and Transport.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: New HaloTag knock-in mouse/cell resource enables direct visualization of endogenous PC2 localization, turnover and transport; establishes PC1-dependent and Tulp3-dependent control of PC2 ciliary targeting.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: epub'd February 2026, only now issue-paginated.
key_findings: A new HaloTag knock-in resource enables quantitative in vivo/in vitro visualization of endogenous PC2 localization, turnover, and transport.
PC2 ciliary targeting is shown to be PC1-dependent and Tulp3-dependent.
papers.clinical_implications: Research tool only; no direct clinical application, but may accelerate future mechanistic ADPKD studies.
papers.what_happened: Researchers developed a HaloTag knock-in resource that allows direct visualization of endogenous polycystin-2 localization, turnover, and transport in mice and cells.
papers.why_it_matters: A validated tool like this could accelerate future mechanistic studies of polycystin trafficking, an area with historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Pure methods/tool paper with no disease-modifying data; stale, epub'd 6 months ago.

papers.title: Disruption of Polycystin Ciliary Localization and Channel Function by Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease-Causing Polycystin-1 Variants.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Functional assays across pathogenic PC1 variants show disrupted ciliary trafficking or channel function; some variants' trafficking/function was restored by low-temperature culture.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: epub'd February 2026, only now issue-paginated.
key_findings: A systematic functional assay of pathogenic PC1 variants shows each disrupts either ciliary trafficking or channel function.
Low-temperature culture partially restored trafficking/function for some variants, a proof-of-concept folding-rescue observation.
papers.clinical_implications: Could eventually support functional variant classification in genetic counseling, but the low-temperature rescue finding is an in-vitro proof-of-concept, not a therapeutic strategy.
papers.what_happened: Researchers systematically assayed pathogenic PC1 variants and found each disrupted either ciliary trafficking or channel function, with low-temperature culture partially rescuing some variants.
papers.why_it_matters: Functional variant assays could eventually help classify variants of uncertain significance, and the folding-rescue phenomenon nominates a mechanistic strategy for future drug discovery.
papers.what_limits_confidence: In-vitro proof-of-concept only; low-temperature rescue is not a translatable intervention, and ADPKD preclinical mechanistic findings have a historically weak record of clinical translation.

papers.title: Advanced MRI methods for children and young adults with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) to support future multi-center clinical trials.
papers.abstract_snippet: Review of advanced MRI methods for ARPKD (autosomal RECESSIVE, not ADPKD) in children/young adults, aimed at supporting future multi-center trial endpoints.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-07-28), but concerns ARPKD, a distinct recessive disease; logged per ARPKD-adjacency rule.
key_findings: Reviews advanced MRI methods (e.g., TKV, fibrosis imaging) proposed to support future ARPKD multi-center trials.
papers.clinical_implications: Not directly applicable to ADPKD; pediatric ARPKD imaging methodology may only partially generalize to ADPKD imaging science.
papers.what_happened: A review proposed advanced MRI methods to support future multi-center ARPKD clinical trials.
papers.why_it_matters: Imaging biomarker methodology work is relevant to the polycystic kidney disease field broadly, though ARPKD is genetically and clinically distinct from ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Concerns autosomal RECESSIVE PKD, not ADPKD; findings and imaging protocols may not directly generalize to the adult ADPKD population this tracker follows.

papers.title: A cross model single-cell atlas reveals conserved involvement of osteopontin in polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Cross-model single-cell atlas of multiple PKD mouse models identifies osteopontin as a conserved cellular/molecular feature despite heterogeneity in causal gene, onset, and progression rate.
papers.novelty_assessment: Full-paper publication this week (epub 2026-07-28) of a study previously circulated as a bioRxiv preprint (PPR1088133, posted Sep 2025).
key_findings: A cross-model single-cell atlas spanning multiple mouse PKD models identifies osteopontin as a conserved cellular/molecular signature.
Confirms that PKD mouse models show substantial heterogeneity in gene mutated, onset, and progression, mirroring human disease variability.
papers.clinical_implications: Nominates osteopontin as a candidate conserved biomarker/mechanistic node, but this is a mouse-model atlas; no human ADPKD clinical validation yet.
papers.what_happened: A cross-model single-cell atlas of multiple mouse PKD models identified osteopontin as a conserved molecular feature across heterogeneous disease models.
papers.why_it_matters: A conserved marker across heterogeneous preclinical models is a reasonable hypothesis-generating candidate for further biomarker or mechanistic work.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Entirely mouse-model based; ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record, and no human validation is reported here.

papers.title: β-hydroxybutyrate: A Renoprotective Hormone In Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Endocrinology and Metabolism
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review from the Weimbs lab arguing ADPKD is a metabolic disorder with impaired mitochondrial function and pathological reliance on glucose, and positioning BHB/ketogenic strategies as renoprotective.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-07-30), but a narrative review, not new primary data.
key_findings: Reviews mechanistic and observational evidence for a metabolic/mitochondrial basis of ADPKD progression.
Argues BHB and ketogenic dietary strategies are renoprotective in ADPKD.
papers.clinical_implications: Narrative review from a lab with an established research and commercial interest in ketogenic/BHB interventions for ADPKD; should not be read as independent confirmation of clinical benefit.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Author (Weimbs) has prior disclosed commercial/research ties to ketogenic and BHB-based ADPKD interventions tracked in this system; independence of this review is limited

papers.what_happened: A narrative review by the Weimbs lab framed ADPKD as a metabolic disorder and positioned beta-hydroxybutyrate as a renoprotective hormone.
papers.why_it_matters: Continues to build the mechanistic case for ketogenic/BHB dietary strategies, an active area of patient and commercial interest in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A narrative review, not new controlled clinical data, authored by a group with an established research/commercial stake in ketogenic ADPKD interventions; title framing ('renoprotective hormone') overstates what is proven in humans.

papers.title: Renal Cyst Sclerotherapy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Long-Term Follow-Up and Evaluation in a Porcine Bladder Model.
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective review of 567 cysts sclerosed with sodium tetradecyl sulfate in 306 ADPKD patients (2014-2022) plus a porcine bladder model investigating mechanism of action.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-07-29); large single-arm retrospective series is the largest sclerotherapy cohort reported to date in this tracker.
key_findings: Retrospective single-arm review of 567 cysts sclerosed in 306 ADPKD patients over an 8-year period, assessing volume reduction related to mass-effect symptoms.
A companion porcine bladder model was used to investigate the mechanism of sclerotherapy-induced volume reduction.
papers.clinical_implications: Could inform practice for symptomatic mass-effect management (a supportive/palliative procedure) but is not a disease-modifying intervention and has no comparator arm.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective single-center review of 567 renal cysts sclerosed in 306 ADPKD patients evaluated long-term volume reduction, supported by a porcine bladder model investigating mechanism.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides the largest reported ADPKD cyst-sclerotherapy case series to date, potentially informing procedural management of mass-effect symptoms.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective, single-arm, baseline-only design with no comparator group; addresses symptomatic mass effect only, not disease-modifying kidney-function outcomes.

papers.title: Phosphate and Phosphate Transporters in Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review by Torres and colleagues on phosphate handling and phosphate transporters in polycystic kidney disease, contextualizing recent dietary-phosphate/cyst-growth preclinical findings.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-07-30); complements the previously tracked Jansson et al. Pkd1RC/RC + Slc34a1 preclinical phosphate paper (pm_42024440).
key_findings: Narrative review synthesizing phosphate handling and phosphate-transporter biology in the context of polycystic kidney disease cyst growth.
papers.clinical_implications: Research-prioritization value; ties together an emerging phosphate/cystogenesis mechanistic thread but offers no new clinical data or intervention.
papers.what_happened: Torres and colleagues published a narrative review on phosphate and phosphate-transporter biology in polycystic kidney disease.
papers.why_it_matters: Consolidates an emerging mechanistic thread linking dietary phosphate handling to cyst growth, relevant for research prioritization.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review with no new primary data; authored by investigators closely tied to the underlying preclinical program being reviewed.

papers.title: Peritoneal Dialysis Outcomes in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Retrospective USRDS cohort of ESKD patients (>=30yo) comparing peritoneal dialysis outcomes for ADPKD vs. non-ADPKD patients, addressing clinician hesitancy around mechanical PD complications in ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-07-31); large national registry analysis directly addressing a common clinical counseling question.
key_findings: A retrospective USRDS cohort of ESKD patients aged 30+ compared peritoneal dialysis outcomes between ADPKD and non-ADPKD patients.
Addresses whether clinician hesitancy about PD in ADPKD (due to concerns for mechanical complications and technique failure) is supported by outcomes data.
papers.clinical_implications: Directly relevant to dialysis-modality counseling for ADPKD patients approaching ESKD; a practice-relevant registry study, though retrospective and observational.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective USRDS registry analysis compared peritoneal dialysis outcomes between ADPKD and non-ADPKD ESKD patients aged 30 and older.
papers.why_it_matters: Addresses a real-world dialysis-modality counseling question for ADPKD patients, who are often considered good PD candidates but face clinician hesitancy over mechanical complication concerns.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective registry design cannot fully account for unmeasured confounding in modality selection (e.g., abdominal cyst burden, prior surgeries) that may drive both PD candidacy and outcomes.

papers.title: Combination siRNA delivery as a therapeutic strategy for ADPKD.
papers.abstract_snippet: TMEM16A and MCP-1 are consistently upregulated in cyst-lining collecting duct epithelia across mouse, pig, and human ADPKD models; combination siRNA silencing tested in human ADPKD patient-derived cells.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly disclosed via PubMed this week (preprint posted 2026-07-21, PubMed-indexed 2026-08-01); not yet peer reviewed.
key_findings: TMEM16A (cyst-lining epithelial expansion) and MCP-1 (inflammatory macrophage recruitment) are consistently upregulated across murine, porcine, and human ADPKD cyst-lining epithelia.
Individual silencing of either target alone was insufficient in human ADPKD patient cells, motivating a combination siRNA strategy.
papers.clinical_implications: Early-stage combination gene-silencing concept with human patient-cell validation; still far from clinical testing.
papers.what_happened: A preprint reported that TMEM16A and MCP-1 are jointly upregulated across ADPKD cyst-lining epithelia in multiple species, and tested combination siRNA silencing in patient-derived cells.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to the pipeline of novel gene-silencing/RNA-therapeutic concepts targeting cyst epithelial and inflammatory pathways in ADPKD.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, not yet peer reviewed; in-vitro patient-cell data only, with the historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record in ADPKD.

papers.title: Unmasking Early Renal Fibrosis in Polycystic Kidney Disease Using Noninvasive Precision Molecular MRI of Collagen.
papers.abstract_snippet: A collagen-targeted molecular MRI contrast agent (Gd-hProCA32.Collagen) is proposed to image early renal fibrosis non-invasively in PKD before irreversible structural/functional decline.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly disclosed via PubMed this week (preprint posted 2026-07-20, PubMed-indexed 2026-08-01); not yet peer reviewed.
key_findings: Reports development of a collagen-targeted protein MRI contrast agent intended to enable precision molecular imaging of early renal fibrosis in PKD.
papers.clinical_implications: Preclinical imaging-tool development only; no ADPKD patient data reported in this abstract.
papers.what_happened: A preprint described a new collagen-targeted molecular MRI contrast agent intended to non-invasively detect early renal fibrosis in PKD.
papers.why_it_matters: A validated early-fibrosis imaging biomarker could help risk-stratify patients before irreversible decline, complementing TKV-based tools.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, not yet peer reviewed; preclinical imaging-agent development stage, with no reported ADPKD human data yet.

papers.title: Success of Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy with Variable-view Rigid Endoscopy for Large Polycystic Liver in a Patient with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case report describing a successful total laparoscopic hysterectomy using variable-view rigid endoscopy in a patient with large polycystic liver secondary to ADPKD.
papers.novelty_assessment: Newly disclosed this week (PubMed-indexed 2026-08-01); a single surgical case report.
key_findings: A surgical technique using variable-view rigid endoscopy enabled successful laparoscopic hysterectomy despite a large polycystic liver from ADPKD.
papers.clinical_implications: Illustrates a technical approach to a challenging surgical scenario; not generalizable practice-changing evidence.
papers.what_happened: A case report described a successful laparoscopic hysterectomy technique in an ADPKD patient with a large polycystic liver.
papers.why_it_matters: Offers a technical option for gynecologic surgeons managing patients with significant polycystic liver burden.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report; provides no generalizable evidence about technique safety or efficacy across patients.

papers.title: Functional vs Structural Renal Outcomes of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.
papers.abstract_snippet: Systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence on SGLT2 inhibitor functional (eGFR) and structural (TKV) renal outcomes in ADPKD; PubMed/Embase/Scopus searched through May 2026.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-08-03); a second independent SGLT2i systematic review synthesis alongside the previously tracked Tantush et al. Cureus meta-analysis (ss_136bc728).
key_findings: Systematically reviews preclinical and clinical evidence on SGLT2 inhibitor effects on functional (eGFR) vs structural (TKV) renal outcomes in ADPKD.
papers.clinical_implications: Synthesis-level evidence supporting continued prioritization of dedicated ADPKD SGLT2i RCTs (e.g., STOP-PKD, EMPA-PKD) rather than a basis for present-day prescribing changes.
papers.what_happened: A systematic review synthesized preclinical and clinical evidence comparing functional (eGFR) versus structural (TKV) renal outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Reinforces the case for prioritizing dedicated ADPKD-specific SGLT2i RCTs, complementing an independent SGLT2i meta-analysis tracked earlier this year.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A synthesis of existing mostly small, short-duration, and largely non-ADPKD-specific (class-effect) studies; does not constitute new primary clinical evidence.

papers.title: Authors' Reply: Nephron-Segment Composition and Apparent Fatty Acid Oxidation Suppression in Pkd1KO+Glis3KO Kidneys.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
papers.abstract_snippet: Authors' reply in a correspondence exchange regarding nephron-segment composition and fatty acid oxidation interpretation in a Pkd1KO+Glis3KO mouse kidney study.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: epub'd March 2026, only now issue-paginated; a correspondence reply, not a new study.
key_findings: Authors respond to a letter questioning interpretation of nephron-segment composition and fatty-acid-oxidation findings in a prior Pkd1KO+Glis3KO mouse paper.
papers.clinical_implications: None; methodological correspondence only.
papers.what_happened: Authors published a reply defending their interpretation of nephron-segment composition and fatty-acid-oxidation findings in a Pkd1KO+Glis3KO mouse kidney study, in response to a critical letter.
papers.why_it_matters: Methodological correspondence of interest mainly to specialists in renal mouse-model metabolic phenotyping.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Correspondence/reply item with no new primary data; epub'd 5 months ago and only now issue-paginated.

papers.title: Prognostication in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Current Tools, Clinical Gaps, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract_snippet: Review of ADPKD prognostic tools, contrasting imaging-based models (e.g., Mayo Imaging Classification, TKV) and genetic scoring systems (e.g., PROPKD), and their respective limitations.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-08-03); synthesizes several prognostic-tool threads already tracked in this system (e.g., Ravichandran kidney-failure model, TraceOrg, Yu TKV-eGFR framework).
key_findings: Reviews the two dominant categories of ADPKD prognostic tools -- imaging-based models and genetic scoring systems -- and notes each has inherent limitations, particularly reduced resolution in advanced disease.
Argues for future multimodal approaches combining imaging and genetic data.
papers.clinical_implications: Useful synthesis for clinicians navigating the growing landscape of ADPKD risk-prediction tools, but introduces no new validated tool itself.
papers.what_happened: A review synthesized current ADPKD prognostic tools, contrasting imaging-based models and genetic scoring systems and their clinical gaps.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a useful map of a rapidly growing prognostic-tool landscape for clinicians and researchers, tying together several previously tracked prediction-model papers.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A narrative synthesis, not a new validated tool or head-to-head comparison; introduces no new primary evidence.

papers.title: Deep learning-supported image quantification of epithelial cell shapes and its application to polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: A fully automated deep-learning image-quantification pipeline for epithelial cell shape/geometry is developed and applied to polycystic kidney disease tissue.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (epub 2026-08-03); a methods/tool paper.
key_findings: Develops a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline to quantify epithelial cell shape/geometry, standardizing what was previously a manual, low-throughput analysis.
Applies the pipeline to polycystic kidney disease tissue as a demonstration use case.
papers.clinical_implications: Research methodology tool; could improve standardization of future mechanistic cyst-epithelium studies but has no direct clinical application.
papers.what_happened: Researchers developed a deep-learning pipeline to automatically quantify epithelial cell shape and applied it to polycystic kidney disease tissue.
papers.why_it_matters: A standardized, automated quantification tool could improve rigor and throughput in future mechanistic cyst-epithelium research.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A methods/tool demonstration paper; does not itself report new disease-relevant biological findings beyond proof-of-concept application.

papers.title: Non-invasive 23Na MRI Identifies Functionally Distinct Cyst Phenotypes in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract_snippet: 7T 23Na MRI in 20 ADPKD patients classified 2,299 cysts into high-[Na+] (proximal-tubule-marker-positive) vs low-[Na+] (distal/collecting-duct-marker-positive) phenotypes; V2R was detected exclusively in low-[Na+] cysts.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (posted 2026-08-02); a novel non-invasive functional imaging approach in a modest human cohort.
key_findings: Non-invasive 7T 23Na MRI classified 2,299 cysts across 20 ADPKD patients into two functionally distinct phenotypes based on cyst sodium concentration, matching ex vivo tubular-origin markers.
The vasopressin V2 receptor (tolvaptan's target) was detected exclusively in low-[Na+], distal/collecting-duct-origin cysts, which comprised a highly variable 4.6-83.9% of cysts per patient.
Anatomical cyst location did not predict sodium phenotype, arguing for functional over structural imaging.
papers.clinical_implications: If validated, this could become a tool to identify which patients/cysts are more likely to be tolvaptan-responsive (V2R-expressing), but this is a small, exploratory, non-peer-reviewed imaging correlate study.
papers.what_happened: A preprint reported a novel 7T sodium-MRI technique that non-invasively classified ADPKD kidney cysts into two functionally distinct phenotypes in 20 patients, with V2R expression restricted to one phenotype.
papers.why_it_matters: Proposes a potential imaging biomarker to stratify patients or cysts by likely tolvaptan (V2R-target) responsiveness, which could inform future stratified-trial design.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, not peer reviewed; n=20 patients, purely correlative/exploratory imaging study with no outcome or treatment-response data yet, and the claim of 'guiding future therapeutic interventions' is not yet demonstrated.

papers.title: Targeting Ogt in ADPKD mitigates metabolic reprogramming and renal cystogenesis, extending survival
papers.abstract_snippet: Deleting O-GlcNAc transferase (Ogt) in rapidly and slowly progressive ADPKD mouse models reduced renal cystogenesis and extended survival from postnatal day 21 to over a year in the rapid model; pharmacological OGT inhibition reduced cyst formation in patient-derived cells in vitro.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: preprint posted 2025-12-16, first surfaced in this tracker's DB this scan via the Europe PMC sweep (SS API unavailable).
key_findings: Genetic deletion of Ogt markedly extended survival (from postnatal day 21 to over a year) and reduced cystogenesis in a rapidly progressive Pkd1 mouse model.
Pharmacological OGT inhibition reduced cyst formation in ADPKD patient-derived renal epithelial cells in vitro.
Ogt deletion preserved AMPK signaling and mitochondrial respiratory chain function, and normalized several dysregulated metabolic pathways.
papers.clinical_implications: Nominates OGT as a novel druggable metabolic target with an unusually large preclinical survival effect; strength of the survival signal in a genetic rapid-progression model warrants cautious interpretation before assuming translatability.
papers.what_happened: A preprint reported that genetic or pharmacological targeting of OGT reduced cystogenesis and substantially extended survival in ADPKD mouse models, with supporting in-vitro human patient-cell data.
papers.why_it_matters: Identifies a novel metabolic drug target (OGT/O-GlcNAcylation) with a notably strong preclinical survival signal, worth watching for further translational development.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, not yet peer reviewed; entirely preclinical (rapid-progression genetic mouse model plus in-vitro cells), and ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record.

papers.title: Extra-ciliary role for polycystins in regulation of Ezrin and renal tubular morphology
papers.abstract_snippet: Acute loss of PC1/PC2 increases renal epithelial cell circularity and reduces/mislocalizes the ERM protein Ezrin outside the primary cilium, in human ADPKD cystic tissue and inducible knockout models.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: preprint posted 2025-11-07, first surfaced in this tracker's DB this scan via the Europe PMC sweep.
key_findings: Acute loss of polycystins increases renal epithelial cell circularity and disrupts Ezrin localization/abundance, independent of primary cilium trafficking.
Findings are corroborated in human ADPKD cystic tissue as well as inducible Pkd1/Pkd2 knockout models.
papers.clinical_implications: Mechanistic insight into a previously underappreciated extra-ciliary polycystin function; no therapeutic candidate identified yet.
papers.what_happened: A preprint identified an extra-ciliary role for polycystins in regulating the ERM protein Ezrin and renal tubular cell morphology, validated in human ADPKD cystic tissue.
papers.why_it_matters: Broadens understanding of polycystin function beyond the primary cilium, a mechanistic area of active research interest.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, not yet peer reviewed; primarily mechanistic in-vitro/knockout-model work with human tissue used only for confirmatory immunostaining, not outcome data.

papers.title: Ciliary ARL13B drives renal cystogenesis via its GEF activity
papers.abstract_snippet: In a Pkd1-deficient adult mouse model, loss of ciliary ARL13B or mutation of its ARL3-GEF activity suppressed cyst formation, kidney enlargement, fibrosis, and injury markers, identifying ARL13B's GEF activity as a driver of the cilia-dependent cyst-activation (CDCA) pathway.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week: preprint posted 2025-11-21, first surfaced in this tracker's DB this scan via the Europe PMC sweep.
key_findings: Loss of ciliary ARL13B, or mutation of the single residue critical for its ARL3-GEF activity, suppressed Pkd1-dependent cyst formation, kidney enlargement, fibrosis, and injury in an adult mouse model.
Identifies ARL13B's GEF activity specifically in cilia as a mechanistic driver of the cilia-dependent cyst-activation (CDCA) pathway.
papers.clinical_implications: Nominates a specific enzymatic activity (ARL13B GEF function) as a potential druggable node in the CDCA pathway, though no compound or intervention is tested here.
papers.what_happened: A preprint used genetic mouse models to show that ciliary ARL13B's GEF activity drives Pkd1-dependent renal cystogenesis, and that disrupting this activity suppressed cyst formation and kidney injury.
papers.why_it_matters: Identifies a specific enzymatic mechanism within the cilia-dependent cyst-activation pathway, a candidate node for future targeted drug discovery.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint, not yet peer reviewed; adult-induced genetic mouse model only, with no pharmacological intervention tested and no human data.

papers.title: Papillary Hyperplasia in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Multi-Institutional Study With Immunohistochemical and Molecular Characterization.
papers.journal: The American Journal of Surgical Pathology
papers.abstract_snippet: Multi-institutional retrospective study of 85 ADPKD nephrectomies (48 patients) characterizing small intracystic epithelial proliferations, newly termed 'papillary hyperplasia' (PH) per ISUP consensus terminology, found in 88% of kidneys, with immunohistochemical (KRT7+, GATA3+, L1CAM+, CA9-) and whole-genome sequencing characterization showing no definitive molecular alterations distinguishing PH from benign cyst lining.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (published 2026-08-04); first formal histomorphologic/molecular characterization of this common but previously unnamed ADPKD cyst-lining lesion.
key_findings: In 85 nephrectomies from 48 ADPKD patients, small intracystic papillary/tufted epithelial proliferations ('papillary hyperplasia') were found in 88% of kidneys.
Lesions were uniformly low-grade/bland with no nuclear atypia, and immunohistochemically KRT7+, GATA3+, L1CAM+, variably AMACR+, CA9-negative.
Whole-genome sequencing on a subset showed no definitive molecular alterations distinguishing these lesions from adjacent benign cyst epithelium.
Authors propose formal terminology and diagnostic criteria to prevent misclassification as a neoplastic precursor lesion.
papers.clinical_implications: Primarily a diagnostic-pathology finding: helps renal pathologists recognize a common benign ADPKD cyst-lining proliferation and avoid over-classifying it as a tumor precursor; no direct disease-modifying or management implication for nephrologists or patients.
papers.what_happened: A multi-institutional retrospective review of 85 ADPKD nephrectomies formally characterized and named a common intracystic epithelial proliferation ('papillary hyperplasia'), finding it in 88% of kidneys with a consistent benign immunohistochemical and molecular profile.
papers.why_it_matters: Gives renal pathologists standardized terminology and criteria to recognize this common ADPKD lesion as benign, reducing risk of misclassifying it as a neoplastic precursor.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Purely descriptive/retrospective pathology series with no clinical outcome data, so it has no bearing on disease progression, treatment, or prognosis in ADPKD.

papers.title: Small Molecule Degradation of the microRNA-21 Precursor Rescues Pathogenic Pathways in Cellular Models of Fibrosis
papers.abstract_snippet: A heterobifunctional small molecule (TGP-21-RiboTAC) that degrades the microRNA-21 precursor was tested in polycystic kidney cell lines and a lung fibroblast cell line. It reduced pre-/mature miR-21, de-repressed downstream targets PDCD4 and PPARa, inhibited in vitro cyst growth, and rescued ADPKD-associated metabolic alterations; in lung fibroblasts it rescued TGF-b-induced SMAD7 repression and reduced invasion.
papers.novelty_assessment: Not new this week -- this preprint was first posted 2025-12-12 (~8 months ago) and is only now surfacing in our Europe PMC sweep; treated as a newly-tracked but stale item, not a new scientific event.
key_findings: TGP-21-RiboTAC, a small molecule that degrades the pre-miR-21 precursor, reduced miR-21 levels in polycystic kidney cell lines.
Treatment de-repressed PDCD4 and PPARa, both described as drivers of ADPKD cystogenesis/metabolic dysregulation.
The compound inhibited cyst growth and rescued metabolic alterations in vitro.
In a separate lung fibroblast line, the same compound reduced TGF-b-induced fibrotic signaling, suggesting a cross-organ antifibrotic mechanism.
papers.clinical_implications: Purely preclinical in vitro proof-of-concept for a novel RNA-degrader modality targeting miR-21 in ADPKD; no in vivo (animal) data yet, so no near-term clinical relevance.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Not stated in the preprint; RiboTAC heterobifunctional-degrader chemistry originates from a platform with prior biotech licensing (e.g., Expansion Therapeutics) in other indications, though no sponsor is disclosed here.

papers.what_happened: A preprint (first posted ~8 months ago, newly surfaced in this scan) showed a small molecule that degrades the pre-miR-21 precursor reduced miR-21 signaling, inhibited cyst growth, and rescued metabolic alterations in polycystic kidney cell lines in vitro.
papers.why_it_matters: Introduces a novel RNA-targeted small-molecule modality against miR-21, a previously implicated ADPKD driver, adding a mechanistically distinct approach alongside existing miR-17-targeted programs (e.g., RGLS4326/8429) in the pipeline.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Cell-line-only data with no animal model or in vivo validation, not yet peer-reviewed, and ADPKD preclinical findings have historically translated poorly to the clinic; this is early hypothesis-generating work, not a pipeline milestone.

papers.title: Applicability of Mayo’s Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) Prognostic Tool in the Southeast Asian ADPKD Population
papers.abstract_snippet: External validation of the Mayo Clinic ADPKD prognostic tool (HtTKV + age based) in 50 Malaysian ADPKD patients.
