Model-predicted eGFR correlated strongly with actual eGFR measured over 24 months (cc 0.748-0.815, p<0.001), and Bland-Altman analysis showed P30 agreement >90%, supporting applicability of the tool outside its original derivation cohorts.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (first posted 2026-08-06); first known external validation of the Mayo Clinic ADPKD prognostic tool in a Southeast Asian (Malaysian) cohort.
key_findings: In 50 Malaysian ADPKD patients, Mayo Clinic model-predicted eGFR correlated strongly with actual CKD-EPI eGFR measured over 24 months (cc 0.748-0.815, p<0.001).
Bland-Altman analysis showed high agreement, with P30 (prediction within 30% of measured eGFR) exceeding 90%.
Authors conclude the Mayo prognostic tool provides accurate disease-progression predictions in this Southeast Asian population.
papers.clinical_implications: If confirmed in peer review, extends the evidence base for using the Mayo Clinic ADPKD classification tool to counsel and risk-stratify Southeast Asian ADPKD patients, a population not represented in the tool's original derivation cohorts.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: None apparent; academic Malaysian centers, no disclosed sponsor.

papers.what_happened: A preprint (posted 2026-08-06) reports that Mayo Clinic ADPKD prognostic-tool-predicted eGFR values correlated strongly with actual eGFR measured over 24 months in 50 Malaysian ADPKD patients.
papers.why_it_matters: Extends external validation of the widely used Mayo Clinic ADPKD classification/prognostic tool to a Southeast Asian population not represented in its original derivation cohorts.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small single-cohort sample (n=50), not yet peer-reviewed, and the analysis validates a model-predicted surrogate (eGFR) rather than an independent patient-important outcome.

papers.title: A novel PKHD1 missense variant disrupting splicing in a fetus with Caroli disease.
papers.abstract_snippet: Exome sequencing in a fetus with Caroli disease and features of autosomal RECESSIVE polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) identified a novel PKHD1 missense variant causing exon 40 skipping; minigene assays and AlphaFold3 structural modeling characterized its pathogenicity.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new this week (published 2026-08-04), but the disease and gene (PKHD1, autosomal RECESSIVE PKD) are distinct from ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2); logged per ARPKD-adjacency rule rather than as ADPKD-relevant news.
key_findings: Exome sequencing of a fetus with prenatal Caroli disease and ARPKD features identified compound heterozygous PKHD1 variants, including a novel missense variant.
Minigene assays showed the novel variant causes exon 40 skipping and an in-frame deletion.
Structural modeling (AlphaFold3) predicts the deletion destabilizes a beta-barrel domain of the PKHD1 protein.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct ADPKD relevance -- PKHD1/ARPKD is a genetically and clinically distinct autosomal recessive disease from ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2); relevant only as background genetics context.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes a novel PKHD1 splicing variant, identified by exome sequencing, in a fetus with prenatal Caroli disease and features of autosomal RECESSIVE polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD).
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to the PKHD1 variant-pathogenicity catalog for ARPKD/Caroli disease, a distinct recessive condition; of only tangential background interest to ADPKD (dominant, PKD1/PKD2) trackers.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-family case report of a recessive disease unrelated to ADPKD's autosomal dominant genetics, so findings do not generalize to ADPKD patients or management.

papers.title: SGLT2 inhibitors in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: rationale, evidence gaps, and ongoing clinical trials.
papers.abstract_snippet: Narrative review summarizing the rationale for SGLT2 inhibitor use in ADPKD, the evidence gap created by ADPKD patients' exclusion from pivotal CKD RCTs (over concerns about eGFR decline and TKV growth), and ongoing trials aiming to resolve safety/efficacy uncertainty.
papers.novelty_assessment: New publication this week but is a narrative synthesis of already-known evidence gaps and ongoing trials, not new data.
key_findings: ADPKD patients have historically been excluded from pivotal SGLT2i CKD trials due to concerns about eGFR decline, cyst growth, and TKV increase.
Available observational studies show mixed (both beneficial and adverse) signals for SGLT2i in ADPKD.
Ongoing RCTs are cited as needed to resolve safety/efficacy uncertainty; none are newly reported here.
papers.clinical_implications: No new clinical guidance; reinforces that SGLT2i use in ADPKD remains off-label and evidence-gapped pending dedicated trials.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review synthesizes existing rationale, evidence gaps, and ongoing trials for SGLT2 inhibitor use in ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Useful orientation for clinicians/researchers on why ADPKD-specific SGLT2i evidence remains thin, but adds no new data itself.
papers.what_limits_confidence: As a narrative (non-systematic) review with no new primary data, it carries background/context value only; see the companion meta-analysis (PMID 42586506) this week for the actual pooled evidence.

papers.title: Polycystin-1 suppresses apoptotic signalling in endothelial cells and protects from atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract_snippet: Zebrafish and mouse endothelial-specific PKD1 loss-of-function studies, combined with human aortic endothelial cell knockdown, identify PKD1 (polycystin-1) as an anti-apoptotic, athero-protective factor via eNOS/THBS1/CCN1 signaling; EC-specific PKD1 loss increased atherosclerosis in mice.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new preclinical mechanistic finding this week, first disclosure of this data.
key_findings: Zebrafish endothelial mechanoreceptor screen identified PKD1/PKD2 as anti-apoptotic, protective factors in endothelium.
Inducible endothelial-cell-specific PKD1 (not PKD2) loss increased atherosclerosis in mice.
PKD1 knockdown in human aortic endothelial cells increased apoptosis and reduced eNOS expression via THBS1/CCN1.
papers.clinical_implications: Purely preclinical/mechanistic; may help explain elevated cardiovascular morbidity reported in ADPKD, but does not itself support any clinical or therapeutic action.
papers.what_happened: Zebrafish, mouse, and human endothelial cell experiments show polycystin-1 (PKD1) loss increases endothelial apoptosis and atherosclerosis.
papers.why_it_matters: Offers a plausible mechanistic link between PKD1 mutation and the cardiovascular manifestations seen in ADPKD (e.g., aneurysms, cardiovascular morbidity).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Entirely preclinical (zebrafish/mouse/cell-line); ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record, so this should not raise clinical confidence about cardiovascular risk management.

papers.title: Dysregulated Ferritin and Iron Homeostasis in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
papers.abstract_snippet: PKD mouse studies show ferritin is upregulated in cyst-lining epithelium/macrophages and ferritin trafficking is dysregulated in cystic kidneys, but conditional knockout of ferritin heavy chain (FTH) in collecting duct or myeloid cells did not affect cyst growth.
papers.novelty_assessment: New preclinical finding this week; first disclosure of this specific FTH conditional-knockout dataset.
key_findings: Ferritin is upregulated in cyst-lining epithelial cells and macrophages in PKD mouse and human kidneys.
Conditional FTH knockout in collecting duct or myeloid lineage did NOT change renal cyst growth (negative functional result).
Ferritin infusion caused abnormal renal ferritin/iron accumulation specifically in PKD (not wild-type) mouse kidneys, suggesting dysfunctional ferritin trafficking without altering cyst progression.
papers.clinical_implications: None directly; the key functional manipulation tested (FTH deletion) did not alter cystic progression, arguing against ferritin/iron handling as a primary druggable driver of cyst growth in this model.
papers.what_happened: A mouse-model study shows ferritin/iron handling is disrupted in cystic kidneys, but conditional knockout of ferritin heavy chain did not change cyst growth.
papers.why_it_matters: A well-designed negative functional result -- it helps prune ferritin/FTH itself as a likely direct cyst-growth driver, even as it documents broader iron-trafficking dysregulation.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse-model only, with ADPKD's historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record, and the primary functional test (FTH knockout) was negative for the outcome that matters (cyst growth).

papers.title: Kidney outcomes and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract_snippet: PRISMA/PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis of 6 clinical studies (451 ADPKD patients) on SGLT2 inhibitor therapy: eGFR decline was significantly attenuated in the first year versus each patient's own pre-SGLT2i slope (+0.65 mL/min/1.73m2/yr, 95% CI 0.05-1.26), but this significance was lost when compared against a genuine non-SGLT2i comparator group (+2.12, 95% CI -8.13 to 12.38), and no significant difference was found in total kidney volume change.
papers.novelty_assessment: Genuinely new synthesis this week (PROSPERO CRD420261295918), first meta-analysis pooling ADPKD-specific SGLT2i observational data.
key_findings: Pooled analysis of 6 studies (451 ADPKD patients) found eGFR decline slowed significantly versus patients' own pre-treatment slope (mean difference 0.65 mL/min/1.73m2/yr, 95% CI 0.05-1.26).
That significance disappeared in the more rigorous comparison against a non-SGLT2i-treated ADPKD comparator group (mean difference 2.12, 95% CI -8.13 to 12.38, not significant).
No significant difference in total kidney volume change was detected between SGLT2i and non-SGLT2i groups.
papers.clinical_implications: Does not establish SGLT2i efficacy for ADPKD-specific kidney protection; the only statistically significant result came from a baseline-only pre/post comparison, a weak design, while the properly controlled comparison and the TKV endpoint were both null. Underscores the need for a dedicated ADPKD RCT rather than supporting off-label extrapolation from general CKD data.
papers.what_happened: A PRISMA/PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis of 6 studies (451 ADPKD patients, likely predominantly observational since ADPKD patients are excluded from pivotal SGLT2i RCTs) found a significant slowing of eGFR decline only versus patients' own pre-treatment baseline, not versus a non-SGLT2i comparator group, and no significant total-kidney-volume difference.
papers.why_it_matters: Addresses a genuine evidence gap -- clinicians are increasingly using SGLT2i off-label in ADPKD despite exclusion from major CKD trials -- but the headline 'kidney outcomes and safety' undersells that the actual between-group comparison was null.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The only statistically significant finding used a baseline-only pre/post design (a recognized weak-evidence pattern with regression-to-the-mean and confounding risk), the underlying 6 studies are mostly observational/uncontrolled, the pooled sample is small (n=451), and first-year follow-up is short for a slow-progressing disease like ADPKD; this does not currently justify treating SGLT2i as an established ADPKD-specific kidney-protective therapy and instead argues for a dedicated RCT.

papers.title: Renal Volume Reduction on Magnetic Resonance Imaging During Tolvaptan Therapy in Patients with ADPKD: A Case Series.
papers.abstract_snippet: Case series of 4 ADPKD patients on tolvaptan who showed a decrease (rather than the typically expected slowed increase) in height-adjusted total kidney volume on serial MRI between 2020-2025; eGFR changes were minimal and heterogeneous (-9 to 0 mL/min/1.73m2).
papers.novelty_assessment: New this week; a genuinely uncommon observation (kidney volume decrease rather than merely slowed growth) worth flagging, but only as an anecdote.
key_findings: 4 ADPKD patients on tolvaptan showed a reduction (not just slowed growth) in htTKV on serial MRI.
The largest volume reduction occurred in the patient with the highest baseline htTKV.
eGFR changes were minimal and did not track with the volume reduction (range -9 to 0 mL/min/1.73m2), and none of the patients had other interventions during follow-up.
papers.clinical_implications: Illustrates heterogeneity in tolvaptan response and that volume change does not always parallel renal function change; too small and uncontrolled to change monitoring or counseling practice.
papers.what_happened: A 4-patient case series reports kidney volume reduction (not just slowed growth) on MRI during tolvaptan therapy, with minimal and inconsistent eGFR change.
papers.why_it_matters: A notable anecdote of an unusually strong volumetric response to tolvaptan, useful only as a hypothesis-generating observation about response heterogeneity.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Uncontrolled, single-arm, baseline-only case series of just 4 patients -- far too small and unstructured to support any generalizable claim about tolvaptan's volumetric effects.

papers.title: Enhancer Collapse Dictates PKHD1 Silencing and Centrosome-Mediated Chromosomal Instability and Metastasis in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract_snippet: Machine-learning/Mendelian-randomization screening plus single-cell, spatial transcriptomic and functional assays in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) identify PKHD1 (the ARPKD gene, not ADPKD's PKD1/PKD2) as a centrosome-localized guardian against chromosomal instability, silenced via enhancer collapse in ccRCC.
papers.novelty_assessment: New this week but concerns PKHD1 (ARPKD gene) in kidney cancer biology, not ADPKD or PKD1/PKD2.
key_findings: PKHD1 localizes to the centrosome and maintains the CEP97-CP110 complex.
PKHD1 loss triggers chromosomal instability and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition in ccRCC.
PKHD1 is epigenetically silenced in ccRCC via collapse of a distal enhancer.
papers.clinical_implications: No direct ADPKD relevance -- concerns PKHD1 (autosomal recessive PKD gene) in sporadic kidney cancer biology, genetically and clinically distinct from ADPKD's PKD1/PKD2.
papers.what_happened: A cancer-biology study finds PKHD1 (the ARPKD gene) acts as a centrosome-associated tumor suppressor silenced by enhancer collapse in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.why_it_matters: Tangential background interest only -- concerns a different gene/disease (PKHD1/ARPKD, kidney cancer) than ADPKD's PKD1/PKD2 cystogenesis pathway.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Logged per ARPKD-adjacency rule; findings do not generalize to ADPKD biology or management.

papers.title: Kidney-specific deletion of the BicC family RNA-binding protein 1 triggers an ADPKD-like cystogenic program.
papers.abstract_snippet: Conditional Bicc1 knockout mouse study: adult renal-tubule-wide deletion caused few cysts over 6 months, but distal-nephron-specific in-utero deletion caused aggressive PKD-like disease with activation of cAMP/YAP signaling pathways that overlap with ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2) pathobiology.
papers.novelty_assessment: New preclinical mechanistic finding this week, first disclosure of this cKO dataset and the ARTCyQ image-analysis pipeline.
key_findings: Adult inducible renal-tubule-wide Bicc1 deletion produced relatively few cysts within 6 months.
Distal-nephron-specific in-utero Bicc1 deletion produced aggressive PKD-like cystic disease.
Transcriptional profiling showed overlap between Bicc1-deficient cystic kidneys and known ADPKD/injury-repair signatures, including YAP signaling activation.
papers.clinical_implications: None directly; provides a new non-PKD1/PKD2 genetic model that mechanistically converges on ADPKD-relevant pathways (cAMP, YAP), useful for research but not for patient care.
papers.what_happened: A mouse study shows that distal-nephron-specific deletion of Bicc1 (a non-PKD1/PKD2 gene) causes aggressive polycystic-kidney-like disease with pathway overlap to ADPKD.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds a new genetic model for studying cAMP/YAP-driven cystogenesis mechanistically relevant to ADPKD, of research interest for target discovery.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preclinical mouse model with a gene distinct from PKD1/PKD2, and ADPKD has a historically weak preclinical-to-clinical translation record, so this should not raise clinical confidence about any pathway-targeted therapy.
